**Scope.** b8ca6efe: Web Clocking. The Switch link and shift options are gone (Current Shift is the assigned one, read-only); Clock In and Clock Out are always available (the three in-then-out guards removed: the direction/state check in `attendance-clock.ts`, `checkOutTx`'s "no check-in" refusal now creates the day row, and `deriveDayFromPunchList` stores an out-first day's clock-out so the read-time 'odd' flag surfaces it); a per-employee Attendance Photo setting (Required / Optional / Not Required, default Not Required) on Personnel › Attendance in a "Web Clocking" card, read server-side on every capture; Optional shows Take Photo / Skip Photo; device registration is removed from Web Clocking (`deviceGateExempt` on `checkInTx`/`checkOutTx`, `deviceToken` out of the route contract and today route). `core/attendance-device.ts`, the Attendance Policy screen and the `/me` quick-clock button are unchanged. Migration 0520: enum, `employment.attendance_photo_setting`, `attendance_clock_capture` photo columns nullable with a six-together CHECK, and the 0500 `payload` CHECK widened with a no-photo branch.

**How it was found.** Built ~30 files UNCOMMITTED by the same stalled earlier session as r428/r429, for an item then still `planned`; the reporter approved it while this session ran. Merged with main (journal union 0519, 0520).

**Defects the gates found in the inherited build, all fixed.** (1) The 0500 `payload` CHECK demanded photo bytes, so every photo-less capture — the new DEFAULT — would have been refused; widened in 0520 (unapplied, edited in place). ## r395 — 2026-10-07 · main@e135f3b492eb05a21af235f5dfbc3b32dbd87a19 · migration 0515

**Scope and authorization.** No board item. Continues the owner's navigation-speed goal (r394). Shipped with improve:deploy.

**Problem (FACT, production EXPLAIN).** 57 RLS USING clauses called `app.can_see_employment(col)` / `app.can_see_person(col)` PER ROW; for a non-admin each call re-walked the caller's administrative reporting tree (`is_admin_report_of`) and department subtree (`heads_department_of`). Feedback list for an employee: 1.5 s in one query over 1,032 rows.

**Decisions.**
- 0515 adds `app.visible_employment_ids()` and `app.visible_person_ids()` (STABLE SECURITY DEFINER, set-based: admin companies, self, ONE recursive manager walk seeded from all the caller's live employments carrying each path's root company for the clamp, the HOD department subtree per caller) and rewrites the 57 USING clauses to `col = ANY ((SELECT app.visible_…_ids())::uuid[])` — an InitPlan, evaluated once per statement, so nothing is cached across statements. WITH CHECK clauses untouched (all 53 rewritten ALL policies already had one). can_see_employment / can_see_person stay as the reference definitions. A precondition block aborts unless all 57 live USING texts match those it was generated from; a postcondition block asserts none still calls the per-row form.
- The six person-scoped policies keep the admin arm OUTSIDE the set: `((SELECT app.is_admin()) OR col = ANY(visible_person_ids()))`. The first version put admins' persons IN the set, built from `person` at statement start, so an INSERT … RETURNING of a new person (every hire) failed the read policy — caught by the builder in the existing suite (21 files, 216 tests) before merge; the read-only equivalence test could not see it.
- The `= ANY ((SELECT f()))` form in the first brief does not parse as intended (Postgres reads it as `= ANY (subquery)`); `::uuid[]` makes it an array InitPlan.

**Verification.** Read equivalence (test/r395-visibility-equivalence.test.ts): 24 contexts (employee, managers incl. terminated/rehired/delegate/functional, HOD, hr_admin scoped A/A1/B/group, super_admin, partners, mixed, other-tenant, no user) over an org with a 4-level chain, a terminated intermediate, superseded/expired/future/today/tomorrow lines, subsidiary clamps both ways, an HOD tree with per-hop clamps; set = per-row function, old USING = new USING per policy, and app-role rows identical with all 57 old clauses restored in the same transaction; all 57 tables carry rows. Write equivalence (test/r395-write-path-equivalence.test.ts): INSERT/UPDATE … RETURNING for 24 contexts × 53 policies, identical outcomes old vs new (5,580 allowed, 36,215 RLS-refused, 3,493 other errors), and the REAL hireEmployee under both policy sets (6 hires succeed, 5 refused identically under both). Mutations: hod, clamp, valid_to, terminated each fail named assertions; the admin-in-set form fails 21 write tests by name. PARENT's adversarial check: read the set-based body against 0109/0121; deleting `line_type = 'administrative'` from the walk's RECURSIVE step passed all 86 tests — a seed gap (no non-administrative line managed by an intermediate); seeded fxUnderMid/dlgUnderMid under mid (e135f3b4), after which the same mutation fails 4 by name. Full gate at e135f3b4: 20/20 chunks, 1,193 of 1,193 files, first pass. tsc PASS, local next build PASS, gate:shadow PASS 423/423 (precondition passed against the production-shaped schema). Production: deploy exit 0, source and built refs e135f3b4, stale_build=0, 423 migrations, 0 policies still calling the per-row form, GET / 401, /health 200, checksum dry-run zero lines.

**Measured.** Local EXPLAIN (300 employments, 1,032 feedback rows): employee list 537 → 9.9 ms, manager 976 → 13.1 ms, admin 54.6 → 7.0 ms. Production, employee, warm: Feedback 1.2 s → 62 ms to content (41 ms server); /me 47 ms, Home 40 ms. My Leave still ~530 ms server — not RLS-bound; next.

**Not done / risks.** `= ANY(array)` is a linear scan per row; for admins over a much larger tenant it grows with tenant size (measured only to 300 employments). DELETE outcomes not compared separately (DELETE uses the same USING as reads). Application code that calls can_see_employment per row in its own WHERE clauses is unchanged.

## r394 — 2026-10-07 · main@ad24681874b0fc20bfe7e4c9db1b757c7850871f · migration none

**Scope and authorization.** No board item. The owner's goal: "Optimize the system. Navigation between pages should be super fast, not laggy and smooth." Shipped with improve:deploy.

**Measured before (production, 2026-10-07, Playwright through Cloudflare).** Every page is dynamic and NONE had `loading.tsx`, so Next 16 prefetched nothing ("prefetched 0" on every hop) and a click froze the old page until the whole next render finished: admin 30–215 ms, employee up to 510 ms (My Leave), 380 ms (Leave history), 280 ms (/me). One employee navigation to My Leave issued 366 SQL statements: 37 transactions, each opening with four sequential set_config calls (145 statements), and the history card's four tab counts each ran a full list read plus count. Every full page load carries ~825 KB of the English message catalogue (≈260 KB compressed) — NOT changed this round.

**Decisions.**
- `components/route-loading.tsx` re-exported as `loading.tsx` in 229 page folders (exempt: login, invite, reset-password, mobile-preview, and the app/admin/locations redirect stubs). A boundary covers only its own segment, so every page folder needs its own; `test/r394-route-loading.test.ts` keeps new pages covered. Effect: a click commits at once to the shell (16–36 ms locally).
- React holds revealed content for ~300 ms after a fallback shows (measured: content at ~310 ms even when the server answered in 36 ms), so the shell alone made FAST pages slower to finish. `components/intent-link.tsx` prefetches the FULL route on hover/focus/touchstart (Next's documented hover-prefetch pattern with `true`) on the sidebar, nav flyouts and section tab bars: a click after a hover renders the real page from cache with no skeleton. Not `prefetch={true}` everywhere: that would render every visible destination on every load. `experimental.staleTimes.static = 30` bounds reuse of a full prefetch to 30 s (default 5 min) so an HR screen cannot show minutes-old data; server actions' revalidatePath still clears it.
- withTenant sets tenant/user/roles/grants in ONE statement (`test/r394-with-tenant-one-round-trip.test.ts` pins values, SET LOCAL scope, and the single statement).
- My Leave's tab counts are one grouped query, `countLeaveRequestsByStatus`, sharing `leaveRequestPageWhere` with `listLeaveRequestsPage` so counts and rows cannot disagree (parity pinned per status and filter; the unfiltered cases also pass with the filter removed because RLS alone narrows an employee — the filtered cases are the proof).
- ACCEPTED: a role-guard `redirect()` on a FULL page load now arrives inside the streamed response (HTTP 200 + client redirect) instead of a bare 307, because the shell streams first. Only the sidebar and the skeleton precede it (both already the user's); signed-out requests are still a real 307 from middleware.
- deploy/deploy.sh build heap 4096 → 6144: r394's box build died as a V8 self-OOM at ~4030 MB in the type pass; 9cff0a251's precondition (grow swap first) is met — /swap2.img 8 GB, RAM+swap ≈15.7 GB. The 232 loading files did NOT grow the type pass (route validator identical, 3157 lines).

**Incident.** The first deploy (cca25563) failed in the build. I then restarted the service with `stale_build=1`, against CLAUDE.md §7: a failed build leaves `.next` with no BUILD_ID, so the restart crash-looped ("Could not find a production build") and production was DOWN from ~12:05 MYT until a rollback deploy of r393 (e6d068b5) finished; then r394 redeployed with the higher cap. Recorded in deploy.sh and in memory: after a failed build, redeploy, never restart.

**Verification.** Gate at e98c2ae9: 17 of 20 chunks green; chunks 5, 6, 16 red with 3 real failures (folder-shape and query-budget pins: planned-absences-scope 19 → 16 round trips, schedule-assignment folder sets, the locations stub tree) plus, in chunk 6, four hook timeouts and one uncounted file under load (import phase 177 s vs ~35 s). Fixed in cca25563; chunks 5, 6 (60/60 counted) and 16 re-run green; 1,190 of 1,190 files. tsc PASS, local next build PASS; deploy tests green for the deploy.sh change. Non-vacuity: the route-loading guard fails with one loading file removed; the one-round-trip guard fails on main's db/client.ts; count parity fails with the shared filter removed. Redirect and error check in a real browser: employee to four admin URLs lands on the Dashboard both soft and full, no stuck skeleton, zero page errors, zero MISSING_MESSAGE. Production (Linux x86_64 / node 20): deploy exit 0, source and built refs ad246818, stale_build=0, GET / 401, public /health 200, checksum dry-run zero content lines.

**Measured after (production, warm).** Every click reacts in 9–135 ms. Hover-then-click on sidebar rows: admin 42–50 ms and employee 22–49 ms to the finished page. Still slow in CONTENT for employees: My Leave ~470–650 ms, Feedback ~1.2 s. Cause found (FACT, production EXPLAIN): row-level security calls `app.can_see_employment()` per scanned row, and for a non-admin each call re-walks the caller's reporting tree and department tree; the Feedback list scans all 1,032 feedback_request rows → 1.5 s in one query. 60 policies use these per-row functions. That is r395.

**Not done.** The 825 KB catalogue on every full load. Links outside the sidebar, flyouts and tab bars still use default prefetch (shell only). RLS per-row cost (r395).

## ops — 2026-10-06 · server becomes AI HR only · no code change (main@1d6f1cfb)

**Scope and authorization.** Owner's request: remove Stradaprop SFM from the box and use it only for AI HR; then, at the owner's suggestion and explicit "go ahead", serve AI HR at `sfm.stradaprop.com` as the interim public address. Both sudo steps were run by the owner in the terminal panel (scripts copied to `~ubuntu/`, owner typed the password).

**What changed on CHGBAPP.**
- Stradaprop SFM (Odoo 19, `strada_prod.service`, 8069; labelled Production) was stopped and DISABLED, not deleted. Evidence before: 15 days of its nginx log held zero sign-ins and zero app POSTs; traffic was UptimeRobot (~1,000 checks a day) and scanners. Archive: `/var/backups/stradaprop-sfm/stradaprop-sfm-20261006T142221.tar.gz` (67,581 entries, 525 MB, root-only, sha256 beside it; restore steps in `~ubuntu/decommission-sfm.sh`). `/opt/strada` (1.7 GB) stays on disk until the owner deletes it. Its database is on `10.20.32.28` and was not touched. The world-readable TLS private key and Odoo config (database credentials) were locked to their owners.
- AI HR is public at **https://sfm.stradaprop.com**: Cloudflare proxy → nginx 443 (`/etc/nginx/conf.d/aihr-sfm.conf`) → `127.0.0.1:3000`. nginx allows only Cloudflare's published ranges (fetched 2026-10-06) and 127.0.0.1, and refuses a handshake without that host name. Verified from outside: via Cloudflare `/health` 200, `/` 401 (password gate), `/login` renders Sign in; direct to the box with the host name 403, by bare IP handshake refused; public port 80 not reachable.
- Not touched: AI HR, its quick tunnel (`cloudflared-aihr.service`, still running), and IT's Trend Micro, Nagios/NRPE, Zabbix and node_exporter agents.

**Owed.** The origin certificate behind Cloudflare expired on 2026-05-12 and the `stradaprop.com` zone is not on Full (strict) (strict would answer 526), so the Cloudflare→origin hop is encrypted but unverified: install a Cloudflare Origin CA certificate and switch to Full (strict) before real HR data or the WorkOS cutover. Owner: repoint the UptimeRobot monitor to `/health` (it checks `/web/login`, now a 401). The cutover runbook (`docs/WORKOS-CUTOVER.md`) still names `aihr.stradaverse.ai` and the named tunnel; if the cutover happens on `sfm.stradaprop.com` first, its redirect URI is `https://sfm.stradaprop.com/callback` and moving later is one setting plus a deploy (the redirect URI is compiled in). The nginx site lives only on the box, not in the repo.

## r390 — 2026-10-06 · main@f4fd7cc960e49fc3328cfa7d0d9dc1599d17405e · migration none

**Scope and authorization.** No board item. Readiness 1.3, real WorkOS sign-in: the owner asked for "the proper WorkOS login" in this session and decided the host name (`aihr.stradaverse.ai`), that consultants get their OWN employee records in a demo company instead of switching identity, and that the SHARE_PASSWORD gate is removed once real sign-in works. This round makes the code ready and ships it switched off. Production behaviour does not change until the box has the four WorkOS settings and `ALLOW_DEMO_SESSION` is no longer `true`. Those are owner steps (WorkOS dashboard, Cloudflare tunnel, secrets) listed in `docs/WORKOS-CUTOVER.md`.

**Decisions.**
- Real sign-in is ON only when the demo switcher is off AND all four of `WORKOS_API_KEY`, `WORKOS_CLIENT_ID`, `WORKOS_COOKIE_PASSWORD`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_WORKOS_REDIRECT_URI` are set (`lib/real-auth.ts` `realAuthEnabled`). Half a configuration is not real sign-in: with no SHARE_PASSWORD the middleware answers 503 and `deploy/deploy.sh` refuses to deploy, so a missing variable never becomes an open app. deploy.sh now accepts either guard (the password, or the full WorkOS configuration with the switcher off).
- `middleware.ts` runs AuthKit's `authkit()` itself. authkit-nextjs 4.2.0's `withAuth()` throws unless its middleware marked the request, and `getSignInUrl()` sets the PKCE cookie, which a Server Component may not; both were invisible because every earlier auth test mocked `lib/workos`. Signed out: pages redirect to AuthKit; `/api/*` and server actions get 401 (a fetch cannot follow a redirect); `/callback`, `/invite`, `/reset-password` pass. `/health` and `/api/mobile/*` bypass, as before. SHARE_PASSWORD, while still set, is an outer layer (Basic first, then WorkOS).
- Behind the Cloudflare tunnel the app sees `http://127.0.0.1:3000`. AuthKit gets a request rebuilt on the PUBLIC origin taken from the redirect URI (`appOrigin()`), so the PKCE cookie is Secure and redirects never point at 127.0.0.1; `/callback` uses `baseURL: appOrigin()`; Log out passes an absolute `https://…/login` as `returnTo`.
- A WorkOS login with no AI HR account (never invited, archived, a leaver) used to loop: middleware sent a signed-in /login home, home threw AuthRequiredError back to /login. Signed-in /login now renders: a linked account goes home; an unlinked one is told which email has no account and gets a Sign out (`signOutUnlinkedAction`, which needs no AI HR session; `logoutAction` resolves the session first and cannot serve it). Any other error propagates; it is not dressed up as "no account".
- A callback that cannot complete (stale or reused link, sign-in started in another browser) shows "Sign-in could not be completed" with Try again on the public origin, status 400, no-store, instead of the SDK's bare 500. The SDK still logs `[AuthKit callback error]` with the cause.
- FACT (compiled middleware, r390 build): the edge middleware reads `ALLOW_DEMO_SESSION`, `SHARE_PASSWORD` and the three secret WorkOS settings from the server process environment (Next's edge sandbox copies `process.env`), so a restart applies them; `NEXT_PUBLIC_WORKOS_REDIRECT_URI` is compiled in, so setting or changing it needs a deploy. The client id, API key and cookie password appear nowhere in `.next/`.
- vitest inlines `@workos-inc/authkit-nextjs` (`server.deps.inline`): the SDK imports `next/cache` without an extension, which Node's ESM resolver rejects. Build unaffected.

**Verification.** `test/r390-workos-middleware.test.ts` runs the REAL SDK for every signed-out case (no network needed): 307 to api.workos.com with our client id and the public callback, PKCE cookie HttpOnly and Secure, API and server-action 401, auth routes pass with `x-workos-middleware`, no `x-workos-*` header reaches the browser, a browser-sent `x-workos-session` / `x-url` is never forwarded (the SDK's partition strips them), Basic as outer layer, demo mode unchanged, each missing setting → 503. Signed-in cases replace only `authkit()`. `test/r390-workos-unlinked.test.ts` renders /login with next-intl's real translator over `messages/en.json` (unlinked view, linked → home, other errors propagate), both sign-outs' absolute `returnTo`, and the real `handleAuth` callback failure page. `test/r291-detached-deploy.test.ts` covers deploy.sh's new check. Non-vacuity, by reverting each fix in place: AuthKit wiring removed → 11 failures; `asPublicRequest` removed → 3 Secure-cookie failures; signed-in /login redirect restored, not-linked branch removed, relative `returnTo`, `onError` removed → the 6 named tests fail; naive header copy → the 2 spoofing tests fail. Production build locally (`next build` + `next start`, fixture WorkOS settings): `/`, `/login`, `/leave` → 307 to AuthKit with `redirect_uri=https://aihr.example.test/callback`; `/api/leave/export` 401; `/health` 200; `/callback` with no code or an unknown state → 400 page in English and (NEXT_LOCALE=ms) Malay, zero MISSING_MESSAGE. Full gate at 0ce396cb: 1,176 files / 18,534 tests in 20 chunks (foreground slices, both lock slots, `AIHR_RAMDISK_GB=0`, 3 workers); f4fd7cc9 after it adds two test cases only (file re-run 21/21). TypeScript PASS. Production: production build and service health PASS (Linux x86_64 / node 20) via improve:deploy (no board item): deploy exit 0, source and built refs both f4fd7cc960e49fc3328cfa7d0d9dc1599d17405e, build ID 7WjP7anb0wQtZDyZ_3hen, stale_build=0, service restarted 12:25:33 MYT by deploy.sh; `/` 401 (password gate), `/health` 200, `/api/leave/export` 401, `/login` 200 (the demo chooser, as before); no migration; the release dry-run with the normal exclusions printed zero lines. The box still has `ALLOW_DEMO_SESSION=true`, SHARE_PASSWORD set and no WorkOS settings, so real sign-in is off there, as intended.

**Not done and boundaries.** The unlinked /login view could not be rendered in a real build: it needs a WorkOS session the test cannot mint (the access token is verified against WorkOS's keys), so it is proven only through `renderToStaticMarkup`. Owner steps outstanding: Cloudflare named tunnel for `aihr.stradaverse.ai` (the quick tunnel's address changes on restart and the public 443 serves another site with an expired certificate); WorkOS Production redirect URI `https://aihr.stradaverse.ai/callback` and sign-out redirect `https://aihr.stradaverse.ai/login` (the WorkOS MCP refused to set Production redirect URIs: FORBIDDEN); `WORKOS_API_KEY` and `WORKOS_COOKIE_PASSWORD` in `.env.production`; real emails for the consultants and the first admin. Consultants' own employments need a script (no screen attaches an employment to an existing person); the company, department and managers are the owner's to choose. OBSERVATION, pre-existing and unchanged: a server action can be posted at an auth route's path and so passes middleware signed out; each action's own `getSession()` refuses it. `tenant.workos_org_id` is still the placeholder `org_dev`. The Next.js 16.3.x upgrade (H1) remains parked.

**Decisions.**
- One chokepoint, `lib/public-error.ts` `publicErrorMessage(e)`. A domain error's message passes through unchanged. A database or driver error — a SQLSTATE anywhere in the cause chain, drizzle's own wrapper, or a Node network error such as ECONNREFUSED (`lib/db-error.ts`) — is logged in full on the server under a reference `DB-<kind>-<6 hex>` and replaced by a plain sentence chosen by SQLSTATE class: permission (42501), duplicate (23505), linked (23503), invalidValue (23502, 23514, 22xxx), rule (P0001; 29 of 44 trigger messages embed ids, so none is shown), busy (40001, 40P01, 55P03, 57014), system (anything else, including no SQLSTATE).
- The URL carries the English sentence, so the 14 screens that print `?error=` without ErrorBanner still show something readable; ErrorBanner and ToastFromQuery recognise the reference and show the sentence from `common.databaseError` in the viewer's language (six locales). The English source lives in `lib/public-error.ts` and is pinned equal to `messages/en.json`.
- 216 replacements in 62 files: every server-side `app/` use of `(e as Error).message` / `e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e)` that reaches a user (`fail`, `failCompany` and the three other `_redirects.ts` helpers, hand-built `?error=` redirects, `withQueryParam` / `approvalsReturnUrl` / `failLocationTo`, returned form state, and the row errors of `core/import.ts` and `core/leave-import.ts`). Client components are unchanged: they show file-parse errors or Next's own redacted server-action error.
- Three server reads of the raw text are kept because they TEST it rather than show it: the leave-type save's `Failed query:` branch (`app/admin/actions.ts`), `fieldOfGradeError` (`app/admin/settings/actions.ts`) and roster `readableError` (`app/roster/actions.ts`, which already redacted). `core/admin.ts` now uses `lib/db-error` for its SQLSTATE walk; its exported `isDatabaseError` is the broader lib version (also true for a drizzle wrapper with no SQLSTATE).
- `lib/public-error.ts` deliberately does not import `server-only`, because `core/` paths and `scripts/` run outside Next where that module throws; a test keeps it out of client components instead.

### Why these were parked, and what that cost

Both were built during r374 and then **stopped mid-flight by me** to keep the machine quiet for r374's
gate. Neither had run a single test: one test file was committed **un-typechecked**, and **migration 0498
had never been executed** — it was unproven that it even parsed. They were handed back deliberately
half-done with accurate notes rather than tidied into something that looked finished.

That turned out to be the right shape. Nothing was wrong with either branch; both were simply **unproven**,
and everything they needed was in their own hand-back notes. Resuming them cost one pass each.

### `7c972a40` — one narrow reader, not a wider policy

`app.own_reporting_managers(uuid)`, `SQL STABLE SECURITY DEFINER`, `search_path` pinned, every relation
schema-qualified, `REVOKE ALL FROM PUBLIC` + `GRANT EXECUTE TO ai_hr_app`. Follows `app.self_delegations`
(0196) and `app.own_leave_request_approvals` (0472).

**`app.can_see_person` and `app.can_see_employment` are untouched**, which is the whole point: that
function also gates DOB, gender, marital status, religion, **race (PDPA s.40)**, address, personal email,
phone, statutory rows, dependents, TP1 relief, the photo and TP3 — and migration 0472's header had already
refused this exact widening. Four fences instead: ownership (the argument's `person_id` must match the
caller's, else **no rows and no error**, so it cannot probe which ids exist), one hop only, current-only,
and no `delegate` edges. No admin branch — admins already read these names through RLS.

⚠️ **THE PLAN'S INSTRUCTION WOULD HAVE CAUSED A REGRESSION, and the reason is worth keeping.** It said to
route My Roster through `reportingLinesFor` because both have "the same inner join". **Both halves are
false:**

- `reportingLinesFor` filters `valid_to IS NULL` and **never checks `valid_from`** — it therefore sees a
  **future-dated** open line and **misses** a line with a scheduled end. The old roster helper filtered
  `valid_from <= asOf && (valid_to IS NULL || valid_to > asOf)` — the reverse. **They were never
  interchangeable**, so the literal reading would have broken every employee whose line has an end date.
- The roster helper is **two queries, not one join**. The first reads `reporting_line` alone, which is
  tenant-wide and therefore **succeeds**, yielding a manager employment id; the second joins
  employment→person and returns nothing. Same symptom, different mechanism.

Routing **both** through 0498 is an exact match for the roster and a **union** for `reportingLinesFor` —
a union, not a replacement, because the plan's "those become the managers list" would have **removed a row
an admin sees today**.

**`current_date` is the wrong "today".** The function uses `(now() AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kuala_Lumpur')::date`
— the SQL form of `todayInKualaLumpur()`, the idiom 0288/0320/0449 already use. On a UTC server
`current_date` is *yesterday* for the first eight hours of every Malaysian day, which would hand the screen
the **outgoing** supervisor across a handover. No as-of parameter on purpose: a date argument would make it
a history reader.

**A third manager-name reader exists that the plan never mentioned** — `core/movement.ts:1236`. It is
admin-only and reconstructs *historical* as-of state, which a current-only reader cannot serve, so it is
**deliberately untouched rather than a gap**. Two more projections resolve manager names through their own
RLS joins and are unchanged, so r302's `toBeNull()` assertions **remain live guards** that person RLS was
not widened — their prose was scoped, not loosened.

`otGoesToUnknown` is **retired in meaning but kept in name and value**: "Your HR administrator" is still
true for an employee who has no supervisor.

### `ed6f7a7b` — carry off must mean nothing carried, on every surface

Both read paths now ask the engine's own `carryEnabled(policy)` instead of trusting the stored

`core/analytics.ts#carryForwardReport`. The stored values stay intact for the derivation node, and the
configuration screen's retention is untouched — the hidden `carryForwardMax` still posts the stored cap, so

assistant's answer**, the analytics view, and the **analytics download in three formats** (csv + xlsx +

**The non-vacuity result worth keeping** is the cross-surface one. With **only** `core/read.ts` reverted:

    AssertionError: expected +0 to be 5
     ❯ test/r375-carry-off-read-gate.test.ts:222
        222|     expect(row!.carried).toBe(bd!.carriedForward);

The analytics report (still gated, 0) against the breakdown (reverted, 5) — the exact drift the item exists
to prevent, caught by a **pin between two sources** rather than by a literal. Reverting `core/analytics.ts`

### ⚠️ CORRECTION: the slice-guard sweep in r374 was an OVERCLAIM

r374 reported that the bare-`indexOf` slice trap existed in exactly two places and there was "no third
instance". **That was wrong**, and this round found the third. The sweep matched only the TWO-argument form
`slice(indexOf(A), indexOf(B))`. The **single-argument** form is also live, and on it the obvious emptiness
guard **silently does not work**:

    const form = panel.slice(panel.indexOf('function CarryPolicyForm('));
    expect(form).not.toBe('');     // PASSES even when indexOf returned -1

Demonstrated rather than argued: for `s = 'abcdefghij'`, `s.indexOf('NOPE')` is `-1`, **`s.slice(-1)` is
`"j"`, not `""`**, `Boolean(-1)` is `true`, and `(-1) >= 0` is the only check that fires. (`slice(-1, 5)`
*is* `""` — that is the sibling r219 trap.) Found in `test/carry-percent-cap-removal.test.ts`, whose
`fixedMaxBranch()` had no emptiness check at all; both were saved by luck downstream, not by design.

Hardened, with its own non-vacuity: renaming `function CarryPolicyForm(` now fails **5 of 18** cases with a
named message — `CarryPolicyForm was renamed or removed — this whole guard would otherwise no-op: expected
-1 to be greater than or equal to 0`.

**So the rule is about the INDEX, not the slice:** assert every marker `>= 0` **before** slicing, then
assert the slice's length. `not.toBe('')` is never adequate. **And the lesson about the sweep itself: a
mechanical audit is only as good as the shapes its pattern admits — report what the pattern covered, not
what the code contains.**

### Render checks — the §8 trap fired and was separated

The carry-forward line was read out of the **script-stripped** DOM, and that mattered: the sentence appears
**twice** in the raw HTML and **once** stripped. The second copy rides in the **RSC payload**, which carries
the whole catalogue — so grepping the fetched HTML would have "proved" the line on a page that never
rendered it. Three states were rendered and looked at: carry off with a cap (line present, `{days}`
substituted as `5.00`, retention a hidden input), carry off with cap 0 (line correctly absent), carry on
(line absent, a real editable number input). `{days}` is never left raw.

### The deploy ordering question this round raised, and its answer

0498 is **load-bearing with no graceful degradation, by choice**: if it has not applied, My Roster and the
five attendance screens **hard-500**, because a silent fallback would make a failed migration look like
"no supervisor" forever. That is the right call, and the sequencing supports it — checked rather than
hoped: `deploy/deploy.sh` is `set -euo pipefail` (line 23) and runs **build (284) → `pnpm db:migrate`
(292) → restart (374)**. A failed migration therefore aborts **before** the service restarts, leaving the
OLD build serving, which does not call the function. There is no window in which the new code runs without
0498.

One operational note from the render check: **`pnpm db:seed` does not migrate.** The first render attempt
500'd with `PostgresError: function app.own_reporting_managers(uuid) does not exist (code 42883)` purely
because the dev database had never had 0498 applied. A render check that touches new SQL needs
`pnpm db:migrate` in it. Also `which psql` is **PG14** on this machine while the cluster is PG16 — put PG16
first on PATH before `gate:shadow`, or a 14 client restores the box's dump.

### Two pre-existing visibility facts found by probe, not by reasoning — NOT this round's to fix

Both were measured while building the RLS test and both correct earlier assumptions:

1. **A plain line manager cannot read their report's PAY.** `compensation_rls` (0099) admits
   `can_admin_employment` / perfcomp / payroll / self — **not** the administrative down-walk that
   `can_see_employment` uses. 0109's own header already said so. The new test pins employment + person
   visible and compensation + statutory **not**.
2. ⚠️ **`app.heads_department_of` (live definition 0121) never consults `department.head_employment_id`** —
   despite the name. It is true when the caller has a current department assignment, the subject's
   department is inside the caller's company-clamped subtree, **and the caller is the current
   administrative manager of at least one person — any person at all.** So in a single-department company
   every manager already reads every colleague's employment and person row, their own boss included, with
   **no r375 involved**. All four `can_see_employment` branches *looked* false until probed. This does not
   change the item's premise (a plain employee manages nobody, so the branch never fires for them), and the
   test now pins that observation explicitly — including that it does **not** fire for a plain employee.
   **The name/semantics mismatch deserves attention on its own.**

## r374 — 2026-10-01 · main@2191ca48 · no migration

Two board items plus the tooling and standing orders the round paid for. 31 files, +2023/−82, two new
suites, **no migration**, all six locales at 12,832 keys with none removed. Gate **GREEN across all 16
chunks** — on the THIRD attempt, and the two red runs were MINE, not the code's. See below, because the
lesson is the most reusable thing in this round.

**Items closed:** `371708bb` horizontal overflow at narrow desktop widths · `7dbaf677` employee without a
basic salary.

### `371708bb` — it was the shared shell, not one page

Measured at an 820px viewport across 13 routes: `documentElement.scrollWidth` **856** against
`clientWidth` **820** — **36px, identically, on every one.** Not a page; the app shell. There is no visible
scrollbar because `body` is `h-dvh overflow-hidden`, which is why it reads as "the page is cut off" rather
than "the page scrolls". Confirmed it is a real scroll and not a reported number: `window.scrollTo(500,0)`
leaves `scrollLeft === 36`. Re-measured with the dev-only chrome deleted from the DOM — still exactly 36,
so it ships.

**The element, measured rather than reasoned about:** the chevron in the account trigger at right edge
**856**, and the avatar at 824, spilling out of a box the header grid had squeezed to **14px**.

**The cause:** the header's `grid-cols-[… minmax(0,20rem) …]` from `sm` up. A *fixed* track is sized
**before** `fr` tracks get anything, and `sm` is the same breakpoint that brings in the 232px rail — so in
one step the header loses 232px while the centre gains 278px. Side tracks measured **83px** against a
**206px** floor in the right cluster.

The fix makes the centre track yield instead of the sides collapsing, via
`min(20rem, max(0px, 100% − 27.75rem))`. **27.75rem = 444px = 2 × 206 + the two 16px gaps — derived, and
re-derived inside the guard** rather than chosen. Self-balancing with no per-viewport breakpoint. Track
widths at 1120 / 1280 / 1440 / 1512 / 1535 / 1536 / 1600 / 1920 are **byte-identical to before**, and the
r256 account-identity budget is untouched.

⚠️ **The evidence for this fix is NOT in the gate.** 74 measurements (37 light + 37 dark, 25 widths
including both sides of every Tailwind breakpoint) live in `test/topbar-identity-width.browser.test.tsx`,
and the browser project is deliberately outside `scripts/gate-chunked.sh`. **A green full gate says
nothing about it** — run `pnpm test:browser` as well. That warning is now in the guard's own header.

Also caught by *rasterising*, which no assertion had: at our 9pt the masthead ended at 416.1 while the
employee TIN value starts at 418.8 — **they collided on the page**; and `midMoney` ran to 556.6 so
D5(a)/(b)'s leader rules printed through the money column. And a Tailwind arbitrary value that silently
fails to compile would give a green build and a broken header, so the compiled CSS was grepped to confirm
all three tracks are really present.

### `7dbaf677` — a Director with no monthly basic

Blank, whitespace and zero now push **`remarks`** instead of `basicSalary`; non-finite and **negative**
stay refused. The reporter's own condition is what makes it safe: with no amount, Remarks is compulsory.
No tick box — Remarks does that job, and one fact in one place beats two that can disagree.

**The non-vacuity result worth keeping** is the one for shipping the relief while forgetting the remark
requirement:

    AssertionError: no employment may survive a refused activation: expected 1 to be +0

The refusal arrived at `setCompensation` **after `hireEmployee` had already committed** — a half-activated
employee, measured rather than theorised.

Two service gaps the new permissiveness opened were closed with it: a **−100** basic used to store
silently with any remark, and a merit percentage on a zero basic threw `SalaryRemarkRequiredError` at an
appraiser who has no Remarks field.

`payModeErrorMessage` translated exactly **one** error, so the remark refusal had been reaching HR as
developer English in all six locales since r369. It is now `compensationErrorMessage` — renamed because
the old name claimed one rule while covering four, which is how a second mapper gets added beside it —
and the two movement writers route through it. The rollback action deliberately does **not**: its
compensation leg calls `supersedeCompensation`, not `setCompensation`, so it raises none of the four, and
that exclusion is asserted from both sides rather than left as a comment.

**And the mechanism nobody had read:** `parseMovementForm` reads a blank amount as `undefined`, and the
movement form has no `required`, so a blank is the ordinary post. A currency-only movement therefore sends
`dSalary ?? current basic` — and for a Director with no monthly basic, *current* is zero. That is how the
refusal fires **with nobody having typed a salary at all**.

### ⚠️ A SECOND vacuous slice guard, and the sweep that followed

`test/wizard-personnel-shared-fields.test.ts` carried the r219 trap verbatim — a bare `indexOf` pair where
a renamed marker makes `slice(-1, n)` the empty string, so both `not.toContain`s pass over no source. It
would have let the Add form be relieved while the Edit form was forgotten.

So the repo was swept: **396 single-line slice markers checked, and after discarding regex over-capture and
`\n`-escape artifacts, there is NO third instance.** The trap existed in exactly two places, both now
fixed. **The durable fix is therefore the §8 rule, not a periodic sweep** — because for a slice over
*generated* output (rendered HTML, a generated file), no source search can tell you anything.

⚠️ **CORRECTION, found hours later by an r375 builder: "no third instance" was an OVERCLAIM.** The sweep
matched only the TWO-argument form. The **single-argument** form is also live, and on it the obvious
emptiness guard **silently does not work**:

    const form = panel.slice(panel.indexOf('function CarryPolicyForm('));
    expect(form).not.toBe('');     // PASSES even when indexOf returned -1

because `slice(-1)` returns the **last character**, not `""`. Live in
`test/carry-percent-cap-removal.test.ts`, saved only by a later `expect(start).toBeGreaterThan(-1)` — by
luck downstream, not by design; its `fixedMaxBranch()` has no emptiness check at all. **So the rule is
about the INDEX, not the slice:** assert every marker `>= 0` BEFORE slicing, then assert length.
`not.toBe('')` is never adequate — `-1` is truthy and `slice(-1)` is non-empty. And the lesson about the
sweep itself: a mechanical audit is only as good as the shapes its pattern admits, so report what the
pattern covered rather than what the code contains.

### Tooling, and two standing orders

- **`improve:pull-planned`.** A `planned` item's PLAN TEXT was **unreachable from the CLI**: `boardStatus()`
  selects `left(id::text, 8)` so the full id never leaves the database, `pull-item` needs a whole uuid, and
  `pullPlannable`/`pullApproved`/`pullBlocked` all skip `planned`. That matters because a plan goes stale
  while it waits — r373 shipped an item whose approved plan's central premise had become false.
- **`scratchpad/` is now gitignored.** It was not, and a build agent's render evidence reached **4.2 MB**
  untracked in a worktree, one `git add -A` from being committed.

### ⚠️ THREE GATE ATTEMPTS, AND BOTH REDS WERE RESOURCE CONTENTION, NOT CODE

| attempt | result | cause |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 8 failed, **0 AssertionErrors**, 8 unrelated suites | two builders' vitest vs the per-chunk cluster rebuild |
| 2 | 9 failed, **0 AssertionErrors**, 4 × `Hook timed out in 30000ms` | a builder's `tsc` at **1.19 GB** (later 2.4 GB) beside 3 vitest workers |
| 3 | **GREEN 16/16** | gate held BOTH lock slots |

Two mechanisms, both now in §10:

1. **`gate-chunked.sh` calls `dev-db-rebuild.sh` INSIDE its per-chunk loop**, so a 16-chunk gate rebuilds
   the whole cluster 16 times. That destroys any concurrent vitest's databases **whatever its
   `TEST_DB_NAMESPACE`** — a namespace separates agents from *each other*, never from a cluster rebuild.
2. **`testlock.sh` has two slots, so it grants a builder one while the gate holds the other.** It was never
   a gate lock.

**The fix is not a better instruction — it is making the lock enforce it.** Hold both slots by nesting:
`testlock.sh gate-a -- testlock.sh gate-b -- <gate>`. Nesting also **self-sequences**: it waited 40s for a
builder's in-flight `tsc` to release slot.2, so nothing had to be killed. The instruction route cannot
work on its own, because a message reaches an agent at its *next tool round* — useless when it is already
blocked inside a two-minute `tsc`.

**One diagnostic correction owed:** I was counting "environment-shaped errors" with a grep that also matches
benign Postgres `does not exist, skipping` migration notices, which inflated it to 136 and 129. The signal
that actually held both times was **failing tests with ZERO AssertionErrors**. A single real AssertionError
in attempt 2 (`test/tp1-relief-redesign.test.ts`, `not to contain '9999'`) turned out to be collateral too —
chunk 1 is green in attempt 3 with no change to that test.

`String.prototype.slice` reads a negative start as `length + start`, so **a −1 start lands after the end

before the fix: slice length **0**. Several rounds believed the EA labels were guarded. The case now

### `f022dd70` — payroll-cycle multi-selection, built AGAINST its own approved plan

The plan said the wage column already double-counts on a multi-run month, that this feature neither
causes nor fixes it, and told the reporter: *"picking a single cycle will often show a smaller, more
correct wage figure than picking All. That difference is the old fault showing, not a new one."*

**That premise died inside the same branch.** r372's wage fix landed first, and with it in place the
plan's own prescription — filter the payslip query, hand the existing fold a shorter list — produces the
error in the **opposite** direction. `core/payroll.ts:6582` stamps `statBases.epf` as the whole month's
normal wage, re-derived from compensation on **every** run, including a bonus run that paid only a bonus.
So a Bonus-only Borang A built by filtering would print the full month's salary as Upah. Measured
against a real kernel: **Upah 5200 where 1200 is correct.**

So the two wage-bearing reads still read the **whole month** and apply the selection afterwards; only
CP39, which has no wage column, filters its SQL. `scopedMonthWagesFrom` decomposes EPF by stream: the
**normal** stream counts only if the selection holds a `run_type = 'regular'` run, and the **additional**
stream contributes the sum of the selected runs' own increments, each measured against the previous
stamped run **of the month** — which is precisely why the query may not be filtered: *an increment cannot
be read off a run whose predecessor was filtered out.* Ticking everything telescopes back to the
unfiltered answer, asserted to the sen, and `monthWagesFrom` is untouched.

New: `lib/payroll-run-selection.ts` (absent ⇒ every run, which makes the no-change guarantee structural;
a malformed value **refuses** rather than silently building the file over a different population than the
URL named), `listFilableRunsForPeriod`, `app/payroll/payment-submission/runs/route.ts` (reaching payroll
**through `packs/payroll/service`**), and the `run-picker`. Three new 422 refusals, all legible.

run, but `bases.socsoEis` is stamped on every run, so a selection with no regular run would carry a full
month's salary against **zero** contributions. `socsoEisOutsideSelection` holds the PDF, the text export
and the upload file with a named reason. Raised as `99a46b4e` for the reporter to decide, rather than

### Findings that outlive this round

**A dev fixture that finishes and then never exits is holding a pool it never meant to open.**
`db/client.ts:265` creates the app singleton **at import time**, and `db/client.ts:163` caches pools by
connection **string** — `DATABASE_URL` and `MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL` are different strings for the same
database, so a fixture ends up with two pools. Closing its own leaves Node alive on the other's idle
handle: **zero active queries, zero CPU, indefinite hold on the dev-DB lock.** One fixture ran 18
minutes that way and was killed as "hung" when it had in fact finished. The discriminator is a single
import: `core/payroll.ts` takes only *types* from `db/client` (erased, no pool), `core/comp.ts` takes a
*value* (pool opens). End a throwaway fixture with an explicit `process.exit(0)`. Add to the bar for
any fixture: **runs clean twice AND exits without being killed.** macOS has no `timeout`.

**`pnpm db:seed` cannot support a render check on any payroll-derived document.** `db/seed.ts`
TRUNCATEs `payroll_batch` and `payslip` and inserts **neither** (`select count(*) from payslip` → 0),
and the demo companies have **no address columns**, so an EA employer block off a bare seed is ~12
characters and exercises the *unchanged* path. Such a check looks green and tests nothing. Drive the
kernel instead. This narrows the standing instruction that the seed needs no override — true for the
seed, false for anything payroll-derived.

**The scratchpad and the dev port are shared, and that can make one agent report another's evidence as
its own.** Two agents both chose `scratchpad/render/` and port 3111. One's cleanup deleted the other's
served PDFs mid-round. It was caught only because a `dev.log` one had just written contained
`GET /payroll/pcb-detail?…` requests it never made. **A render check's evidence IS `dev.log`, and
reading a sibling's is indistinguishable from reading your own.** Round-scope the output directory and
the port, for the same reason `TEST_DB_NAMESPACE` exists.

**A database test is not automatically the stronger test.** A revert that *failed* the pure test
*passed* the database test, because Postgres happened to return rows in `run_seq` order. The DB test
was the more easily fooled one. Pin the invariant, not the order the database happens to give you.

**Absent means leave alone, never `""`.** Saving EPF blanked SOCSO's code by writing a field it had no
value for.

**"Grep before the gate" has to include positive assertions naming the expression being deleted.**
A guard asserting `toContain('b.epf')` was invisible to searches for retired prose and retired shapes,
because it asserted the *presence* of what was being removed rather than the absence of what was added.

**A stale `.next/` reports a deleted route as a source error.** After the statutory route was removed,
`tsc` failed in `.next/types/validator.ts` naming a `page.js` that no longer exists. `.next/` is
gitignored; clearing it made `tsc` exit 0. Generated output is not source, and it is evidence about the
last build, not this tree.

**A committed dev fixture is bound by the pack boundaries — `scripts/` is scanned.** The first
integration gate went red in two chunks, both on `scripts/dev-fixture-pcb-detail.ts`: ADR-0080 **D9**
(`test/payroll-pack-drift.test.ts`) for importing `core/payroll`, and **D7/D4**
(`test/country-pack-drift.test.ts`) for importing `localization/my/statutory`. Both allowlists say they
only ever shrink, so an entry would have been the failure rather than the fix. The fixture keeps driving
the kernel — raw INSERTs would fake the very thing a payroll render check exists to exercise — and goes
through the seams instead: `packs/payroll/service` (which re-exports both modules wholesale) and
`requirePackFor('MY').statutory.set/.setTax`, which per `localization/country-pack.ts` **are**
`setStatutoryProfileMY`/`setTaxProfileMY`. The other committed fixture,
`scripts/dev-fixture-pooled-leave.ts`, trips neither because it writes via drizzle; the scripts that ARE
allowlisted are production/cron jobs. Checked after the change that the fixture still **runs and exits**
— `tsc` alone says nothing about a facade's twenty-module `export *` graph at runtime.

**A red gate is not automatically yours, and on 1 October it was the calendar.** The clock rolled over
mid-round and `test/r302fp-my-leave-fixpass.test.ts` went red at `00:03:18` on a file this round never
touched. Ownership was settled cheaply: the test and **every** source file it exercises are
byte-identical to `main`, so it fails on main too. The product is right —
`offeredLeaveYears` labels a cycle by how far BACK it is (`currentYear − N`), which r302 chose
deliberately because "the cycle that STARTS in year Y" showed one cycle twice and skipped another. The
TEST seeded both accruals in **January** and assumed those named years `YEAR-1`/`YEAR-2`; for an October
type a January row sits in the cycle that opened the *previous* October, and which N that is **flips on
the anniversary itself**. With the year unoffered, `resolveSelectedLeaveYear`'s
`years.includes(y) ? y : currentYear` **silently fell back to the current year**, so the second
selection came back equal to the first. Fixed by seeding inside the cycles the test selects. **When two
selections come back equal, suspect a silent fallback before suspecting the arithmetic.**

## r370 — 2026-09-30 · main@a5064c68 · no migration

The mobile app begins. ADR-0088 (Accepted) plus phase 1 slice 1: the server's mobile API foundation
and the Expo app. **Closes no board item** (shipped with `improve:deploy`). The owner asked for a mobile
app; the round answered in the order the facts forced: benchmark, decision, API, app.

### DECISIONS THE REQUEST DID NOT SETTLE
- **Native, not a PWA.** Challenged first (production authenticated nobody, there was no API, the web
  shell is desktop-only), then reversed by the owner's answers: store listing, anti-spoofing AND offline
  clocking are all required, and each needs native. Audience: employees + approvers; payroll/admin stay
  desktop. WorkOS cutover (readiness 1.3) goes first. All in ADR-0088.
- **Expo, not bare React Native.** Owner asked twice; answered with sources. The app code is React Native
  either way, `expo prebuild` makes the switch one-way safe, and EAS cloud builds route round this Mac's
  Xcode 16.0 (SDK 57 needs 26.4+).
- **A 30-vendor benchmark changed the plan** (`docs/research/hr-mobile-app-benchmark.md`). The three
  contradictions that changed ADR text: a mock-location flag of `false` proves NOTHING (Apple's own forums;
  a USB spoofer passes App Attest), so it adds nothing to `verified`; attestation cannot run offline, so
  offline punches are signed with a key attested at registration; iOS `systemUptime` stops in sleep.
  Plus: record every failed clock-in as an attempt (the lateness-penalty complaint that dominates
  Malaysian reviews), foreground-only location, and face matching out of scope (sensitive data under
  Act A1727).
- **My own draft set two different rules for the same employee.** ADR-0070's web path REFUSES an out-of-fence
  punch; the first ADR-0088 draft only flagged it on mobile. Corrected: core's geofence is the one rule,
  the mobile evidence ledger sits beside it.
- **WorkOS refresh needs no secret, although the reference page says it does.** WorkOS's own
  expo-authkit-example refreshes from the device, and @workos-inc/node 10.7.0 serialises `client_secret`
  from an absent key. Working code outranked the docs; no server-side refresh proxy.

### WHAT SHIPPED
- `lib/session.ts` `getMobileSession()`: a verified WorkOS bearer JWT → the SAME `principal_by_subject` →
  `resolveWorkosPrincipal` → `withEntitlements`. Bearer only, never the `dev_user` cookie; refuses
  everything while `WORKOS_CLIENT_ID` is unset — **so on production today every mobile call is a 401.**
- `lib/mobile-api/jwt.ts`: RS256-only with `node:crypto` (jose is only transitive), client-scoped JWKS,
  kid rotation with a rate-limited refresh, stale keys served through an outage; outage = 503, credential
  fault = 401. `iss`/`aud` deliberately NOT checked: parity with the web's own AuthKit verifier.
- `contract.ts` (zod, strips unlisted keys: `myEmployments`' basic/allowance cannot reach a phone),
  `handler.ts` `mobileRoute()` (the only way a route gets a session or sends a body; no-store; bare

- `core/read.ts` `myReleasedPayslips`: the released-only rule had lived ONLY in `app/me/page.tsx`; a
  second consumer would have shown employees their payslips before payday.
- `middleware.ts`: `/api/mobile/*` bypasses the Basic CHALLENGE (the bearer needs the header), never the
  unconfigured refusal.
- `mobile/` (npm, own lockfile, excluded from root tsc/ESLint): expo-router, PKCE in the system browser,
  SecureStore `WHEN_UNLOCKED_THIS_DEVICE_ONLY`, single-flight refresh, biometric/passcode unlock,

- WorkOS **Staging** redirect `aihr://auth/callback` added (placeholder scheme until the store name).

1085 of 1085 files, 16 chunks, `VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=3`, every chunk exit 0, counts read from the chunk

## r368 (2026-09-30) — two documents stopped saying things that were not true. `main@149ef06f`, **no migration**.

Closed: `970e4143`, `c8282468`. Gate: **1069 files — equal to the suite file count**, 16 chunks at `VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=4`, zero AssertionErrors, first attempt. `tsc` 0, `next build` 0, `i18n-check` PASS.

### 970e4143 — A PAYSLIP THAT STATED RM99,999 TAKEN FROM RM11,000 OF PAY

Two faults, both reproduced on real generated documents before anything was changed.

**The rows over-added.** CP38 is folded into stored `other_deductions`, and the renderers printed a CP38 row *and* a residual that still contained it — so the lines exceeded the total printed beneath them by exactly the instalment.

**And the stamped figure was the PRE-CLAMP one.** On a clamped instalment the document overstated what was taken:

```
BEFORE   CP38 99,999.00 · Other deductions 9,748.35     rows = 111,000.00
         TOTAL DEDUCTIONS 11,000.00
AFTER    CP38  9,623.35 · Other deductions    125.00     rows =  11,000.00
```

`99,999` now appears nowhere — zero occurrences in both PDFs and both screens.

**⚠️ EIGHT SURFACES, NOT SEVEN — AND `grep` IS WHY WE THOUGHT OTHERWISE.** `app/payroll/transaction-view/history-pivot.ts` joins a composite key on a literal NUL (`` `${companyId}\x00${runType}` ``). `file` reports it as **`data`**, and plain `grep -c` prints **nothing at all and exits 0** — not "Binary file … matches", nothing. `grep -ac` finds six. The plan, built on a repo-wide grep, asserted the file "contains NO cp38 … do not go looking for a correct residual there, there isn't one." It contained both, printed the pre-clamp figure, and drove a column to **−3,393.35** on a clamped slip. Found only because the builder read the directory rather than trusting the search. **Use `grep -ra` for any sweep whose completeness you are about to rely on.**

Two of the eight did not double-count — they fell SHORT, having no residual row at all, and one of them carried a header asserting "the deduction columns visibly reconcile against Total Deductions". They didn't. Prose fixed with the code.

**The fixture was built so the test could fail.** With a CP38 alone, `other_deductions` IS the instalment, the residual nets to zero, and a double-counting renderer draws exactly what a correct one draws. A keyed deduction item makes the two figures differ, and the vacuity guard refuses that shape — plus a zero CP38, a zero column and a zero residual — before any sum is asserted.

### c8282468 — THE CORRECTION SCREEN PROMISED A PREVIOUS VALUE NOTHING STORED

The caption told HR the system records "who changed it, when, the previous value and this reason". Who, when and why were kept; **the previous value was not stored anywhere** — a blind upsert with no read of the existing row, and an after-only event payload.

It now records a top-level `{before, after}` pair over one named 33-column projection used for both sides, so they cannot carry different key sets. `after` is **re-read from the row**, never assembled from the inputs, because the OT path can re-assert minutes after the upsert and an assembled value would report a figure not on the row.

**The 14 geo/method columns are in the pair.** A correction nulls them today and nothing said so; that clearing now shows as a loss instead of vanishing — which matters, because it is the evidence the punch happened where it claims.

The key was **renamed** rather than reworded, so `67268d83` round 2 cannot compile against the stale caption. Fourteen real `old → new` lines were read out of the live audit markup in both locales, with no UI work — the renderer already handled the convention.

### JUDGEMENT CALLS

- `calcTrace` is in the pair, so one line of the audit entry is truncated JSON among thirteen clean ones. **Kept**: it is destroyed data and the old figures' working cannot be re-derived. Narrowing how object values render is a separate display item.
- Zakat was left alone by instruction. An OBSERVATION stands unreproduced: the three screens print a zakat row on `zakat > 0` without consulting `countedInTotal`, unlike the PDF, so a pre-3a092cf0 slip's screen and its own PDF can disagree.

### NOT DONE

## r365 (2026-09-30) — a standing manual EPF amount, and the Leave Credit row gets its space back. `main@9cb50181`, **migration 0491**.

Closed: `70b14723`, `cbfa8b0b` (**round one of three**). Gate: **1060 files — equal to the suite file count**, 16 chunks at `VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=4`, zero AssertionErrors, first attempt on a machine verified quiet. `tsc` 0, `next build` 0, `i18n-check` PASS, `gate:shadow` PASS 404/404.

### 70b14723 — AND THE ANSWER BEGAN WITH "YOU CAN ALREADY DO MOST OF THIS"

Payroll → Statutory Adjustment already lets an operator type an exact employee AND employer EPF amount with a mandatory reason, and it already survives every reprocess — because it is stored as an INPUT the generator reads, not as an output it overwrites. **It was not rebuilt.** What was missing is a STANDING per-employee amount: the adjustment's window is `status === 'processed'` only, so the order is process-then-adjust and the figure is re-keyed every month.

Where both exist the adjustment still wins, because it runs after the pack's computation — and its own "system" leg now records the standing amount it displaced, so the screen can say which of the two produced the figure.

**THE AMOUNT IS SUBSTITUTED INSIDE THE PACK'S EPF COMPUTATION, and the arithmetic is why.** Applying it after the statutory core would charge the full monthly amount onto a bonus run as well — the mis-application ADR-0046 predicted — and would need an `isAdditionalRun` special case. Inside, it telescopes for free: `deltaStat` charges the month with this run's additional minus the month without, so for a constant M the additional run charges `max(0, M − M) = 0` and a regular run restating a bonus month charges `M − (M − M) = M`. Charged once, in any order, with no special case anywhere. And Kₜ is defined as the month's lookup minus the same lookup on the normal wage alone, so through the **same function** Kₜ = 0 by subtraction and K₁ + Kₜ = the employee EPF exactly.

Four rules needed it, not one: `epf()` is reached only by Part A, so the non-citizen flat rate, Part E and the age ≥ 75 short-circuit were substituted at `epfContribution` too. **No round-up** (a typed figure is not a schedule reading) and **no floor** — this is the only EPF mode that can go down, which is the point.

**It extended r364's provenance seam rather than building beside it**: one member on the source union, one arm, no second banner and no second label. One shape change was needed and is the right one — the seam's single `reason` string became one note per source, because two sources can sit on one payslip and a single string silently attaches one decision's justification to the other.

Surfaces that would otherwise have failed silently and are in: the **multi-cycle worksheet**, which re-derives EPF from wages and would have verdicted every manual employee-month "unexplained" on a document an accountant signs; the **audit event**, which recorded the mode after-only while the block beside it had proper before/after; and the **zakat election's read-modify-write**, which would have nulled the amounts and then thrown.

**TWO DEVIATIONS FROM THE APPROVED PLAN, BOTH BECAUSE THE PLAN ASKED FOR SOMETHING THAT CANNOT EXIST.**

- The plan said to offer the three categories in the create-employee wizard with no amount boxes. That combination is unreachable: the resolver refuses a manual category with no amount, and it runs inside a step the draft reaches only AFTER the employee has been committed. The choice would either fail an activation that had already created a person, or be silently downgraded to Auto — a wrong payslip on a money field. It downgrades **explicitly**, with a hint pointing at the card that has the boxes.
- "Refused if you leave its amount blank" is narrowed to "no amount on EITHER side". The three categories ARE the three combinations of two nullable amounts — nothing stores a category — so an employee amount with a blank employer amount IS "Manual (Employee by Amount)", and the employer side keeping the schedule is what a blank side means.

**THE VACUITY TRAP CAUGHT THE BUILDER TWICE, AND IT FIXED BOTH RATHER THAN CLAIMING THEM.** The KWSP submission-file case spelled the seven-field mapping out inline instead of calling the mapper the production route uses, so zeroing the employee contribution left it **green**. And "Kₜ = 0" is two claims: on Part A the zero falls out of the substitution itself, so removing the wrapper's explicit zero changed nothing. The branch case now runs all four rules with a bonus and asserts the rule figures it displaces are non-zero, so it cannot pass on branches with nothing to zero.

### cbfa8b0b ROUND ONE — and the reporter's complaint was arithmetic

"The row is too crowded, with text overlapping under Day Type" was not a matter of taste. The filled cell stacks a 16px line and an 11px line that inherits the same 16px line-height inside a fixed 36px box with 8px of padding — **40px of content in 36px**, on every filled row. Dropping the two reference columns for one Attendance column with a View button is what gives the row its space back, and the browser run now measures the caption ending at 355.8 inside a cell running to 362.8.

**No popover primitive existed** — neither Radix popover nor tooltip is installed. Rather than add one, the working anchored panel that had lived inline in the attendance figure cells since 7c834696 was extracted to `components/ui/anchored-panel.tsx` and BOTH callers moved onto it, with the below-`lg` sheet handled by the Drawer this product already has. The reporter asked for a bottom sheet; there is no bottom sheet, and the plan said so rather than inventing one.

**THE EXTRACTION WAS UNFALSIFIABLE UNTIL THIS ROUND.** `AttendanceFigureCells` had no DOM test at all, so "behaviour preserved" could not be checked. It now has one — with **stubbed rects**, because jsdom has no layout and every unstubbed placement assertion would pass identically whatever the code did.

**Approved Plan OT moved to the EMPLOYEE's panel**, because the case the reporter asked for on the approver's side cannot arise: the OT/credit overlap check blocks in both directions, so a claim sitting in a queue can never carry an approved plan for the same date. On the employee's panel it pre-explains a refusal they would otherwise hit at submit.

### A GUARD THAT PASSED WITH ITS OWN DEFECT APPLIED

The source guard for "the panel must not block the claim" scanned the `blocked` expression for forbidden words and **went green** with the blocking predicate in place — because the predicate was defined three lines above and reached by an innocuous name inside. Replaced with an exact-set assertion over the gate's operands, which then failed naming the intruder. That is the second guard in two rounds found vouching for nothing, after r364's layout guard counting a tag inside a comment.

### VERIFICATION, STATED AS A CHAIN

Both items' screens were driven in a real browser by their builders, under `devdb-lock.sh`, with fixtures the seed cannot produce. On the merged tree the six files they rendered are **byte-identical by git object hash**, so that evidence carries; on top of it, this round's own merged-tree check confirms both screens serve 200 with zero i18n errors, the retired Leave Credit cells are gone from the markup, all three EPF categories reach the client island, and **the Statutory Detail export was opened and read** — a real spreadsheet whose two "system calculated" columns are correctly ABSENT on unadjusted data, which is the evidence that an ordinary export is unchanged.

### NOT DONE, AND NAMED

- **The status dot cannot see a clock-out that reads as next day.** `actualClockOut` is a time with no date, so someone who clocked out at 17:00 and claims 18:00–23:51 produces no dot. It needs a dated clock-out from the attendance engine, and **a test now pins the wrong answer** so a later round cannot paper over it with a better guess.
- **The panel pre-explains only an APPROVED overtime plan, while submit is refused by pending OR approved.** The mockup said approved and that is what shipped; closing the gap is a line and a sentence in six locales — a copy decision the reporter has not been asked.
- Rounds two (the attendance snapshot, migration **0492**) and three (the approver's View with the Claimed/Recorded comparison) are deliberately unbuilt. The guard pinning that is written **by shape** rather than by a journal number, after a first cut asserting `max(idx) === 490` went stale within the hour.
- The create-employee wizard does not offer the manual categories, for the reason above; the Statutory Detail export's *positive* case (columns present with an adjustment) is held by a guard proven to bite rather than by a downloaded file.

## r364 (2026-09-29) — the EA form says how many children again, and three screens stop asserting things that were not true. `main@d5a2697a`, **no migration**.

Closed: `fda53352`, `c36e1ae6`, `ec30b2e9`, `208beb8b`. Gate: **1058 files — equal to the suite file count**, 16 chunks at `VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=4`, zero AssertionErrors, first attempt. `tsc` 0, `next build` 0, `scripts/i18n-check.mjs` PASS.

### fda53352 — WE PUT A WRONG FIGURE ON A FORM EMPLOYEES SIGN, AND THE REPORTER CAUGHT IT

r359 made EA item 8 the s.48-**weighted** child figure — 9 for an employee with two children, and **fractional** for a shared-custody child, so the live form could print "4.5 children". It is a count. `Bilangan anak yang layak untuk pelepasan cukai`; the agency's own English is "Number of children qualified for tax relief".

**The evidence was inside the document r359 cited.** `pcb-calculation-slip-specimen-2026-12.pdf` (renamed in r369; see the correction at the foot of the r359 entry — it is a filled specimen, NOT an agency publication, and the conclusion below rests on LHDN's own specification, whose printed p.10 and p.27 say the same) prints a child grid on **page 1** showing one child under 18 and one disabled child still studying — **two children** — and `C = Number of eligible children 9.00` on **page 6**. LHDN prints 2 where it means children and 9 where it means C, in one file. r359 read half of it and reasoned from the MTD specification, which governs the monthly tax calculation and not this form. **This repo's own field register said so at r351 and r359 overrode it.**

- A.8 is a count again, per mode, and **a 50% shared child counts as ONE** — both branches return integers, so a fraction is now unreachable.
- The false invariant is gone. r359 asserted `A.8 × per-child deduction IS D.6`; the weighting is exactly why that is false, and the case now asserts its negation with r359's claim quoted under a REVERSED banner.
- **One behaviour is deliberately not r353's**: a missing count in a column-reading mode now prints the agency's empty rule rather than `0`, because `0` asserts that no child qualifies.
- **The part r359 got RIGHT is untouched** and was confirmed green: on the MTD worksheet Q is the per-child deduction and C is the weighted number, because LHDN's slip prints exactly that.

### 208beb8b — a screen that credited a typed figure to a government schedule

Overriding EPF through Statutory Adjustment left the Statutory Detail screen dividing the amount by the wage and printing the result as an effective rate **captioned as the KWSP Third Schedule**. The money was right; the explanation was false, on the one screen whose job is defending a figure to an auditor.

Fixed across **all nine** adjustment lines, not the one the ticket named — and the sharpest was HRD levy, the only line printing `base × rate = amount`, an equation that stops evaluating the moment somebody types the amount.

**The compile-time guard did the work it exists for.** `RULE_LABEL` is exhaustive by type in the view *and in the export route*, so adding `'manual'` broke `tsc` in both — which is the mechanism that forces the file an auditor downloads to be updated in the same pass. It was not widened to silence it, and the export was demonstrated failing with the banner absent: truth on screen, schedule in the file.

### c36e1ae6 + ec30b2e9

The Leave Credit amber warning fired on **every** rest-day, off-day and holiday row whether or not a clock-out existed, because `derive`'s two exits disagreed and the assessed one asked about an argument it had deliberately nulled. Display-only, and proved so: with the fix reverted, minutes, credit and total are byte-identical while the warning returns.

The OT overwrite is refused — and **the trap was real**. The obvious guard sits inside `if (hasOt)`, which is also true for the clock correction the refusal message recommends; the naive version was demonstrated refusing the remedy in the same breath as suggesting it. The refusal is now a typed error resolved through the catalogue, and the Malay banner was read off the DOM, which a raw English throw cannot produce.

### THREE INSTRUMENTS THAT WERE NOT MEASURING

- **`<input>` is not permitted as a child of `<tr>`.** Four hidden fields sat directly under the Leave Credit row, so the parser foster-parented them out of the table and this screen logged a hydration error on every load. It had not corrupted a submission — foster-parenting preserves relative order and the action zips by index — but that is a coincidence, not a contract, and by-index zipping is the only contract that form has.
- **A layout guard counted a tag inside a comment.** Explaining the above pushed `expect(src.match(/<table/g)).toBe(1)` to 2. A tag in a comment is not a tag, exactly as a guard name in a comment is not a call — the same blind spot r362 fixed in the auth guard, inverted.
- **A test asserted a rest-day row must HIDE a clock-out the system holds.** Not one of the two guards the brief named; the builder found the real one and inverted it with the old claim quoted.
