## r363 (2026-09-29) — one word for one state, one name per field, and two sentences that contradicted themselves. `main@4493a096`, **no migration**.

Closed: `4c8aae68`, `e0b6e3b8`. Gate: **1058 files — equal to the suite file count**, 16 chunks at `VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=4`. Chunks 2–16 green in the full run; **chunk 1 went red on contention I caused and green on a quiet re-run** (67/67 files, 912/912 tests). See the note at the foot, `tsc` 0, `next build` 0, `scripts/i18n-check.mjs` PASS.

### 4c8aae68 — the screen stopped using two words for one state

My Attendance Request Status lists overtime plans AND attendance corrections, and `cancelled` rendered "Withdrawn" on one and "Cancelled" on the other, with a filter chip that had to pick one and therefore disagreed with half its own rows.

**Revision 1 of this plan was a half-measure and was rejected as one.** It changed only the chip, which relocates the mismatch onto the correction rows. What settled it is who can write the state: exactly two callers exist in the whole tree, `cancelPlannedOvertime` and `cancelOwnAttendanceCorrection`, and **both are subject-only**. Nobody but the employee can put a row there, so "the employee took their own request back" is the only thing it can mean — and the comment defending the split ("'Cancelled' would read as somebody else having called it off") was arguing from a premise true of both branches.

- Display text only. The stored enum, `REQUEST_STATUSES`, `?status=cancelled` and every function name are untouched, and **`attendance-screens-layout` cases C, A2 and D passed with zero edits** — which is the evidence, not a claim.
- The new guard compares the chip, a cancelled OVERTIME row and a cancelled CORRECTION row **to each other in all six locales**, never to the literal "Withdrawn", and asserts the two row kinds really take different branches before comparing. Pinning the English would pass against a screen that had drifted apart again.

**And the round created one inconsistency of its own, fixed here rather than logged.** The refusal interpolated the stored enum, so a taken-back row read "already been **cancelled**, so it can no longer be **withdrawn**". A status-to-word map is presentation and does not belong in the kernel; naming the state is not what the sentence is for. It now says "no longer waiting for a decision" — true of approved, rejected and withdrawn alike, and it leaks no enum. The guard gained an assertion that the message must not match `/approved|cancelled|rejected|pending/`.

### e0b6e3b8 — the filter and the field beside it had the same name

r360 made the payslip body print the configured cycle name; the chooser above it still narrows by run TYPE, and **both labels were the identical string in all six catalogues**. One code line changed — the label — proven by filtering comments out of `git diff -U0`. The five tests that prove the change is display-only passed **untouched**. The translations reuse the term a human translator already approved for the same concept on the Payroll Cycle configuration screen: a new key, not new wording.

**THE EXISTING i18n GUARD STRUCTURALLY CANNOT SEE THIS CLASS OF BUG.** `i18n-coverage`'s Check C skips any file binding more than one namespace, and that screen binds five — so Check C gives ZERO signal there. Only Check A applies, and Check A is presence-in-every-locale, which passed happily for however long the two labels were identical. Demonstrated: with one locale's new label set equal to the old one, **`i18n-coverage` passed** while the new value-level case failed. Two labels being the same words is not a missing key, and nothing in this repo was looking for it.

### THE GATE WENT RED ONCE, AND IT WAS MINE

Chunk 1 reported 10 failed files and **zero AssertionErrors**: 9 hook timeouts, 2 Postgres deadlocks (`40P01`, `AccessExclusiveLock` on TRUNCATE) and one test timeout, with an `import` phase of **897s against ~30s in every other chunk**. I had merged and launched the gate within a couple of minutes of a build agent finishing its render check, without confirming its dev server and Postgres connections had been released — and `dev-db-rebuild.sh` rebuilds the cluster once per chunk.

**It was diagnosed rather than assumed**, because §4 warns that the same zero-AssertionError signature is what a file failing to IMPORT looks like. Three things separated them: none of the 10 failing files reads any file this round changed; two of them had run green in a builder's own 29-file run on this code minutes earlier; and the re-run on a quiet machine came back 67/67 in 95s with import at 44s. Only then was it called contention.

### NOT DONE

- **`pnpm db:seed` produces a database that cannot be paid.** One seeded employee is hired with no compensation row while every other one gets one, so `generatePayslips` over that scope fails closed with `PreProcessBlockedError` — which blocks the §8 render check on every payroll screen. One line to fix, but 10+ tests read the seeder and the gate was already running, so it is recorded rather than slipped in.
- **The same concept now has two names across screens.** Transaction View's filter also narrows by run type and is still labelled "Payroll cycle". No collision there — that screen has no cycle-name field beside it — but the product is inconsistent until it is renamed.
- `statusLabel`'s `isOvertime` parameter is now dead on every branch. Kept deliberately, because dropping it forces an edit to case A2, which exists precisely because a verifier once mutated that argument and nothing failed. The cost is recorded: A2 has degraded from a behaviour test to a shape check, and the new equality case is what actually pins the property now.

## r362 (2026-09-29) — seven board items, two repo-wide guards that were not guarding, and three money paths a new record shape would have broken. `main@8d8396bf`, **migration 0490**.

Closed: `2aef3cd8`, `ce5ded11`, `5c72039e`, `58424c7f`, `3f15ffdb`, `b833a077`, `f618065d`. Gate: **1057 files — equal to the suite file count**, 16 chunks at `VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=4`, zero AssertionErrors, `tsc` 0, `next build` 0. Shipped together with r361 in one deploy.

**Round number:** a concurrent session holds `build/r360-security-fixes`; r360 and r361 were taken here first, so that work takes the next free number. Round ids belong to the history entry, not the branch name.

### TWO REPO-WIDE GUARDS WERE GREEN WITHOUT CHECKING ANYTHING

Both were found by reading, not reported, and both are the same failure: **an instrument everybody trusts, quietly measuring nothing.**

- **`test/function-access.test.ts` accepted a comment as an authentication guard.** It tested RAW source, so `GUARD_RE` matched the guard name inside the header comment that EXPLAINS the guard. A page could lose `await scopedSession()` and stay "guarded" for as long as its comment still named it — and this is the repo's ONLY page-boundary auth check. Measured before changing: of every `page.tsx` under `app/`, **exactly one** is classified differently once comments are stripped, and it is a documented redirect-only segment that reads nothing. Comments are now stripped and the exemption is EXACT, so it is stronger in both directions: lose a real guard and the set grows and names the route; give the redirect a guard and the exemption goes unmatched. The old assertion passed with the first defect applied.
- **`scripts/i18n-check.mjs` printed FAIL on a clean tree**, on placeholder drift in all five non-English locales. It was not drift. The extractor could not tell an ICU argument from a one-word branch body — they are spelled identically — so `other {applies}` read as a placeholder named `applies`, while the translations say `terpakai` / `适用` and matched nothing. That one word was the entire "drift", in every locale. **A gate that always fails is worse than no gate**: a real drift arrives as one more line in noise everyone has learned to skip. It now walks the message instead of matching it, and PASSES across 12,376 keys × 5 locales — with a renamed and a deleted placeholder both still caught.

### 3f15ffdb — AN APPROVED LEAVE RECORD WITH NO LEDGER DEBIT IS A SHAPE THIS SYSTEM HAD NEVER HAD

Leave History Import writes `leave_request` rows (status approved, no approval steps, **no ledger row**) because Leave History IS `leave_request`. Every consumer was swept, and three of them were wrong for the new shape. **All three are money.**

- **`applyLeaveCancellationApprovalTx` — phantom deduction.** The whole-span reversal was guarded on `chargedDays > 0`; the **per-segment re-debit was not**. Giving back 1 day of a 5-day uncharged record reversed 0.00 and then inserted a fresh **−4.00** — days taken off a balance that was never charged. **Reachable by an ordinary employee**, because a migration legitimately carries approved future leave. The guard tests the LEDGER, not the import marker, and is pinned by a case using a non-imported uncharged row.
- **`unpaidDaysByEmployment` — salary cut.** It reads `leave_request`, not the ledger. One imported unpaid record in a not-yet-run period would have cut that person's pay.
- **`approvedLeaveDaysAfter` — false final-pay hint**, whose premise ("already debited at approval") is false for these rows.

The existing importer was NOT duplicated: it is the **balance** importer (ledger-only), and it was renamed "Leave Balance Import" so the two stop reading as the same thing. Migration **0490**, allocated from `max(idx)`, never `entries.length`; a PARTIAL unique index so ordinary rows stay unconstrained; GRANTed.

### ce5ded11 — THE OT PLAN CALENDAR, BUILT FROM THE REPORTER'S PROSE RATHER THAN THEIR SCREENSHOTS

Sections 1–12 of that ticket transcribe two photographs of a rival product. The approved plan was built around the reporter's own sentence instead, and every refusal in its OUT list is now held by a test. The month read calls the existing `classifyScheduleDay` rather than restating the precedence ladder, and the grid reuses `lib/roster-month.ts`, so the OT calendar cannot disagree with the roster screen. Every shade carries a word — in the cell, in the `aria-label` and in the legend.

**A claim in the build brief was wrong and the builder caught it**: `<ToastFromQuery />` is already mounted in the root layout, so "render the toast nothing reads" would have shown the confirmation twice. The stale comment was corrected instead.

### b833a077 — A REMOVAL WHOSE KEPT PIECES WERE HELD BY A COMMENT

My Travel is gone from the menu, the page, the approvals screen and the bell; the table and every row stay. **Four of the ticket's removal targets did not exist** — the command palette never had a travel entry, the Mobile App Preview has no travel screen, no dashboard tile points at it, and `core/notifications.ts` has no travel event key at all: travel notified nobody, ever. They were re-verified rather than "removed".

**The find that justified the round.** The `lib/approval-history.ts` travel mapping was kept deliberately — and deleting it was GREEN: `tsc` 0, `test/approval-history.test.ts` and `i18n-coverage` both passing. The decision was held by a comment. And the consequence is worse than "blank": `moduleOfAggregate[r.aggregateType] ?? 'leave'` means every historic travel decision would have rendered as **"Leave"** in the approval history, for every tenant — a silent mislabel of the audit record that "keep it for audit" was supposed to buy. It is now guarded, and the obligation is **derived from the immutable migrations** (0288 / 0320) that still emit those events rather than restated, so if a later migration ever drops them the case fails and says the mapping may be retired.

**A brief of mine was wrong and the builder checked instead of complying.** I said the new redirect page would land in `function-access`'s registered-but-unguarded set and should be added to `REDIRECT_ONLY_ROUTES`. `/attendance/travel` is not in `REGISTERED_ROUTES` at all, and the assertion iterates that set — so adding it would have failed the exact-set check I had just tightened. Neither file was touched, and the fact is now pinned positively (`expect(REGISTERED_ROUTES.has(row.href)).toBe(false)`).

### f618065d — THREE OF THE ASKS WERE ALREADY TRUE, AND TWO MORE SHIPPED EARLIER TODAY

Already correct before the round and left alone: the list sorted by OT date descending, the screen reading "Withdrawn" and never "Cancelled", and Withdraw appearing only where it works. Already built by `ce5ded11` hours earlier: the Approved hours column, the Table/Calendar toggle and the date window on `myOvertimePlans` — so the table is nine columns, not the plan's eight.

Counts come from a **second GROUP BY aggregate**, never from the list, because the list is capped: chips computed over a capped page say "Pending 25" when there are 30, which is the defect `app/feedback/page.tsx` already documents. One predicate builder feeds both reads, so a chip and its rows cannot be narrowed differently. The behavioural fixture files **30 plans against a 25-row page** precisely so that case can fail.

**The build corrected itself against the plan's prose.** Its first cut shipped the refusal (we hold no approver's remark) and dropped the compensation the plan promised — the employee's own note and the decided date. Caught by re-reading the plan, not by a test.

### TWO MORE LIVE DEFECTS FIXED, NEITHER REPORTED

- **Every payslip older than r359 printed `Q = RM0.00` and `C = 0`** beside a QC holding the real relief — three cells that visibly do not multiply, on the screen used to defend a figure to an auditor. r359 added both fields and read them through a coercion that turns absence into zero, while `explainPcb`'s own doc already forbade exactly that ("it does NOT render the legs as zeroes"). Absence now stays absent; the asymmetry is asserted, because the old stamp DID record the relief and never recorded the split. Restoring the coercion fails with `expected { kind: 'money', amount: +0 } to deeply equal { kind: 'notRecorded' }`.
- **Self Overtime printed two dates by two different rules.** The new Submitted on column used `todayInKualaLumpur`; the "counted on" sub-line two rows below kept a UTC slice, naming the previous day for anything counted before 08:00 MYT. `today-in-myt-drift` does not catch it, and that is deliberate: it matches only the argless "what date is NOW" form, because date-only arithmetic is correct in UTC. **A stored instant rendered as a calendar day is neither, and falls in the gap** — so the screen pins both of its dates by name.

### THE SEED DOES NOT COVER EVERY SCREEN, AND NO OVERRIDE FIXES IT

Two rounds hit this independently. `/leave/credit` cannot be rendered from a seeded database at all — `toil` is deliberately excluded from `LEGACY_ENABLED_MODULE_CODES`, so **`TOIL_ENABLED=true pnpm db:seed` produces nothing**, and `DEV_USER_ID` is the HR Admin, who has no employment, so the employee form never renders. `/attendance/plan-ot/apply` seeds with zero shifts and zero roster rows, so a seed-only month proves nothing about the states the check exists for. Both were rendered by seeding and then adding the minimum on top through the product's own service functions. **The dev database is left carrying that state.** A committed per-screen fixture is the standing fix; three rounds have now paid this cost.

### 5c72039e + 58424c7f — ONE BUILDER, BECAUSE THEY ARE ONE FILE

The Day Type cell was serving three states with one sentence, and two of them were **indistinguishable in the state shape**: `facts[d]` is written `null` before the call and the action also resolves `null` for a malformed date. A third record settled in `.finally` tells them apart. One subtlety the plan missed: "resolved empty" is `settled && facts == null`, not `settled` alone — there is one committed render where the date is settled and the row's kind is still blank, and keying off `settled` flashes "Not found" on a row that found its answer.

58424c7f is a DEVIATION NOTICE discharged: we do not refuse an end time earlier than the start, because that is how a night shift is entered. `claimCrossesMidnight` is the roll's own condition lifted out, so the note and the arithmetic cannot drift. **Two money defects were demonstrated through it**: loosening `<` to `<=` brings back r353's full-day-of-free-credit (`expected 1440 to be +0`), and removing the roll turns a four-hour window into nothing (`expected '0' to be '240'`).

### NOT DONE, AND SAID OUT LOUD

- **`fda53352` was contested again during this round, and the reporter is right.** r359 changed EA item 8 to the s.48-weighted figure on the strength of the MTD specification and LHDN's PCB slip — **two documents that do not govern the EA form**. Item A.8 is `Bilangan anak yang layak untuk pelepasan cukai`; *bilangan* is a count. This repo's own field register said so at r351 and r359 overrode it. The wrong value is LIVE on a form employees sign. The r359 PCB-slip Q/C fix is correct and separate and must NOT be swept up in the reversal.
- Raised from findings, not reported: a second OT plan on a date whose hours already landed silently rewrites them (**payroll-affecting**, no test covers it); the Leave Credit clock-out warning fires on every non-workday row whether or not a clock-out exists; and two label inconsistencies.
- `approvedLeaveDates` is not narrowed against imported history, so an imported record suppresses an absence on its dates. Defensible and inert for a migration; named rather than done.

## r361 (2026-09-29) — the PCB detail reads down beside LHDN's own slip, end to end. `main@8d8396bf`, **no migration**.

Closed: `bf3c9712`. Shipped together with r362 in one deploy.

### THE ATTACHMENT WAS THE AGENCY'S OWN OUTPUT, AND IT SET THE STRUCTURE

The reporter attached LHDN's generated PCB Calculation Slip for one employee, 7 pages. Our screen already carried the whole MTD working — every letter the official p.6 defines — but not the two blocks that bracket it. Those are now built from the same run the working reads, so the two documents can be held side by side and read down in the same order.

- **Accumulated remuneration** (official p.1), itemised. The AMOUNT column is summed from the year's prior payslips over `core/payroll.ts`'s own predicate; the TOTAL column is read off the trace (Y, K, Σ(Y−K), X, Z) rather than re-summed, **so the block and the working cannot disagree**.
- **Calculation results** (official p.7) — Net MTD, MTD on additional remuneration, and the rounded figure the payslip actually paid, which is READ from the stamp and never re-rounded here.
- The working is presented as the official's two numbered steps.

### THREE LINES CARRY NO FIGURE, AND THAT IS THE HONEST ANSWER

Fees and commission (no such payroll column — such a pay item lands inside allowance or bonus), the accumulated departure levy (Z is the specification's own COMBINED zakat-and-levy accumulator, so no separate figure exists), and Y on a slip predating its stamp. **The approved plan said the block would carry "accumulated zakat AND levy". It cannot, and printing 0.00 there would deny money that may exist** — so that row says it is not recorded separately. BIK and VOLA do print 0.00, with a note saying the zero means we hold no such figure rather than that the agency has checked there is none.

### THE ITEMISATION AND THE TOTALS ARE TWO COLUMNS BECAUSE THEY ARE TWO MEASURES

The itemisation is what was PAID; Y accumulates what tax is CHARGED on, excluding exempt amounts, and the totals additionally carry the previous employer's TP3 seed. A reader adding the first six lines will not reach Y. The agency's own p.1 has both columns; the section note states both gaps in words.

### A GUARD THAT PASSED WITH THE DEFECT IN PLACE

Re-rounding the deducted figure (`nearestUpperFiveSen(x.pcb)`) left `7f251381`'s "the builder contains no arithmetic at all" **green** — the helper sits above its marker and the call site contains none of the tokens it refuses. The new case is the only thing between that defect and production: `expected { amount: 1234.6 } to deeply equal { amount: 1234.56 }`.

**And one case was vacuous until it was fixed rather than claimed.** The end-to-end results case was first written over a plain regular month, where Net MTD, the normal leg and the deduction are all the same number — the defect produced `Tests 1 passed`. That month now carries a bonus and a zakat so the three cells are three distinct figures, and the case asserts that premise before it asserts the figure.

### NOT DONE

- `pcbDetailModel` is described in three files' prose as the thing a test drives over both paths — and **no test was driving it**. The prose outlived the code. A behavioural assertion was added for the new `closing` field only; the rest of that claim is still unbacked.
- The additional-remuneration leg renders as a zero on the dev fixture (a bonus set on the fixture did not reach the payslip). The non-zero leg IS exercised by the end-to-end vitest case, so the reconciliation is proven with both legs alive — just not on the rendered page.

## r360 (2026-09-29) — the payslip names the real Pay Cycle, and the Day Type is read off the roster rather than asked for. `main@0166e01d`, **no migration**.

Closed: `1fe55a23` (payslip header), `cbfa8b0b` (leave credit Day Type). Gate: **1050 files — equal to the suite file count**, 16 chunks at `VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=4`, `tsc` 0, `next build` 0.

### 1fe55a23 — "Payroll payslip · Regular" was the enum, not the cycle

The reporter asked why the document called their monthly run "Regular". `Regular` is `payroll_batch.run_type`, one of the four fixed behavioural types the kernel gates on; the label they configured is `payroll_cycle.name`, and the batch has recorded which cycle opened it since migration 0441.

Three surfaces print this string from three different reads (the screen, the preview and the downloaded file — the last two are one route), and written out twice the rule is one edit away from a download disagreeing with the screen it came from. ## r359 (2026-09-29) — EA item 8 is C, and the slip's Q and C mean what the specification says. `main@3e4963f5`, **no migration**.

Closed: `fda53352` (revision 7). Gate: **1050 files — equal to the suite file count**, 16 chunks at `VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=4`, `tsc` 0, `next build` 0. Shipped together with r358 in one deploy.

### THE REPORTER WAS RIGHT AND TWO OF OUR ROUNDS WERE WRONG

r351 answered "A.8 is correct as a count" and r353 refined that per mode, both reading "Bilangan anak" as a count of child records. The third contest cited LHDN's own formula letters, and checking them settles it against us: printed p.10 defines "Q  Deduction for qualifying children" and "C  Number of qualifying children" with the P formula carrying the term QC; p.11 restates C per category; and p.27's table is headed **"Relief to be given AS IF THE EMPLOYEE HAS THIS NUMBER OF CHILDREN"**, 4 / 4 / 4 / 8. So C is the weighted figure, and A.8 asks for it in the same words.

**Then a filled specimen slip corroborated it.** ⚠️ CORRECTED IN r369: THIS SENTENCE ORIGINALLY READ "Then the agency's own output confirmed it" and called the attachment "LHDN's generated PCB Calculation Slip". It is not an agency publication — its metadata is Chrome/Skia with the document title "ReportEx2026", it is a FILLED calculation for a fictional employee for December 2026, and its English glossary is a different translation from LHDN's published one ("Individual cut" for D, where the specification prints "Deduction for individual"). Who produced it could not be established. **The conclusion is unaffected**, because it also rests on LHDN's own 2026 specification: printed p.10 defines C as the number of qualifying children and printed p.27 carries the weighting that makes 1 + 8 = 9. Cite the specification, never this file. The attachment on item `bf3c9712` is that specimen slip for the very employee in dispute; its page 6 prints `Q = Deduction for eligible children 2,000.00` and `C = Number of eligible children 9.00`, with `(2000.00 x 9)` inside the P line, for an employee whose page 1 child table shows one child under 18 and one disabled child still studying — 1 + 8 = 9.

### AND CHECKING OUR OWN SLIP AGAINST THAT DEFINITION FOUND A SECOND DEFECT

The PCB slip printed Q as the RM total and C as the record count — two letters from the agency's formula, neither meaning what the formula says, and not multiplying to the relief beside them (Q RM18,000 × C 2 implies RM36,000). Q is now the per-child deduction, C the weighted number, and their product is printed as its own row.

- `localization/my/reports.ts` — A.8 derives from `childReliefFromPayroll`, the same stamped annual relief D.6 prints, over the ruleset's per-child figure. **A.8 × RM2,000 === D.6 by construction.** ABSENT when that stamp is absent, because D.6 is absent then too.
- `localization/my/payroll.ts` — the trace carries C (from the money) and Q (from the ruleset). `reliefs.children` is untouched: **no money moves**, only what the slip calls it.
- the employee card — "Children on record" and "Qualifying children (C)", each naming the document that reads it. The reporter read EA item 8 off the wrong box for two rounds and nothing on the screen said which figure each form takes.

### TWO GUARDS THAT WOULD HAVE PASSED WHILE ASSERTING THE OPPOSITE

- `test/r217-ea-sections` greps for `String(d.employee.children)` and only that expression's SOURCE changed, so the reversal left it green with "A.8 must still print the head count" in its own message. That is the prose-outlives-the-kernel trap inside a test rather than a comment.
- My first Q×C identity assertion was **vacuous**: `richRun` gives the profile three children and no grid, so C equals the record count whatever the code does. Caught by reverting. The decisive case is the reporter's own employee — two children weighted to RM18,000 — which fails with `expected 2 to be 9`.

### WHAT THE FULL GATE CAUGHT THAT MY GREP DID NOT

`test/r353-ea-item8-child-count.test.ts` — five AssertionErrors in one chunk, a whole file pinning the old head-count rule that my pre-gate grep missed. ## r358 (2026-09-29) — every day type is claimed as a window, and the credit follows the hours. `main@3e4963f5`, **no migration**.

Closed: `70294f7a`. Gate: as above, shipped in the same deploy.

### THE OWNER RELEASED THE BLOCK WITH THE RULE WRITTEN OUT

"Whether the employee works on a Normal Working Day, Rest Day, Off Day, or Public Holiday, the Leave Credit calculation rule is the same. 4 hours of eligible work = 0.5 day. 8 hours = 1.0 day … regardless of the Day Type. … Day Type is only for identifying whether the employee worked on a Normal Working Day / Rest Day / Off Day / Public Holiday." That is Option A of the park, spelled out further.

**What the park was about, and how it is resolved.** Building this on the old shape would have switched Leave Credit off for every company: the table read `extendedHoursTiers == null` as "no tier ladder" and blocked every row claiming a window — and that null is what the extended-hours switch produces, false on every company. The ladder and the switch are two facts now (`leaveCreditOfferForEmployment` → `{ tiers, ordinaryDayAllowed }`), and the switch governs exactly one thing: whether an ORDINARY day can earn a credit.

- `claimsTimeWindow` returns true for every type, old rule quoted. What still varies has its own name: `flooredByScheduledShiftEnd`, true for a workday only — and it is decided by the DAY TYPE, not by whether the roster happens to hold a shift end, because a roster can carry one on a rest day and the floor would then eat the first hours of the claim.
- `sourceTypeForDayType` now tests the day type DIRECTLY. Leaving it keyed on `claimsTimeWindow` would have routed rest-day claims into `accrueExtendedWorkdayToilTx`, which refuses any day whose kind is not `workday` and banks `workedDayKind: 'workday'` regardless.
- `days` is GONE from the posted row (removed, not left optional); the declared 1-or-0.5 shape REMAINS for the HR-side callers that post it.

### A DEVIATION FROM THE LETTER OF THE RULE, OWED TO THE REPORTER

"If Extended End is earlier than Extended Start, display an error" is **not** implemented as written: an end before a start is how a shift across midnight is entered, and r353 fixed a money bug to make that roll to the following day. Refusing it would delete the night-shift claim this item exists to enable. An EMPTY window is refused instead. **This must be said on the item.**

### THE SUITE CAUGHT ME ASSUMING TIMES MEAN A WINDOW

An Hour-unit Section A claim has carried `fromTime`/`toTime` since long before this round — `ReplacementClaimLineView`'s own header says so — and reading those as r358 windows refused three existing behaviours. A window line is a DAY-unit line with times and no declared figure.

### NOT DONE

- `app/leave/credit/actions.ts` still reads `formData.getAll('days')` and assigns `days` on the row. It is INERT — the form emits no such input and nothing reads `row.days` — but it is dead code left by this round's own cleanup, and it survived `tsc` through the same excess-property blind spot in `.map()` that hid `workedDayKind` earlier in the build. Being removed in r360.
- The Day Type cell is still an editable dropdown offering a choice the server always refuses, and `dayFactsAction` has no `.catch()` so a failed lookup leaves the row blank forever. Both found while re-planning `cbfa8b0b`; both are r360.

## r357 (2026-09-29) — the command the last round had to do by hand. `main@5b653e47`, **no migration**.

### A ROUND THAT CLOSES NO BOARD ITEM IS A REAL CASE, AND IT HAD NO COMMAND

r356 fixed three defects found by reading rather than reported, so there was no item to hand `releaseBuiltItem` — which takes one, and marks it deployed. It was shipped by typing the rsync and the detached launch out by hand over ssh. That worked, and cost two things worth not paying again:

- **The ANNOUNCE step was forgotten.** `buildPendingCommand` writes the ref to the box BEFORE a byte moves, and `deploy-state.sh` copies it into its record. Without it the box recorded `built_ref=unknown`, so its own `stale_build` check lost the sha it compares against. It still reported `stale_build=0` correctly — `ref` and `built_ref` were both `unknown`, so they matched — and arrival was proved instead by the §3 dry-run, which compares files rather than labels and is the stronger evidence. What was lost is the box's ability to NAME what it is running.
- **`rsync --delete` against production was retyped from memory.** That is the shape `scripts/improve/` exists to remove: one mistyped `--exclude` deletes files on the server.

Steps 1-4 of a release — final gate, announce, rsync, detached `deploy.sh`, poll — are now `deployWorktree({ worktree })`, and `releaseBuiltItem` is that plus the board write. `pnpm improve:deploy <worktree>` exposes it. CLAUDE.md §7 and §9 record it, and **this round shipped through it**, which is the only test of a deploy command that means anything.

### THE GUARD IS ABOUT DRIFT, NOT ABOUT THE HAPPY PATH

`test/r291-detached-deploy.test.ts` owns this area and now pins that the two paths are ONE: `releaseBuiltItem` must ship THROUGH `deployWorktree` and keep no rsync, launch or follow of its own; the shared path must still perform all four steps; and the announce must come BEFORE the rsync — the step the hand-rolled deploy forgot is now inside the path a no-item deploy takes. Two copies of an `rsync --delete` is how the board path and the no-board path come to differ in which excludes they carry. NON-VACUITY: giving `releaseBuiltItem` its own `run('rsync', …)` back fails with "release ships through the shared path".

### NOT DONE

- **`fda53352` and `70294f7a` both need the reporter**, not a build: an approval and an answer respectively. Nothing on the board is buildable.
- **No production read was possible in this session.** The local tooling refuses a read-only `psql` SELECT on the box, which is why `fda53352`'s Employee A was diagnosed from code alone. The request stands.

## r356 (2026-09-29) — a second opinion about the kernel's own arithmetic, and two guards that were watching dead files. `main@a95f1445`, **no migration**.

### THE MULTICYCLE WORKSHEET WAS RE-DERIVING THE PCB ACCUMULATORS, AND HAD FALLEN BEHIND THREE TIMES

`core/payroll.ts` replays the year's earlier payslips into Y, Σ(Y−K), K, X, Z and ∑LP to feed the month it is paying. `localization/my/multicycle-worksheet.ts` `loadPriorAccumulators` replayed the same six to MODEL an already-paid month. Two implementations of one arithmetic, and the copy was behind on all three of the changes made to the original:

- **∑LP seeded from a hard `0`** where the kernel seeds from `tp3_lp`. That is item `20837372`'s defect verbatim — ∑LP is the fourth variable a TP3 feeds (spec printed p.22) and it is SUBTRACTED inside P — still live in the copy a round after being fixed in the kernel. The column was never even SELECTed here.
- **Z summed `zakat` without `zakatRebateTp1`** (r352 / `72d1a390`).
- **Σ(Y−K) folded `payslip.gross_pay`** after the kernel moved onto the stamped `bases.pcb` (r354 / `4011903e`) — the difference being every ringgit that is tax-exempt, docked as unpaid leave, or deducted before tax.

**Why that is worse here than a cosmetic divergence.** These accumulators are fed straight into `statutory(...)`, and the whole worksheet IS the comparison between what that models and what the payslips actually paid. An inflated Σ(Y−K) moves the modelled PCB, both readings then fail to match, and a correctly computed month prints `unexplained` — "paid matches neither reading" — on the document ADR-0024 asks an accountant to sign. The figures were right; the second opinion about them was wrong.

**The fix is one seed and one fold, owned by the pack**: `openingAccumulatorsFromTp3` and `foldPriorSlipIntoAccumulators`, beside `PcbAccumulators`, which is the pack's own type. The kernel reaches both through the pack seam and still names no jurisdiction; the worksheet imports them directly. The kernel's side-maps (`lpFedByEmp`, `rebateFedByEmp`, `exemptionUsed`) deliberately stay in the kernel: they answer what THIS employer has fed, which the worksheet must not see. `openingAccumulatorsFromTp3` returns `Required<PcbAccumulators>` so the kernel's stricter `Acc` needs no cast — a cast there would silence the one check protecting that shape.

**Same family, also fixed:** the worksheet's `zakat_or_lp_present` refusal tested `zakat !== 0 || lp !== 0`, so a month whose ONLY offset was a TP1 rebate walked past it and was then modelled with no offset at all — the very thing the refusal exists to prevent, reachable since r352.

**NON-VACUITY, and the obvious method does not work.** Reverting the shared fold leaves both sides agreeing, because the kernel writes the payslips through the same function the worksheet replays them with. Four unit cases fail on a revert by name; the two database cases need the worksheet's OWN copy restored, and then both fail with `expected 'unexplained' not to be 'unexplained'`. The test file records that so the next verifier does not repeat the first attempt.

### TWO GUARDS WERE READING FILES NOTHING RENDERS

`<SharedLeaveGroupCards>` has had no render site since r302 folded both group placements into the one dashboard grid — and `test/shared-leave-group-display.test.ts` says so itself, asserting `leavePage.match(/<SharedLeaveGroupCards/g)` is empty. Two cases in that same file were nevertheless reading the dead component for the invariants the item exists to protect: "prints the pooled figure through the shared day formatter, never a private toFixed" and "the ceiling is printed BESIDE the figure, never in place of it". Green over markup no screen uses, while the live tile went unguarded.

The component is deleted, `shared-leave-group-cards.tsx` becomes `shared-leave-group-entry.ts` (the name stopped being true at r302, and a `.tsx` with no JSX is its own small lie), and the two cases are re-pointed at `my-leave-dashboard.tsx` with the old claims quoted. One half **cannot** transfer: "server-safe, not `'use client'`" was true of the dead file and is false of the live tile, which sits inside a client island — so what it protected is asserted directly instead, that the labels arrive pre-translated as fields of the entry and the tile resolves none itself. Swapping `{formatDays(g.available)}` for `{g.limitLabel}` in the live tile — the exact overpromise `46afcc48` exists to prevent — now fails; against the old file it stayed green.

### THE COLUMN COUNT IN A SCREEN'S COMMENTS HAD OUTLIVED THREE ROUNDS

`app/leave/employee-balances/page.tsx` kept a running tally in prose — "a screen that already carries thirteen columns", "now a thirteen-column one", "thirteen columns already overflow this table" — while the table has had **sixteen** since r355 added Available Balance. `026e16b9`'s own measurement (eleven columns, the last 23px of the header) is history and stays exactly as written; what was corrected is the sentences asserting a CURRENT count. One annotation now records the count once, measured rather than incremented, and says why a tally is the wrong thing to keep: it is wrong the moment someone forgets it, and silently.

### DECISIONS THIS ROUND MAKES THAT NO TICKET SETTLED

- **A derivation the kernel owns is not copied into a pack module; it is moved INTO the pack and called from both.** `PcbAccumulators` is the pack's type, so its fold belongs beside it, on the seam. Both old regexes are quoted with the reason they moved.

### `77e882f5` — THE TICK IS CONSENT, NOT AN OVERRIDE, AND IT MOVES MONEY

The owner reversed item `6c635212`'s precedence in their own words: the checkbox states an intention to claim and must not override the statutory eligibility validation. The ladder is now tick → date of birth → age → applicable relief condition. A ticked child over 18 carrying no qualifying category stops counting — the outcome the reporter asked for twice, on a child born 2004 whose category reads `under_18`.

`childReliefCategory` therefore stops being a pricing field and becomes an eligibility input. Which categories justify a claim past 18 was read off the catalogue rather than inferred from the price: `study_preu` is defined in this repo as "18+ in full-time pre-university study", so it is in the set with `study_tertiary`, `disabled` and `disabled_study`; `under_18` is the only one that asserts the opposite and so the only one excluded.

**That reading now has primary-source footing it did not have when it shipped.** LHDN's PCB 2026 specification, printed page 26, allows RM2,000 "per child … if the child is unmarried, 18 years of age and above, and is receiving full-time education" — pre-university study at 18+ is inside that sentence. The build note had flagged `study_preu` as UNKNOWN and told the builder to resolve it against the spec; the builder resolved it from the catalogue instead and reached the same answer.

Two things deliberately unchanged, both asserted: an explicit `false` still refuses at any age, and a NULL tick keeps the pre-r355 inference. Null is most legacy rows, and reading it as "not claimed" would drop every never-ticked child out of relief in one nightly resync — a mass relief loss from a rule nobody asked for.

The pooled figure prints, and the Explain panel says why the row's three cells do not reach it.

`leaveBalances().available` is now rounded at the point of computation, as its twin in `core/leave.ts` already was: `0.30 − 0.10` is 0.19999999999999998.

## r354 (2026-09-28) — the accumulated figure was right to distrust, and wrong about why. `main@026d7d9e`, **no migration**.

Closed: `4011903e`. Gate: **1047 files — equal to the suite file count**, 16 chunks, `tsc` 0, `next build` 0. No `gate:shadow`: `db/` untouched, watermark unchanged at `max(idx)=489`.

### THE REPORTER FOUND A REAL DEFECT AND NAMED A CAUSE THAT CANNOT EXIST

They reported October's Σ(Y−K) RM1,500 too high and attributed it to July/August/September's TP1 relief being deducted again. Both halves of that are refuted, and both refutations are now pinned:

- **LP never enters Σ(Y−K).** It is a separate subtrahend inside P; the replay adds it to `acc.lpAccumulated` alone.
- **The sign is wrong.** Relief is SUBTRACTED, so applying it twice makes tax LOWER. Their symptom is an over-deduction.

The figure they pointed at was nevertheless wrong.

### WHAT WAS ACTUALLY WRONG

`core/payroll.ts` accumulated `payslip.gross_pay` per prior month. PCB is charged on `statutory.bases.pcb`:

    bases.pcb = max(0, wagesExOt + statOvertime − pcbWageDeduction) + statAdditional
    grossPay  = basic + allowanceApplied + reimburse + otConvertAmount + overtime + bonus

Three kinds of money sit in the second and are deliberately absent from the first **in the month they are paid**: tax-exempt allowances (carved into `reimburse` by the exemption ledger), unpaid leave (subtracted from `wagesExOt`, never from gross, because it is a deduction LINE), and any pay item configured to come off before tax.

So every prior month inflated Σ(Y−K), P came out too high, and the employee was **over-deducted** — the direction reported. It contradicts the specification this repo took delivery of in r352: rule 9, printed p.20, *"All the tax exemption ... shall be EXCLUDED FROM THE REMUNERATION for MTD purposes."*

### Y IS WRITTEN DOWN, AND THE GUARD THAT FORBADE IT IS INVERTED RATHER THAN DELETED

LHDN's Y was never stored, so the worksheet printed a labelled *"not recorded separately"* row and `test/7f251381` refused any row equal to `Σ(Y−K) + K`. That was right: the sum is arithmetically Y, and printing it would have been a figure this system never produced.

The same replay now accumulates Y over the same per-month figure, so **Y − K = Σ(Y−K) by construction**. The old value-sweep could not survive that — a correctly stamped Y *equals* the sum — so the protection moved from the VALUE to the SOURCE: Y prints only when the engine stamped one, and a slip predating this item still says the figure is not recorded. The old claim is kept as that fallback case.

### TWO FAULTS IN MY OWN WORK, CAUGHT BEFORE THEY SHIPPED

- **The Y seed was wrong.** `tp3_epf_claimed` holds the CLAIMED EPF; `tp3_net` was computed with `min(claimed, cap)`. Seeding Y from the uncapped column would have broken `Y − K = Σ(Y−K)` for anyone over the cap — silently, on the one screen whose purpose is to reconcile those two numbers. Both seeds now derive from one capped value.
- **My first test was vacuous.** On a plain salary gross and the PCB base are EQUAL, so every assertion passed with the fix reverted. The money assertion moved onto `test/pcb-classification.test.ts`'s exempt-allowance fixture — the only place in the suite where the two genuinely differ. Reverting now fails with `expected 12000 to be close to 9000`, and the RM3,000 gap is exactly the exempt total the same test already asserts.
- **And a third, in the test itself:** I first inserted the March run BEFORE the EA assertions, which were written for two months; the RM3,000 cap is spent by February, so March's whole allowance is taxable and B.1(c) became 3,000 against the 1,000 those lines pin. Order is what keeps both claims true, and the file now says so.

### THE FALLBACK IS COUNTED, NOT SILENT

`bases` has been stamped since r187. A slip older than that has none, and `grossPay` remains the only figure available for it — a DIFFERENT number, not a rounding difference. `acc.legacyBaseSlips` counts them and the snapshot carries the count, so a figure nobody can account for is disclosed rather than absorbed.

### NOT DONE

- **The three other points of `4011903e`'s plan.** The Y row now prints, but the PCB-detail screen's TP1 schedule still re-derives from TODAY's declarations (`app/payroll/pcb-detail/slip-data.ts:215-235`), printing the declared annual beside an `LP1` of 0.00 — which is very likely what the reporter read as "applied again". That is point 4 and it is unbuilt. Two further re-derivations on the same screen (`currentPcbReliefs`, `previousEmploymentForPayslip` reading LIVE `tp3_*`) are disclosed in-code and untouched.
- **`localization/my/multicycle-worksheet.ts` still misses `zakatRebateTp1`** — a divergence **r352 introduced** and r354 did not fix.
- **No production verification.** We never obtained Employee A's records, so which of four candidate causes produced their specific RM1,500 is UNKNOWN. This fix addresses one of them; the plan asked for the records and the request stands.
- Five items are planned and unbuilt: `d323c224`, `70294f7a`, `4c63b37e`, `8d3a7bff`, and the remainder of `4011903e`.

### THE MACHINE, AND WHY THE FIRST GATE ATTEMPT WAS RED

16 failed files on the first run: **one real, fifteen environmental**, and separating them was the work.

The real one was `test/00e28308`, an exact-shape `toEqual` over the whole stored payslip payload. `ytdGross` legitimately joined it, which is precisely what that guard exists to force someone to notice.

The other fifteen were hook timeouts, and the cause is structural rather than random: **the gate rebuilds the cluster per chunk, and each rebuild queues a background `rm -rf` of the one it moved aside.** Sixteen chunks queue sixteen drains, and they accumulate ACROSS ROUNDS — 19 had built up over r352–r354, 56G, of which **52G was `pg_wal`**. With this box's endpoint-security agent inspecting every unlink, `apfsd` and CoreServices went hot too and load hit 15.79/31.56. Chunk 1 took **2164s**.

§5's remedy, applied: clear the `pg_wal` directories inside the moved-aside clusters first (the data directories are what the slow drain is for). **56G → 3.3G in 5 seconds, load 15.79 → 1.57, chunk 1 2164s → 79s — a 27× speedup.** The live cluster is a symlink to the RAM disk and matched none of the 19 targets, which was checked before anything was deleted.

**Worth a standing note:** a gate leaves 16 moved-aside clusters behind. Sweeping their `pg_wal` before a gate, not after a problem, would have avoided this entirely.
## r353 (2026-09-28) — four items, and three of my own instructions were wrong. `main@373cd3af`, **no migration**.

Closed: `cbfa8b0b`, `fda53352`, `15e5bd93`, `77e882f5`. Gate: **1046 files — equal to the suite file count**, 16 chunks, `tsc` 0, `next build` 0. No `gate:shadow`: `db/` untouched, watermark unchanged at `max(idx)=489`.

### THE ROUND'S REAL FINDING: THREE BRIEFS OF MINE WERE WRONG AND THE AGENTS REFUSED THEM

Each was refused with evidence, and each refusal was correct. Recorded here because the pattern matters more than any one feature.

1. **The `auto_table` sync gate would have moved real tax.** My `fda53352` brief said "extend the sync gate to 'auto_table' (its grid already derives)". It does not. `core/dependents.ts:569` gates on `!== 'auto'` and `:636` writes `childReliefMode: 'auto'` **hardcoded**, alongside `childReliefTable: state.grid` — null when a category is missing. Widening it would have replaced every `auto_table` employee's DECLARED grid with the register's and flipped their mode, on the rail built to prevent exactly that. For a disabled child in higher education: RM16,000 → RM2,000. Built as a READ instead (`childReliefTableHeadCount`, `core/dependents.ts` untouched). **I verified the refusal in the source before accepting it.**

2. **A false justification in my brief would have hidden a bug.** I told the `15e5bd93` builder to keep r352's `EmployeeSearchField` fix "because the personnel tab-save guards depend on it." They grepped: the dom file about to be retired was the **only** test in the repo exercising `hiddenInputIsUserFacing` / `controlDisplay`. Deleting it on my say-so would have left r352's silent-data-loss fix as untested code behind a green suite. They tested both functions directly instead.

3. **`cbfa8b0b` item 7 was half wrong**, and the builder said so: on rest/off/PH rows the time cells genuinely are disabled, so "it still says they do not ask for hours" was TRUE. What was stale was the sentence's account of how an ordinary day's credit is derived.

### `cbfa8b0b` — THE ENTERED WINDOW IS THE CLAIM, AND THE SAFETY MOVED TO THE APPROVER

The clock-out clip and the measured cap are gone from `lib/extended-hours.ts`; the shift-end floor and cross-midnight roll stay. `eligibleExtendedMinutes` is now a projection of one `assessExtendedClaim`, so the figure and the approver's warning cannot disagree. `measuredExtendedMinutes` was dropped from the signature, which is what caught all four stale call sites at compile time.

**A money bug found outside the brief and hand-fixed:** the cross-midnight roll tested `<=`, so `claimEnd === claimStart` rolled to +1440 — **a full day's credit from an obvious mis-entry**. Masked by the measured cap; removing the cap exposed it. Verified by execution, pinned.

**RESIDUAL HOLE, STATED NOT HIDDEN:** `actualClockOut` is a time with no date, so a clock-out *earlier* than the claimed start reads as next-day. Someone who left at 17:00 and claims 18:00–23:51 gets the credit and no warning. Every alternative traced broke the ordinary evening-shift case. Needs a dated clock-out from the attendance engine.

**THE RULE MY PLAN DROPPED.** Their contest listed four business rules "do not change"; the plan carried three. The missing one: *"Rest day / off day / public holiday use the same time fields."* Their point 8 was pointing at it and I read it as a wording fix. They approved a plan that had silently lost one of their own rules. Raised as its own item with the money consequence named (a 2-hour rest-day claim goes from 1 day to nothing under their 240-minute rule).

### `fda53352` — SECTION B CARRIES THE TAXABLE EXCESS ONLY

`eaStatement` now derives `taxableAllowances = allowances − exemptAllowances`. The annual cap is NOT re-derived: `roomFor()` already applied it, so the over-limit remainder is already in `allowanceApplied`. The exempt total was being printed **twice** on one form — inside 1(c) and again in Section F. Non-vacuity re-derived **by me, not just reported**: reverting the subtraction fails by exactly RM3,000, the exempt slice.

The HTML statement read the exempt figure three times on one screen; now once, in Section F. `notTracked` and `exemptAllowances` retired in place.

**Geometry, measured rather than eyeballed — and two of the reporter's premises were inverted.** Section A's pitch was 14.5pt against the agency's 13.8, i.e. already *wider*; the genuinely tight gap was our section square sitting 0.6pt under the banner where the agency leaves 4.0. The officer box has five 13.2pt rows = **two** writing lines, so the plan's "two lines to three" is not on the form; the real defect was `fitSize` flooring at 1pt and shrinking a four-part address to ~6pt. `scripts/measure-ea-official-pdf.ts` is **committed this time** — r349's was written and never committed, which is why r351 was still guessing.

`captionWithInlineRule` now THROWS if a caller's `ruleTo` would put the `')'` past `moneyLeft`, so r351's overprint cannot return by someone re-typing a literal.

### `15e5bd93` — A DEDICATED SCREEN, AFTER WE BUILT THE WRONG SHAPE THIS MORNING

r352 shipped a rail + workspace inside the tab; they contested it and asked for a dedicated screen with view/edit modes, which their original text had already said. The route is `/admin/organization/[companyId]/statutory`, added to `SCREENS` (the trap `test/function-access.test.ts` exists to catch). Per-card `viewing | editing`, one at a time, posting to the existing action. `statutory-tab-actions.ts` and `company-statutory-tab-sections.ts` deleted rather than orphaned.

Read off production: the one non-archived child is born 2004-01-01, not a student, **`child_tax_relief` TRUE**, category `under_18`. ## r352 (2026-09-28) — five items, and the specification this platform cites was never in the building. `main@0724f2f2`, **no migration**.

Closed: `b25e421e`, `04b88724`, `0df7dd44`, `15e5bd93`, `72d1a390`. Gate: **1043 files — equal to the suite file count**, 16 chunks, `tsc` 0, `next build` 0. No `gate:shadow`: `db/` untouched, watermark unchanged at `max(idx)=489`.

### THE DOCUMENT

`docs/forms/pcb-spec-2026-computerised-calculation.pdf` is now in the repo, 52 pages, with rules 5, 9 and 15 transcribed verbatim into `docs/forms/pcb-spec-2026-extracts.txt`. So are the **Form TP1 2026 explanatory notes** and the TP1 form — r350's entry records the TP1/TP3 notes as unobtainable because their URLs 404.

**They 404 because the repo cites the wrong path.** Every `/media/<hash>/` URL in this tree is dead; the live one is `https://www.hasil.gov.my/wp-content/uploads/<name>.pdf`, indexed from `.../majikan/jadual-pcb-dan-spesifikasi-data/`. Four rounds have now reasoned around a document that was one working URL away. `STATUTORY-SOURCES.md` records the retrieval and says to cite the local copy, never a URL.

### `72d1a390` — WE WERE HALF RIGHT, AND THE HALF WE HAD WRONG WAS OURS

We raised this ourselves claiming rule 5 deducts both zakat and the departure levy AND carries any unused part forward.

**Confirmed:** rule 5 (p.19) is headed *"Zakat and departure levy shall be treated as follows"* and its column (b) is *"Zakat and departure levy for current month"*. The Umrah levy on TP1 D1(b) offsets tax exactly as zakat does, and offset nothing — an over-deduction for everyone who claimed it.

**Refuted, and it was our own sentence:** column (d), headed *"carried forward to the following month (value of Z)"*, equals column (b) in **every printed row** — MTD 15.00, zakat 8.00, net 7.00, **(d) 8.00**. It is the Z accumulator taking the full amount, which the kernel already did. There is no residual ledger to build, and a test pins that the remainder is dropped.

**Rule 15 decided the shape and contradicted our own plan.** We had promised to show the figure on the payslip; the spec says a TP1-claimed amount *"should not appear in the payslip and EA Form"* while still being *"treated as zakat for current month"*. So it is a second term beside `effectiveZakat`, stamped as `statutory.zakatRebateTp1`, never folded into the payslip's zakat line, and deliberately not a `DELTA_KEY`.

**FED AS A DELTA, AND THE FIRST CUT HAD THIS WRONG.** Reading only the row whose deduction month is this month loses money outright: a claim FOR March approved in August is in force from August, March is paid, and it lands in neither. A unit case caught it. `tp1RebateInForce` is a running total and the caller feeds `max(0, inForce − alreadyOffset)` replaying its own payslips — `resolveTp1Feed`'s shape for Section C.

Rule 9 also arrived: *"All the tax exemption ... shall be EXCLUDED FROM THE REMUNERATION ... Any amount exceed the restricted amount shall be taxable."* That is the rule `fda53352` point 3 turns on, now quotable from the primary source instead of from a round entry.

### `b25e421e` + `04b88724` — A BIRTHDAY NOW REACHES THE PAYSLIP, AND THE AGE RULE WAS WRONG ON THE DAY

`num_children` / `child_relief_table` are a cached projection whose correct value depends on the CLOCK, invalidated only by writes. `scripts/resync-child-relief-grid.ts` already existed, already called the single author with all four rails, and was simply never scheduled. Now at 01:15 in the crontab, documented in `deploy/DEPLOY.md`, with the property that makes scheduling sufficient pinned in a test (a cron line lives on the box; no test can see it).

**Found while pinning it:** `childAgeYears` computed `floor(elapsed / 365.25 days)` and answered **SEVENTEEN to a child on their eighteenth birthday** — 2008-06-15 to 2026-06-15 is 6,574 days and 18 × 365.25 is 6,574.5. `isChildReliefEligible` tests `age < 18`, so an ineligible child stayed in the PCB relief for up to an extra day, by an amount that depended on how many 29-Februaries fell in the span. `lib/completed-years.ts` already had calendar-accurate math and its header **already asked future age consumers to reuse it**; this was the reinvention it warned about, and `family-form-dialog.tsx` held a third copy. Money-affecting, outside the approved scope, hand-fixed.

### `15e5bd93` — TWO DEFECTS THAT WOULD HAVE SHIPPED GREEN

Rail + workspace + one Save, per the approved mockup. Both defects were invisible to source scan, `tsc` and a static render:

- **The pack flag would have been poisoned.** Every body editor carries a visible `country` (postal address), so `syncCarriedValues` would have overwritten the identity card's hidden `country="MY"` with `"Malaysia"` → *"No statutory pack for Malaysia"* on every identity save. Fixed by the `filingCountry` rename r226 already coined one file over.
- **A signatory-only edit was silently discarded** — `diffTab` skips a hidden input it cannot prove is user-facing, and `EmployeeSearchField` posts through one.

**DEVIATION FROM THE APPROVED MOCKUP, recorded because the reporter approved a picture:** the rail keeps the 3783fd87 summary (employer number + paying account) and is 288px rather than the sketch's 260px. Removing it would regress an item the same reporter approved in r327 — the promise there was that you can read what is set on *every* body at once, and the workspace shows one at a time. Their most likely objection.

### `0df7dd44` — THE MESSAGE EXISTED AND WAS WRITTEN TO THE WRONG SCREEN

Not a missing message: a `redirect()` to the TP1 **list**, while the **form** has a working `ErrorBanner` no action ever targeted — so a 40-box form was lost on every refusal, and five of six locales showed English. Now `useActionState` on the form, six locales, and the box clamps to `limit − alreadyApproved`.

**The clamp target is the load-bearing decision.** Clamping to the annual limit would over-claim for every employee with a prior claim this year — a worse fault than the reported one. Fixtures carry a prior approved claim so `limit` and `remaining` differ.

**A controlled checkbox is not restored by React after a form action resolves** (a controlled `value` is; `checked` is not — the element is referentially identical so nothing re-commits it). A refused Submit silently cleared the Section E declaration and the next press was refused *for the tick*.

### TOOLING

`scripts/gate-chunked.sh` gained `CHUNK_FROM`/`CHUNK_TO`. §4 says the reliable workflow here is chunks in the FOREGROUND, and a foreground call is time-bounded, so a 16-chunk gate could not use it. A slice prints `SLICE GREEN … THIS IS NOT A GATE`, because the one thing a reader must never do is read a green slice as a green gate.

**The first gate attempt was red and it was the environment.** 14 `Hook timed out in 30000ms`, 3 TRUNCATE deadlocks, **zero AssertionErrors** — `vitest.config.ts:8` defaults to `availableParallelism() − 2`, so 12 cores gave 10 workers on a cluster that takes 4. Re-run at `VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=4`. Also: that run was piped through `tail`, so its completion notification read **exit 0** while chunk 1 was red — §4's own warning, demonstrated.

### NOT DONE

- **`cbfa8b0b`** (leave credit) and **`fda53352`** (EA form) are planned, not built.
- **`fda53352` point 3 is now provable and unbuilt**: Section B's own heading in our transcription reads *"EXCLUDING Tax Exempt Allowances"*, we print that caption and put the exempt money under it, and the same money is printed again in Section F. `B1(c) = allowances − exemptAllowances`.
- **The EA's A.8 count**: correct on `'auto'`, unenforced on `'manual'`, and **never synced on `'auto_table'`** — the gate is `!== 'auto'`, so a mode whose name promises derivation keeps a hand-keyed count beside a correct s.48 grid.
- **The `')'` on EA lines 1(c), 3 and 4 overprints the money column** — drawn at `ruleTo + 2 = 483` where `moneyLeft` is 482.3. Unguarded.
- ~~The nightly resync has not run on the box yet~~ **DONE**: installed at 01:15 in the crontab and run on
  production. 4 employees on `auto` across 2 tenants, **all four `unchanged`, 0 payroll alerts** — the
  stored figures already agreed with the register, so no tax moved. ⚠️ Two things learned doing it:
  `--dry-run` does NOT compute a delta (it lists who would be examined and counts everyone `unchanged`),
  so the preview the plan promised the reporter is weaker than described — the before/after must be read
  off the columns. And the crontab routes every job through `deploy/cron-alert.sh` since r295 while
  `DEPLOY.md` still documented the plain `>> log 2>&1` form; the line was installed in the wrapper form
  and `DEPLOY.md` corrected. `crontab -l` is the truth, again.
- Discard on the TP1 month form has never worked (`id: ''` → invalid uuid); left byte-identical.
- Two dirty `TabSaveScope`s on one screen open two unsaved-changes dialogs. Pre-existing shape (personnel mounts five).
## r351 (2026-09-28) — four statutory items in one gate, and the gate earned its keep. `main@cc2f165c`, **migration 0489**.

Closed: `1785b766`, `ad7bc503`, `fda53352`, `04b88724` (screen half — see below). Gate: **1037 files — equal to the suite file count**, 16 chunks, GREEN FIRST PASS on the final tree, `tsc` 0, `next build` 0, `gate:shadow` **PASS 402/402**.

### HOW IT WAS BUILT, AND THE CONSTRAINT THAT SHAPED IT

Three agents plus the parent, in four worktrees, concurrently — and **none of them could run a single test**, because a full gate held the shared cluster and `scripts/gate-chunked.sh` does not take a `testlock.sh` slot. So four branches arrived typechecked, `next build`-clean, and never executed. Every defect below is one that only running them could find, and there were four.

### `1785b766` — THE EXEMPTION IS THE EMPLOYEE'S FOR THE YEAR, NOT EACH EMPLOYER'S

`core/payroll.ts` computed per-code headroom as `cap − priorUsed − used`, and `priorUsed` was replayed from **this employer's** payslips only. A joiner who had already spent the RM6,000 travel exemption elsewhere arrived with a full RM6,000 again. The TP3's Section C now seeds that ledger through a new `tp3_exemption_used` projection (migration **0489**, allocated from `max(idx)=488`, never from `entries.length=401`).

**It also removed a duplicate source of truth**: `MY_TP3_2026_SECTION_C` carried its own copies of 6,000 / 3,000 / 2,000, the same three numbers `MY_PCB_EXEMPTION_CODES` owns. The TP3 limits are now derived from the mapped code and a test pins the equality.

**Idempotence is by construction, and the code says so**: one row per person-year, derived and rewritten whole, never appended. The reporter's points about amendment, reprocessing and cancellation need no mechanism.

### `ad7bc503` — THE AGENCY PRINTS ONE P FORMULA, AND WE PRINTED OUR OWN

Read off the specification: the P formula appears **seven times, always identically**, always carrying `(Yₜ − Kₜ)`, and the worked examples print *"Where (Yt – Kt ) = 0"* beneath it. Step 1 is lettered `[A]`–`[E]` **by the document**. The glossary defines `Q` and `C` separately while the formula prints `QC` — so r340's note was half right and the reporter was right: our figure already holds the product.

`(Yₜ − Kₜ)` is now always shown — **and the guard it reverses was substantively right**: in a bonus month the correct EPF term is `K₂ₜ`, not `K₂`, so the zero limb is rendered from figures, not from `trace.Yt`, and the bonus still reaches the page only through P₂.

**A live defect found by reading the PDF back**: `safe()` mapped anything outside WinAnsi to `?`, so every downloaded statutory explanation printed `?(Y - K)` and `?LP`. There was **no PDF content test at all**; there is one now, and it restates the old fold to prove itself non-vacuous.

### `fda53352` — THE REPORTER'S OWN HANDWRITING, READABLE FOR THE FIRST TIME

`pnpm improve:attachments` (shipped in r350) made their marked-up comparison readable. On it, in their hand: **"Remove this part from the EA Form"**, red-boxing the strip. That **reverses r349**, whose own plan had offered exactly that option. The printed C.P.8A now ends at the officer's box.

- **The EIS figure is on NO printed EA.** That was the cost `da4fc817` and r349 declined to pay; the owner has now paid it. It stays on the HTML statement.
- **The amended marker STAYS.** Not in the red box, not in the approved plan, and different in kind: it discloses that HR overwrote a figure on a tax document.
- **D.6 carries the ringgit.** We never printed a count there — we printed nothing. The count they were reading is A.8, a different box that is correct as a count. D.6 is now `pcbMeta.reliefs.children`, the kernel's own annual s.48-weighted figure, already on the slips `eaStatement` selects. **The LAST month's**, not the sum — the relief is annual and restated monthly, so summing twelve prints twelve times the relief — **which required an ORDER BY**, because §8 forbids reading "the last" off an unordered query.

### `04b88724` — THE SCREEN HALF ONLY, AND THE PLAN PROMISED BOTH

The card now shows what the Family register supports and **names the payslip's figure in amber beside it** whenever they differ. The eight-hour KL/UTC mismatch is closed. The false *"No children are recorded in the Family register"* is replaced. A child with no date of birth is named.

**The payroll kernel is unchanged, and the approved plan said it would follow the register.** The builder declined to move it: three money-path consumers, no test runs available, and this repo already split this exact item once for that reason (r343 the card, r344 the payslip). I accept the split. **`b25e421e` is raised with the correction owed to the reporter at the top of it**, and `scripts/resync-child-relief-grid.ts` already exists and is simply not on cron.

**A WRONG STATUTORY FIGURE WAS LIVE ON SCREEN, unreported and untested**: the guidance badge read *disabled child RM6,000, in higher education RM6,000 plus RM8,000* where HASiL and our own kernel say **RM8,000 and RM16,000** — in all six locales. Verified corrected in what the browser receives.

### WHAT THE GATE CAUGHT THAT NOTHING ELSE DID

Four red chunks on the first pass, three of them **one bug of mine**. D.6's `ORDER BY` landed correctly; the accompanying column insert matched an **earlier, identically-shaped select in a function that does not join `payroll_batch`**, breaking CP39, statutory-forms-scope and slice0.

- **`tsc` passed.** Drizzle accepts a column from an unjoined table and fails only at query-build time — so typecheck, `next build` and 26 files of targeted EA tests were green while CP39 was broken.
- **Those chunks reported ZERO AssertionErrors**, which §4 says normally means the environment. It did not. One file per chunk died on a thrown error — the import/setup signature. **Reading the chunk log instead of trusting the heuristic is what found it.**

The fourth was real and separate: removing the strip orphaned `blankDisclaimer`, the one caption resolved on the blank branch of the label bundle. **r220 had named it in a guard precisely because a key-existence sweep cannot see a deleted branch**, and that guard did its job.

Also caught by running them: a child-relief case still pinned the flat head count and commented that anything more *"would print a figure the payslip denies"* — **that flat figure was the reported defect**. Now pinned as the pair with a non-vacuity assertion that the two must differ. And two defects in the new exemption test, one of which **narrowed the claim the widened `tp3YearMismatch` blocker rests on**: a C2-only form scores zero on the five older money figures only when C1 is also zero.

### GUARDS: FOURTEEN UPDATED, NONE LOOSENED

Every one pinned a decision this round reverses, so each was inverted or re-pointed **with its reasoning written in**. The contract's "every EA field is DRAWN by the PDF" gained ONE explicit exception, `eis`, as a single-member list rather than a relaxed regex — **plus a new case asserting the excepted field is still on the HTML and still amendable**, so the exception cannot become a hole.

### VERIFICATION

TP3 screen, six locales, data planted: `60,000.00 + 1,000.00 − 4,000.00 = 57,000.00`, real translations, 0 intl errors, no retired key visible. Blank EA, both editions: the strip gone in all three of its parts, `5(a)` gone, bare `(a)` present. Guidance figures corrected in the shipped payload.

### NOT DONE

- **`04b88724`'s payroll half** — raised as `b25e421e`. Until it ships, a birthday does not reach the payslip on its own.
- **TP1 zakat and the departure levy are captured and never offset against MTD**, against the specification's own rule 5 — an over-deduction. Raised as `72d1a390`; it needs the levy stamped on the payslip and the Z replay extended, or it creates an opposite error.
- **`fda53352` layout**: B.1's sub-items still read `1(a)`…`1(f)` (the plan over-promised — the agency prints `1.` once, which needs a geometry change); the Section A square and the `)` on B.3/B.4 are unmeasured, because r349's dark-fraction measuring script was never committed, only its method; `EA_FORM.right` is still the tracing's 571.3 where the agency's body edge is 556.6.
