## r350 (2026-09-28) — the TP3's C1 holds only TAXABLE pay, so ΣC2 is added, not subtracted. `main@13d24b37`, **no migration**.

Closed: `20837372`. Gate: **1034 files — equal to the suite file count**, 16 chunks, **15 green on the first pass and chunk 11 green on a re-run**, `tsc` 0, `next build` 0. No `gate:shadow`: `db/` untouched, watermark unchanged at `max(idx)=488`.

### THE REPORTER WAS RIGHT FIVE TIMES AND r348 TOLD THEM THEY WERE NOT

r348's entry is titled *"THE PREMISE WAS FALSE AND THE REPORTER WAS STILL RIGHT"*. The premise was ours. It verified the kernel *"with C1 = 60,000 gross and the allowance inside it"* — an **assumption about what C1 contains, never read off the form** — concluded the arithmetic was correct, and shipped a caption defending it. `localization/my/statutory-tables.ts` had **already written the question down as a live UNKNOWN** and said only `Nota Penerangan Borang TP3 (2026)` could settle it, both of whose URLs 404.

The notes were never needed. **The form settles it**, and the wording is identical in the 2026 and 2023 editions:

    C1  "…termasuk elaun / perkuisit / pemberian / Manfaat YANG DIKENAKAN CUKAI"   ← SUBJECT to tax
    C2  "Jumlah elaun/perkuisit/pemberian/manfaat YANG DIKECUALIKAN CUKAI"         ← EXEMPT from tax

C1 carries **only the taxable items**. The exempt allowances were never in it, so `C1 − ΣC2` removed money that was not there. Every TP3 employee with a C2 figure had their ∑(Y−K) understated by the whole of it, and their **MTD under-deducted every month**.

### FOUR MORE SOURCES, BECAUSE ONE CAPTION IS NOT A FINDING

- the specification's **own worked example**, printed page 21: normal 5,000 + car 800 + meal 300 *(exempt)* + childcare 250 *(exempt)* = 6,350, and *"To determine MTD amount, taxable income as follow: … Total taxable remuneration : RM5,800"*. The exempt items are simply **not in it**;
- printed page 20 item 9: *"MTD is to be deducted from the employee's TAXABLE REMUNERATION ONLY. All the tax exemption … shall be EXCLUDED FROM THE REMUNERATION … Any amount exceed the restricted amount shall be taxable."*;
- Form C.P.8A (EA) Pin. 2023 — Section B is headed *"(EXCLUDING Tax Exempt Allowances / Perquisites / Gifts / Benefits)"* and the exempt total gets its own Section F. **Same architecture on a second prescribed form**;
- our **own** current-employment path (`localization/my/reports.ts:1084-1091`) has always treated the exempt portion as a memo line off the PCB exemption ledger, never a second subtraction. The TP3 path was the only place in the codebase that subtracted it.

### THE ARITHMETIC

    netRemuneration (∑(Y−K)) = C1 + Σ max(C2ₖ − limitₖ, 0) − C3allowable

The within-limit part is genuinely exempt and contributes nothing. The part **above** a limit is taxable and, because C1 holds only taxable pay, is not in C1 either — so it is **added**. The reporter's own two examples are now named assertions with a non-vacuity guard beside them:

    C1 60,000, C2(i) 3,600 (limit 6,000), C3 4,000  →  56,000   (was 52,400)
    C1 60,000, C2(i) 7,000 (limit 6,000), C3 4,000  →  57,000   (was 50,000)

C2(iii) and C2(v) carry no sourced limit, so **no excess can be proven for them and none is asserted** — the screen says "no limit is published" rather than printing 0.00.

### THE PROSE SWEEP FOUND SIX SITES, WHICH IS WHY THE GATE WAS GREEN

CLAUDE.md §8's recurring failure, applied as a checklist before the gate rather than after it. Six places still asserted the old rule: the seed's header, the file header, `tp3ExemptionOverLimits`' comment, the Section C catalogue note, `core/pcb-explain.ts`'s `netRemuneration` doc, and two comments on the TP3 page. **`tp3ExemptionOverLimits`' comment has now been wrong twice in opposite directions and both versions are recorded on it**, because the next reader needs to see that the argument, not the arithmetic, was what kept failing.

The **warning changed with the rule**. It used to end "the FORM was filled wrong". An over-limit box is not a keying error — the previous employer may lawfully pay more than the exempt limit — so `tp3.exemptOverLimit` now names the tax consequence. `totalLessExempt` and `totalExcessNote` are **retired, not deleted**, in all six locales.

### FOUR FIXTURES MOVED, AND EACH SAYS WHY

Every one pinned a decision this round reverses, so each was **updated with its reasoning, never loosened**:

- the negative-accumulator guard: a negative now needs C3 to exceed C1 plus the excess, which is still exactly the shape of a mis-keyed form;
- the "does not add up" refusal, **plus a new non-vacuity case** proving the formerly-refused boxes are now a valid +500 form;
- the non-invertibility pair: it used to coincide via a different *exempt total*; it now coincides via a different *taxable excess* (C1 55,000 with C2(i) 11,000);
- the r342 decision assertion, which now carries **all three** of its values — 46,021 → 53,000 → 58,000 — so the history is readable from the test.

### THE TOOLING THIS ROUND HAD TO BUILD FIRST

`pnpm improve:attachments <feedbackId> [--save <dir>]`. CLAUDE.md §8 makes reading `feedback_attachment` mandatory and **there was no command for it**, so every session hand-rolled an ssh+psql one-liner — unreviewable, and the exact shape a sandbox classifier refuses. Listing and fetching are separate calls: `content` is a bytea holding whole PNGs and docx files and one item carries several MB, so the metadata query must not drag the bytes. It paid for itself immediately on `fda53352`.

### THE GATE, HONESTLY

Chunk 11 failed once with a single AssertionError in `test/r304-approval-template-drawer.dom.test.tsx`
— an approval-drawer DOM test asserting a button re-enables after a rejected save. **Nothing in this
round's diff reaches it** (`grep -c "taxRelief\|tp3" ` on that file returns 0), and it passed both in
isolation and on a full re-run of chunk 11's own 64-file list against a freshly rebuilt cluster (935
tests, 0 AssertionErrors). Recorded as a load-sensitive flake, not a regression — three build agents
were running alongside the gate. It is *not* being called a first-pass green.

### THE RENDER CHECK, WITH THE DATA PLANTED

The Section C block renders only for an employee with a saved form, and the seed plants none — r345 and
r346 both shipped checks that were green because the block never rendered. A form was planted with the
reporter's example 2 (C1 60,000, C2(i) 7,000 over its 6,000 limit, C2(iii) 5,000 with no limit, C3 8,979
over the 4,000 cap) and all six locales read:

    60,000.00  +  1,000.00  −  4,000.00  =  57,000.00

with the exempt note and the no-limit note in **real translations** (not English fallback — the six
payloads differ in size and content), **0 intl errors**, and **no retired key anywhere in the visible
HTML**. Locale comes from the `NEXT_LOCALE` cookie, which is r346's lesson.

### NOT DONE

- **`scripts/resync-tp3-projections.ts` MUST run on the box.** The one production row goes 47,421 (pre-r342) → 52,400 (r342) → **56,000**. `deploy.sh` runs migrations, not scripts, so this round is not finished until it has run and its rows are verified.
- Issued payslips are **not re-cut**. This changes what future runs compute; re-cutting moves money already paid and reported, and that is the reporter's call. Stated in the plan.
- `1785b766`, `04b88724` and `ad7bc503` are approved and **not built**. `fda53352` is planned and awaiting approval.
## r349 (2026-09-27) — the form's own chrome: solid black blocks, white lettering. `main@f1163aed`, **no migration**.

Closed: `fda53352`. Gate: **1034 files — equal to the suite file count**, 16 chunks, first pass, `tsc` 0, `next build` 0. No `gate:shadow`: `db/` untouched.

### WHAT THE REPORTER SENT, AND WHY IT WAS THE RIGHT THING TO SEND

A side-by-side of our page against LHDN's, with red boxes on every difference. Almost all of them were **one thing**: the agency sets its section letters, its banner and its top-right heading as **solid black blocks with white lettering**, and we drew plain text inside an outline. That single treatment is what made our page read as a different document at a glance.

**r346's own round record had already listed exactly this as NOT DONE** — *"the agency's page sets its section letters in filled black boxes … neither was touched"*. They found the list we wrote. A "not done" note is a promise to somebody, and this is the round that pays it.

### MEASURED BEFORE THE BUILD, NOT DURING IT

The measurement was taken and committed **while the item was still awaiting approval** — which is the r346 lesson, where the same plan had asserted "no geometry moves" and was wrong about the money column. Six squares found scanning the agency's whole left margin — one per section A–F and nothing else — all at `x 39.8, width 17.3`; the banner spans its body width.

**The obvious method is wrong, and that is recorded with the numbers.** These blocks contain WHITE TEXT, so a longest-dark-run measure breaks on the letters and under-reports the height — it returned **4.8 pt for a two-line block**. Measuring by dark FRACTION within the block's own window is what works.

### WHAT MOVED

- Six section letters: a filled square at the left margin, white bold letter, title beside it. The letter is **split off the label**, not removed from the catalogues — the form's numbering is part of its wording and `lib/ea-field-register.ts` matches on it.
- The banner: a fill with a white caption, replacing the outlined box.
- The top-right heading: a filled block that **sizes to the edition**. English runs two lines and Malay one; a fixed rectangle leaves the Malay page with a half-empty black box.
- `officerBox.ruleX[0]` **272 → 288**. *"Name and Address of Employer"* ends at 279.9 at Helvetica 8, so the English caption ran **into its own writing line** — the red bar the reporter drew on that box. The Malay caption ends at 260.7 and fit with 11 pt to spare, **which is why it was never seen: the form was only ever read in Malay.**
- The foot strip gets a heavier rule and a line naming it as not part of the official C.P.8A, in all six locales.

### THE DECISION THE PLAN INVITED A REVERSAL ON

The **EIS figure stays.** `da4fc817` established that the official Section E carries exactly two amounts and EIS is not one of them; the figure is real money off the employee's pay and this is their only annual statement, so it lives below the form rather than being dropped. The plan stated that as its one course and explicitly offered to remove the strip outright if the reporter preferred. They approved it as written.

### TWO PARSER BUGS OF MINE, IN THE TEST, WORTH RECORDING

The test asserts the **drawing**, not the source, because white-on-black renders as an **empty black rectangle** if the fill is drawn after the text — and that still returns 200 and still downloads. Writing it found two things about pdf-lib that are not obvious:

- **It does not emit `re`.** A filled rectangle comes out as a `cm` translate plus an `m`/`l`/`h`/`f` path.
- **It writes text as HEX**, `<48656C6C6F> Tj`, not `(Hello) Tj`.

Matching the obvious forms returned nothing — which reads as *"six missing section squares"* on a page that was drawing all six correctly. **A parser that silently finds nothing is worse than no parser**, so the helpers now assert a non-empty result before anything else does.

### SIX GUARDS UPDATED, NOT DELETED

Four sliced `lib/ea-pdf.ts` between `putFit(t.sectionX` markers; one asserted a section heading reaches the page as a single string (it now reaches it as a boxed letter plus a title); one asserted the `if (W.privateStatement2)` branch r349 replaced. **All were caught by sweeping the related tests BEFORE the gate** — the r346 lesson applied, and the reason this round gated green on the first pass.

### THE RENDER CHECK CAUGHT A 500, AND IT WAS THE ENVIRONMENT

The blank EA route returned **500 in all six locales** after a green gate and a green build. `grep` of the dev log: *"No valid dev principal — run `pnpm db:seed`"*. **The chunked gate rebuilds the cluster per chunk, which drops `ai_hr_dev`** — so any render check after a gate must re-seed first. Re-seeded: all six serve a real PDF, 0 intl errors, and the rasterised page shows all six squares, the solid banner, the two-line heading block, clean officer columns and the labelled foot strip.

### NOT DONE

- The remaining geometry constants (Section A's two columns, the JUMLAH rules, `midMoney`) still come from the 150 dpi tracing of a rival vendor's rendering. The agency's own file is on disk and the method is now written down.
- The agency numbers its items `1.` then `(a)` where we set `1(a)`. Visible on a side-by-side, not touched, and not raised by the reporter.

## r348 (2026-09-27) — the figures were right and the sentence said the opposite. `main@b362128f`, **no migration**.

Closed: `20837372`. Gate: **1033 files — equal to the suite file count**, 16 chunks, first pass, `tsc` 0, `next build` 0. No `gate:shadow`: `db/` untouched.

### THE PREMISE WAS FALSE AND THE REPORTER WAS STILL RIGHT

They contested this a **fourth** time, saying the C2 calculation misunderstands the rule. It does not. Verified against the shipped kernel before touching anything, with C1 = 60,000 gross and the allowance inside it:

    keyed 3,600 under a 6,000 limit  →  contributes 0 to netRemuneration
    keyed 7,000 over  a 6,000 limit  →  contributes exactly 1,000
    and the contribution is never negative at any keyed value — no double deduction

That is their own `MAX(keyed − limit, 0)`, reached from the other direction, because C1 is gross and the excess sits in it exactly once.

**The cause was my own copy, shipped in r345.** `taxRelief.tp3.totalCappedNote` read *"RM {counted} **counts towards** Accumulated Net Remuneration"* where `counted` was `exemptTotal + epfAllowable` — the figure **subtracted from** gross to reach it. The two rows above it were labelled "counted", equally ambiguous. The numbers were right and the words described a different system: **the exact one the reporter was telling us not to build.** Anyone reading that screen reaches their conclusion.

### THE FIX

The total is the **sum itself** — gross, less C2, less C3, equals ANR — with explicit minus signs, because a subtraction cannot be read backwards the way a caption can. Every figure is still read **off the seed**; `derived.gross` joins the three already there.

The three misleading keys are **retired, not deleted**, in all six locales. `i18n/request.ts` deep-merges each locale over English, so dropping a key from `en.json` alone would leave the old sentence rendering for a Malay reader — the worst possible half-fix. A test pins that they stay present and marked, and that the page renders none of them.

### THE RECURRING FAILURE, NAMED

This is the **second wording defect on this one screen in two rounds**, and the fourth of its kind this session:

- r342 shipped the C2/C3 capping; `exemptLimitNote` went on saying the keyed figure was "used exactly as it is". Corrected in r345.
- r345 shipped the display; `totalCappedNote` said the exempt amount counts *towards* ANR. Corrected here.
- r344 shipped the weighted child relief; `childQualifyingAutoUnitsNote` went on saying every child counts as one. Corrected in r347.
- r346 traced the EA from a rival vendor's rendering; a comment and a test both *defended* its typo as "the specimen's own spelling".

**Shipping kernel behaviour and leaving prose behind that asserts the old behaviour is the failure mode of this codebase, not the arithmetic.** Every one of these passed `tsc`, the full suite and `next build`. A round that changes what the system does must grep the catalogues and the comments for sentences describing what it used to do.

### THE RENDER CHECK, DONE PROPERLY THIS TIME

The block is behind `derived`, so it renders only for an employee with a saved TP3. The seed plants none, and the first pass reported all four rows **absent in all six locales** — which was the check working, not the code failing. A record was planted with the reporter's own figures and the page re-read:

    en / ms / ta / th / vi / zh  →  60,000.00  −  6,000.00  −  4,000.00  =  50,000.00

the 7,000 capped to 6,000 and the 8,979 capped to 4,000, no retired key on screen, 0 intl errors. **Twice this session a conditional block made a green render check prove nothing** (r345's picker, r346's un-selected employee). Plant the data and read the page.

### NOT DONE

- `fda53352` is planned, not built: the reporter sent a red-boxed comparison showing LHDN sets its section letters and banner as **filled black blocks with white lettering** where we draw plain text — which r346's own record had listed as not done.

## r347 (2026-09-27) — the screen and the payslip disagreed about a weighted child by RM14,000. `main@5842931c`, **no migration**.

Closed: `04b88724`. Gate: **1033 files — equal to the suite file count**, 16 chunks, `tsc` 0, `next build` 0. No `gate:shadow`: `db/` untouched, watermark unchanged at `max(idx)=488`.

### THE DEFECT WAS r344's, WHICH IS MINE

r344 widened three money consumers to price the DERIVED s.48 grid on `'auto'` as well as `'auto_table'` — `core/payroll.ts`, `core/payroll-view.ts`, `localization/my/multicycle-worksheet.ts`. It did **not** widen the fourth, `qualifyingChildBreakdown` in `core/dependents.ts`, which still read `mode === 'auto_table'`.

So an `'auto'` employee whose grid IS derived was relieved at the s.48 weight on their payslip while the Identification & Tax card that **explains** that figure showed the plain head count. Each of the three kernel sites carried its **own copy** of the condition, which is precisely why widening three of four looked finished.

### MEASURED ON PRODUCTION — the answer the reporter is owed

    Daniel Tan, EMP-0002 — mode 'auto', grid STORED
      "Under 18 Child A"  under_18        →  1 unit
      "D Child Study"     disabled_study  →  8 units
      payslip relieves 9 qualifying children = RM18,000   (correct since r344)
      the card was showing 2 qualifying children = RM4,000

**His tax was already right; only the screen was wrong.** Note his child is disabled **and** in qualifying higher education, so **8** units — not the **4** his own example assumed. Also on production: `Aisyah Rahman` EMP-0001 is `'auto'` with **no** grid stored (3 eligible children, 1 categorised) and correctly stays on the head count — she is the case the r345 category-gap list exists to surface.

### THE FIX

One exported predicate, `pricesChildReliefFromGrid`, in `core/dependents.ts` beside the grid it describes. All four consumers read it; none restates it, so a fifth gets it right by construction. The breakdown prices each child through a **one-child grid** run by the same `childReliefFor` the total uses, so the rows provably sum to the total instead of agreeing by coincidence — which is what the reporter asked to see.

r344's completeness gate is **untouched**: a null grid still means "cannot be priced by category yet" and all four fall back to the head count, because `childReliefGridFromFamily` skips a child it cannot classify and a partial grid would relieve *fewer* children than the employee has.

### THREE GUARDS THAT WERE GREEN THROUGH THE DEFECT, AND WHY

This is the part worth reading. All three were well-written, well-reasoned, and could not see it.

- **`a5f21891` (b)/(c)** asserted "all THREE kernel consumers" by grepping each file for its own copy of the literal condition. A fourth consumer was invisible to it by construction.
- **`04b88724` (g)** read the mode literals out of three files and required the three *sets to be equal* — an explicitly-reasoned agreement guard, with a failure message telling a future reader to "find where it went and update this list". It compared the copies it was given. **Comparing copies only ever finds the copies you list.**
- Both now assert the predicate over **all four** consumers and refuse a restated copy. (g) further asserts that **no** consumer carries a private mode gate, so divergence is impossible rather than merely detectable.

### STALE COPY, AGAIN

`childQualifyingAutoUnitsNote` rendered for **every** `'auto'` employee saying *"every eligible child counts as one qualifying child… the relief category shown is for information only"* — flatly untrue for anyone with a derived grid. It now renders only when the figure really IS the head count, and names the missing category as the reason; a new `childQualifyingAutoWeightedNote` covers the other branch. The card branches on a returned `pricedFromGrid` flag rather than on the mode, because since r344 the mode alone no longer determines the rule.

The two `WeightingGap` sentences were rewritten the same way. My first rewrite dropped "over-deducted" from the under-direction sentence and the r343 direction guard caught it — that guard's insistence that *each sentence names its own tax consequence* is correct and survived.

### DECISIONS THE TICKET DID NOT SETTLE

- **`num_children` remains the head count.** Form E, CP8D and the EA read it as one. Physical children and qualifying children stay two figures on the screen, which is what the reporter asked for and what the data already held — only the card had conflated them.
- **The reporter's "Child 18+ in qualifying full-time study → 1 or applicable category"** is not implemented as a conditional: the five s.48 categories are what the Family register stores, and the pack prices them. No new category was invented.

### NOT DONE

- The production read answered the *what*; nobody has re-cut Daniel Tan's issued payslips, and they do not need re-cutting, because the payslip figure was correct throughout.
- The gate ran before two additive DOM cases were appended to an already-covered file; those were run green in isolation (25 passed) and touch no production code.

## r346 (2026-09-26) — the EA was following a revision LHDN does not issue. `main@c70094d9`, **no migration**.

Closed: `fda53352`. Gate: **1032 files — equal to the suite file count**, 16 chunks, `tsc` 0, `next build` 0. No `gate:shadow`: `db/` untouched, watermark unchanged at `max(idx)=488`.

### THE TICKET WAS INVERTED, AND THE REPORTER STILL ENDS UP RIGHT

They asked us to rebuild the EA because ours was "not up to date". Ours printed **`(C.P.8A - Pin. 2024)`**. **LHDN does not issue a Pin. 2024.** Checked against the agency's own site on 2026-09-26: `borang_ea__c.p.8a_-_pin._2023_.pdf` returns `206 application/pdf`; 2024, 2025 and 2026 at the same path return **404**. LHDN's own *"EA & EC Guide Notes — Remuneration for the Year 2024"* accompany the **Pin. 2023** form.

**THE REVISION LABEL IS NOT THE YEAR**, and reading it as one is almost certainly how the error was made upstream. Our claim came from item `ece6d75d`'s attachment — Producer *"Developer Express Inc. DXperience v23.2.5"*, another payroll vendor's rendering. `docs/forms/…-transcription.txt` had **already** flagged that file as *"a TRACING SOURCE, not LHDN artwork"*. The caution was right; the revision number taken from the same file was not.

The reporter's attachment is **byte-identical** to what hasil.gov.my serves (sha256 `6b766381…`, 381,770 bytes) — the first genuine agency artwork this board has received. It is now in `docs/forms/` with the BM xlsx (docProps `Company=LHDNM`).

### WHAT MOVED

- The revision, everywhere: the form, the field register, the report page, 18 catalogue strings across six locales.
- **35 English captions** to the agency's own wording, verbatim. They had been our paraphrase, because until now there was no agency English to check against.
- **The form's furniture is now per-edition.** It was Malay on BOTH forms, on a rationale — *"the viewer's language never changes a Malaysian tax form"* — that LHDN contradicts by publishing an English edition with an English masthead. We were printing the Malay edition's furniture around English captions: a document the agency does not issue.
- **The money column**, measured off the agency's own vector PDF: `482.3 → 556.6`, where the tracing had `504.5 → 571.3` — 22.2 pt too far right, 7.5 pt too narrow, and running to the page frame where the agency's stops 15.3 pt inside it.
- `No. Majikan E`, not `TIN Majikan E` — it is a **file number, not a TIN**; the TIN on that band is the employee's.
- `Nama Pegawai`, not `Name Pegawai` — an inherited typo that a comment in `lib/ea-pdf.ts` and a test had both explicitly **defended** as "the specimen's own spelling".

### DECISIONS THE TICKET DID NOT SETTLE

- **The agency's file is held for comparison; it is not served.** It went to `docs/forms/`, not `public/forms/`. What we print is still our rendering on our paper, so `my.ea.en` / `my.ea.ms` still declare `agency-layout` and still may never declare `official`. The user-facing note "we hold no blank C.P.8A from LHDN" was left alone: its purpose — *this is our page, check it against the real one* — is unchanged.
- **Only the money column was re-measured.** Every other constant is still a 150 dpi tracing of a redrawing, and `lib/ea-pdf.ts` now says exactly that instead of claiming "every number was read off the specimen".

### THREE DEFECTS THE RENDER CHECK CAUGHT THAT NOTHING ELSE COULD

All three passed `tsc`, the suite and `next build` while being **visibly wrong on the page**. They were found by rasterising the blank form and looking at it.

- **Section E printed twice**, the second reading `2. PERKESO: 2. SOCSO : Amount of…`. `contributionAmount` is a **shared caption** for E1 and E2 and I had prefixed it with E2's word. §8: *a shared caption may say only what is true of every member.*
- **`Gratuity for the period from from`** — the renderer already draws `periodFrom` after the caption.
- The English **`PRIVATE SECTOR Employee's Statement of Remuneration` ran left out of its block and straight through the centred `MALAYSIA`**. pdf-lib does not clip, so the page still rendered, still returned 200 and still downloaded — the r205 Borang A lesson, live again. It now wraps to two lines, as the agency's English edition sets it.

### TWO GUARDS THAT PINNED DECISIONS THIS ROUND REVERSES

Updated, not deleted (§8), each carrying the reversal and its evidence:

- *"the agency's words are the SAME in both languages — they are not translated"* asserted the Malay masthead onto the English form. Rewritten to assert each edition prints **its own** words, and that the two really are different pages — keeping what the old case was right about: neither is translated by us.
- *"the officer caption keeps the specimen's own spelling"* pinned `Name Pegawai` and argued that anyone "fixing" it should fail there rather than ship a form *"that no longer matches the page it was traced from"*. Every word true — and the page traced from was a rival vendor's. **A guard that pins a faithful transcription of the wrong source makes the error permanent.**

### A MISTAKE OF MINE THAT COST ~15 MINUTES OF GATE

I renamed the transcription and updated the two references I knew about. A **third** test file (`test/r219-ea-cp8a-form.test.ts`) held the old name and failed the gate at chunk 4 with `ENOENT` — a **collection** error, so `grep -c AssertionError` correctly reported **0**, which §4 reads as "environment". It was not: the file never loaded. Fixing it changed the tree and invalidated the five chunks already run, so the gate restarted. **`grep -rn` for every reference to a renamed file before starting a 40-minute gate**; a targeted run of five EA tests did not include the one that broke.

### NOT DONE

- The remaining geometry constants (banner, officer box, section rules, Section A columns) still come from the tracing. The agency's file is on disk to finish that with.
- The agency's page sets its section letters in filled black boxes and numbers items `1.` then `(a)` where we set `1(a)`. Both are visible on a side-by-side and neither was touched.

## r345 (2026-09-26) — two screens told the truth about arithmetic that was already right. `main@7006882d`, **no migration**.

Closed: `20837372`, `9653472a`. Gate: **1031 files — equal to the suite file count**, 16 chunks, `tsc` 0, `next build` 0. No `gate:shadow`: `db/` untouched, watermark unchanged at `max(idx)=488`.

### BOTH ITEMS WERE THE SAME SHAPE OF DEFECT

Neither ticket was a calculation bug. r342 capped TP3 Section C correctly and r344 weighted child relief correctly; in both cases the round shipped the arithmetic and not the surface that would let anyone SEE it, and in both cases the reporter came back. `20837372` was contested a **third** time. The lesson is not "add a screen" — it is that an approved plan promising a display (`r342`: *"the screen will show what part of it the calculation is allowed to use, beside it"*) is not discharged by shipping the kernel half.

### 20837372 — SECTION C

Each C2 sub-line and C3 now print **limit / tax-exempt / excess / remaining** beside the box, and a section total reads `exemptTotal`, `epfAllowable` and `netRemuneration` **off the seed** rather than summing them again — two call sites each working the caps out is the duplicate source of truth §1 forbids, and is the same defect pointing the other way.

Two things found while building it, neither in the ticket:

- **C3 was drawn as though it had no limit.** It has no `subItems`, so it fell in the whole-line branch beside C1 and C5, whose comment read *"C1, C3 and C5 are not exemptions at all"*. C1 and C5 genuinely carry no limit; C3 is held to the EPF relief cap. The single largest capping on the form — RM4,000 against the reporter's own keyed 8,979 — was the one figure the screen never mentioned. `tp3EpfReliefCap` is now exported so the page and the kernel provably read one cap; the page carries no literal `4000`.
- **`taxRelief.tp3.exemptLimitNote` was false.** It said *"Whatever you key is recorded and used exactly as it is; nothing is trimmed."* That stopped being true when r342 shipped, and it contradicted the very behaviour this item makes visible. The input is still never trimmed and the note still says so; the claim that the whole of it is *used* is gone.

An unlimited sub-line (C2(iii), C2(v)) shows **blank** excess and remaining, never `0.00`: a zero there asserts "we checked and nothing is over", which for a line with no sourced limit is a claim this repo cannot make (§8).

### 9653472a — THE CATEGORY GAP

r344 gated the derived child-relief grid on `built.categorised === built.eligible`. That gate is **right** and is untouched: `childReliefGridFromFamily` skips a child it cannot classify, so a partial grid relieves fewer children than the employee has — production held one employee who would have gone RM4,000 → RM2,000 the moment r344 shipped without it. Its consequence is that the weighting reaches **nobody** until categories are filled in, and nothing said so anywhere. `core/child-relief-review.ts` now carries `categoryGap` beside `recordDisagreement` as a subset of the same `people` objects (no second walk, no second arithmetic).

**Scoped to `auto` and `auto_table` only.** On `manual` the typed figure decides and a category changes nothing, so a manual row would put an action on screen that has no effect. The predicate **names the two modes it trusts** rather than excluding the one it knows, so a hand-edited mode is not silently treated as auto.

**No "you could be relieving RM x" column.** The s.48 weight of an uncategorised child is unknowable — 1 unit or 8 — so that figure cannot be stood behind (§8). Eligible / categorised / missing and relief-given-today are printed instead. No bulk fill: a child's category is a fact about that child.

### DECISIONS THE TICKETS DID NOT SETTLE

- **The TP3 limits reach the screen and never the paper.** They are the specification's, not the form's; a printed TP3 carrying a limit column would not match the one the employee signed. Re-asserted from both sides.
- **`manual` employees are absent from the category-gap list** rather than shown-with-a-caveat. The plan allowed either; a row implying an action that has no effect is worse than no row.

### TWO MISTAKES OF MINE, BOTH CAUGHT BY MY OWN VERIFICATION AND WORTH READING

- **My test proved nothing where it mattered most.** The first cut of `test/9653472a-child-relief-category-gap.test.ts` filtered its fixtures with a **local copy** of the production condition. Loosening the real filter to every mode left all six behavioural cases green — only a source-text assertion failed. `hasCategoryGap` is now exported and the test drives the real predicate; the same revert now fails *"a MANUAL employee is absent"* with a real `AssertionError`. **A behavioural test that restates the rule it is testing is a source-text test wearing better clothes.**
- **My first render check was worthless and looked fine.** Six locales × two routes all returned **200 with zero intl errors** — while every request rendered **English**, because locale comes from the `NEXT_LOCALE` cookie and I was sending `Accept-Language`. It also fetched `/payroll/transactions/tp3` with no `employmentId`, so the Section C block never rendered at all: the pre-existing `colExemptionLimit` came back absent too, which is what exposed it. Re-run with the cookie and a seeded employment id, all six locales render all four columns with no raw keys. **§8's "a 200 is not a render check" is not about status codes — a check can exercise the wrong page in the wrong language and still be all green.**

### NOT DONE

- The child-relief gap card is proven populated only by `test/child-relief-review-locales.dom.test.tsx` (six locales, real catalogues). The dev-server pass renders its **empty** state, because no seeded employee has children — the same gap that file was created for.
- `fda53352` (the EA C.P.8A) is planned, not built, and its plan was corrected mid-session: our form prints `Pin. 2024`, a revision **LHDN does not issue**. The agency publishes `Pin. 2023`, byte-identical to the reporter's attachment. Measured off the genuine vector PDF, the money column also moves (agency `482.3 → 556.6`, ours `504.5 → 571.3`), so `lib/ea-pdf.ts`'s claim that it "is untouched" holds only against the rival vendor's tracing.

## r344 (2026-09-26) — the money half of the child-relief weighting, and a near miss that would have over-deducted. `main@46ef91e8`, **no migration**.

Closed: `a5f21891`. Gate: **1029 files — equal to the suite file count**, 16 chunks, `tsc` 0, `next build` 0. No `gate:shadow`: `db/` untouched, watermark unchanged at `max(idx)=488`.

### WHAT r343 LEFT, AND THIS FINISHES

r343 made the Identification & Tax card **display** the weighted child figure beside the one the payslip uses. It did not make the payslip use it — `childReliefAmount` reached the kernel only for `'auto_table'` — so a disabled child in higher education was relieved RM2,000 where s.48 prices it at RM16,000. The screen said so; the money did not move.

Now the `'auto'` sync **derives** the grid from the Family register instead of carrying the old one forward, and all three money-path consumers widen together: `core/payroll.ts`, `core/payroll-view.ts` and `localization/my/multicycle-worksheet.ts`. Widening one alone would leave the worksheet printing a fabricated difference against the payslips it replays — which is exactly what r343's `(g)` guard exists to catch, and it passes with all three moved.

### THE NEAR MISS, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH READING

`childReliefGridFromFamily` **skips** a child with no `child_relief_category` — it cannot price what it cannot classify — while that same child **does** count towards the head count. So deriving the grid unconditionally relieves *fewer* children than the employee has.

Production has **one `'auto'` employee with 2 eligible children and only 1 categorised**. Shipping the obvious version would have taken them from RM4,000 of relief to RM2,000 — an over-deduction, caused by a change whose entire purpose is to stop over-deducting. It surfaced only because an existing guard asserted the stored grid, and chasing that assertion led to the measurement.

So the grid is stored **only** when every eligible child carries a category. Otherwise it is **nulled** — never carried stale, because a grid that no longer describes the family is worse than no grid — and all three consumers fall back to `num_children × perChild`, exactly today's behaviour. Nobody loses relief while a category is missing.

### TWO BUGS OF MINE, BOTH CAUGHT BY GUARDS I DID NOT WRITE

- **Rail (b) compared the grid with `JSON.stringify`**, which is key-order sensitive, so a grid read back from JSONB never matched an identical freshly-derived one and the sync fired on *every* family edit. Three existing guards caught it — a spouse add, a custom-relationship add, an unchanged re-sync. Now compared canonically.
- **Rail (b) originally compared only the head count**, so changing a child from `under_18` to `disabled_study` — 1 unit to 8, RM2,000 to RM16,000 — would have short-circuited and left the stored grid on the old category indefinitely.

### DECISIONS

- **`num_children` stays the head count.** Form E, CP8D and EA all read it as one; a test asserts the sync still writes the plain count there.
- **One guard updated, not loosened.** `statutory-disabled-spouse-child-table` asserted the grid was carried forward across a family edit. On `'auto'` the register is now the source of truth, and that case adds an *uncategorised* child, so the grid clears and relief falls back to the head count — no money moves for that employee. The claim the case actually defends, that a family edit never withdraws a relief *claim*, is untouched.

### WHAT WAS NOT DONE

- **`scripts/resync-child-relief-grid.ts` has not run yet.** The sync fires only on a family edit, so the three existing `'auto'` employees keep a null grid until somebody touches their record. It calls `syncChildReliefFromFamily` itself rather than writing the column, so every rail comes with it — including rail (d)'s payroll alert when a figure moves under an open batch. It carries forward r342's lesson: a tenant that cannot be resolved is skipped and counted, not allowed to abort the run.
- Issued payslips are not recomputed.

## r343 (2026-09-26) — four items, and two of the round's errors were the plans, not the builds. `main@dd6a9a07`, **no migration ran**.

Closed: `04b88724`, `03f89c0f`, `1478c281`, `cbfa8b0b`. Raised: `a5f21891`.

**`04b88724`'s plan contradicted itself** — it demanded `eligibleChildReliefCount` return a weighted count *and* that `num_children` stay a head count, when that function is precisely what the sync writes there. ### DECISIONS

- **A typed figure is not an error.** `03f89c0f`'s screen words every row as a *disagreement*, says the record is as likely to be the incomplete half, and offers **no bulk action** — 52 children whose reality nobody has established is the worst thing to change in one click.
- **Four day types, always.** `cbfa8b0b` offered three wherever extended hours is off, which is every company. The option list is now the whole vocabulary; an Ordinary Day row explains it earns nothing rather than vanishing.

Now strips comments; proved both ways.

## r342 (2026-09-26) — one item, contested, and it was money that was already wrong. `main@6ba48e0e`, **no migration**.

Closed: `20837372`. Gate: **1020 files — equal to the suite file count**, 16 chunks, `tsc` 0, `next build` 0. No `gate:shadow`: the change is arithmetic plus a resync script, `db/` is untouched, watermark unchanged at `max(idx)=488`.

### THE SAME BOX GAVE TWO ANSWERS, AND ONE OF THEM WAS ON A REAL PAYSLIP

`core/payroll.ts:4349` capped K with `pack.payroll.epfReliefCap`, while `deriveAccumulatorSeed` subtracted the **raw** C3 from accumulated pay. LHDN defines K as capped, so `∑(Y−K)` must be struck against the capped K. The reporter's one production form holds **C3 = 8,979 against a RM4,000 cap**, so `tp3_net_remuneration` was stored at **47,421 where it should be 52,400** — RM4,979 too low, and that employee's PCB light by the tax on it.

### THE C2 HALF REVERSES A DECISION THIS REPO WROTE DOWN TWICE

Both `core/tp3.ts` and a test whose comment read *"THIS ASSERTION IS THE DECISION"* argued that capping C2 *"would tax the same ringgit twice"*. It does not, and the arithmetic settles it:

    C1 57,000 (including a 7,000 travel allowance), C2(i) keyed 7,000, limit 6,000
      uncapped →  net 50,000  — the whole allowance escapes tax
      capped   →  net 51,000  — the 1,000 excess is taxed, ONCE

C1 is **gross** by the file's own definition, so the excess sits in it either way; `C1 − ΣC2` is the single place it is taxed or not. Counting ΣC2 whole subtracts the excess *again*. Capping taxes it once, which is exactly what the specification's printed page 20 item 9 requires: *"Any amount exceed the restricted amount shall be taxable."* Both comments now **record the reversal** rather than being deleted.

### DECISIONS

- **ADR-0008 is preserved, not overridden.** It governs refusing *input*, and nothing here refuses anything: every box stores exactly what was keyed, and only what the *arithmetic* may use is limited. The seed reports both sides — `exemptEntered` beside `exemptTotal`, `epfClaimed` beside `epfAllowable` — and they are asserted separately, because collapsing them is the mistake a later reader is most likely to make.
- **The cap is read from the pack, never written here.** `core/payroll.ts` already owns it and its comment says why ("cap math always matches the calculator"). A second literal would be the duplicate source of truth §1 forbids.
- **No limit is invented.** C2(iii) and C2(v) carry no sourced limit and contribute in full, the same discipline `tp3ExemptionOverLimits` already applied.

### A BUG IN MY OWN FIRST CUT, CAUGHT BY AN EXISTING GUARD

`cappedLineTotal` summed the catalogue's sub-lines, so a payload carrying `amount` with no `subItems` — which `readGroup` cannot produce but a legacy or hand-built payload can — recomputed to **zero** and turned a −400 keying error into +500, hiding the very thing that guard exists to surface. It now falls back to the stored amount, and the case is pinned. The guard that caught it was the negative-net keying-error test, which predates this item by several rounds.

### WHAT WAS NOT DONE

- **Issued payslips are not recomputed.** Correcting the seed changes what future runs compute; re-cutting a payslip moves money already paid and reported. The reporter's decision.
- Five guards were updated rather than loosened, including the two that pinned the old decision. Non-vacuity proven on both halves: uncapping the EPF gives `K as the specification defines it: expected 8979 to be 4000`; uncapping C2 gives `what counts: expected 7000 to be 6000`.

## r341 (2026-09-26) — one item, and the build corrected the premise it was briefed with. `main@c510d515`, **no migration**.

Closed: `8d3a7bff`. Re-planned and returned to the reporter: `20837372`, `cbfa8b0b`. Raised: `1478c281`.
Gate: **1019 files — equal to the suite file count**, 16 chunks, `tsc` 0, `next build` 0. No `gate:shadow`: the approved plan states "no migration, no schema change, no data change", the agent was forbidden from creating one, and `db/` is untouched.

### THE BRIEF WAS WRONG ABOUT THE CODE, AND SO WAS THE CODE'S OWN COMMENT

The approved plan, the agent's brief, `core/read.ts`'s own comment and `test/a0b90c81-shared-group-cards.test.ts` all said the card-hiding rule was *"keyed on the POOLING POINTER, deliberately NOT on group membership"*. It was not. On main the block joined `leave_shared_group_member` to `leave_shared_group`, built `folded` from every member of a placed group, and returned `visible.filter((r) => !folded.has(r.leaveTypeId))` — `balance_source_type_id` appears nowhere in it. The old test pinned the wide behaviour: its fixture types held 4 and 5 days of their own, no pointer, and it asserted they lost their cards.

So on production **Marriage Leave's card was already folded and 59 employments already could not see 177.00 days**. Honouring the approved outcome required *narrowing* the rule to `folded.has(…) && isPoolBorrower(…)`, not preserving a status quo that did not exist. The builder caught it, the verifier confirmed it on main independently, and the parent confirmed it again before accepting.

### A CORRECTION OWED, RAISED BEFORE SHIPPING RATHER THAN AFTER

`1478c281`. The plan described five member cards as **keeping** cards they do not currently draw, so the reporter approved that bullet believing it protected the status quo. It is a change: shipping makes five cards **appear** — Marriage with its 177 days (the fix), plus Caregiver, Examination, Graduation and Study at 0.00. A ticket whose whole point was *fewer* cards ends with more of them. The raise says so plainly and offers the rule they probably pictured: hide a member card that holds nothing, keeping Marriage visible.

### DECISIONS

- **The two settings stay unreconciled.** A shared group is a combined CEILING (`enforceSharedLeaveGroupLimit`); `balance_source_type_id` is a LEDGER ROUTE. Different member sets by design — merging them would put five types on a balance they do not draw, or drop five from a ceiling that caps them.
- **`mayAppearInApplyMenu` is untouched.** A hidden card never removes the right to apply; that distinction is the whole of item `a0b90c81` and it survived.
- **Compose, don't translate.** The merged card's ceiling line reuses the already-translated `ofLimit` rather than a new English string. `alsoCountsToward` is genuinely new, ships English in all six, and the test says so.

### THREE REVIEW FINDINGS, HAND-FIXED

1. **A localisation regression that would have shipped.** `pooledLimitLine` was English in all six and *replaced* a line the vanished tile rendered through the fully-translated `ofLimit` — a `zh` employee would have read English where they used to read Chinese. Now composed from the existing key; a guard pins that `ofLimit` stays distinct across locales (collapsing the five fails `expected 1 to be greater than 1`).
2. **A test comment claimed a guard the file does not provide** — the same defect class as this round's actual bug. The DOM file cannot see the server gate; the widening leaves it green 28/28. The comment now says so and names the server test that does fail.
3. An unreferenced fixture script was removed.

### WHAT WAS NOT DONE

- The four zero-balance member cards stay visible, pending the reporter's answer on `1478c281`.
- The merged card's Taken agrees with the Apply form but **not** with the Employee Balances grid — pre-existing and unchanged (the grid shows the pool's own applications with borrowers under Share). The claim that the two "cannot drift" is wrong and should not be repeated to the reporter.
- The merged-branch render check rests on the builder's pass; its fixture script was removed as unreferenced debt, so that pass is not re-runnable as committed. The parent's own pass covers the standalone branch only, because the seed configures no pooled type.

### THE TWO CONTESTED ITEMS, RE-PLANNED FROM THE REPORTER'S LATEST WORDS

- **`20837372`** — they are right, and half of it is live. The same C3 box is capped for `K` (`core/payroll.ts:4349`) and **uncapped** for `∑(Y−K)` (`core/tp3.ts:350`). Their one TP3 form holds C3 = 8,979 against a RM4,000 cap, so the stored accumulated net is **47,421 where it should be 52,400** — RM4,979 too low, under-deducting PCB. The C2 half reverses a documented decision: the comment argues capping "would tax the same ringgit twice", but C1 is gross by the file's own definition, so `C1 − cappedC2` taxes the excess exactly once — which is what the spec's printed p.20 item 9 requires. ADR-0008 is preserved: it governs refusing *input*, and nothing refuses anything; only what the arithmetic may use is limited.
- **`cbfa8b0b`** — the contest **reverses** the two-section design we had agreed ("do not create separate sections/screens"). Re-planned as the single table they now ask for, with the per-row conditional drawn as disabled cells. The TOIL engine and HR ledger exist and `toil` is active for this tenant; no employee-initiated request path exists at all. The OT double-compensation rule their new words omit was kept, because it is money rather than layout, and they were told so.

## r340 (2026-09-26) — nine items, two workflows, and a money defect the first cut reintroduced. `main@ffe92a8c`, **no migration**.

Closed: `3fa088fb`, `57d48735`, `ad7bc503`, `597c810a`, `04b88724`, `2a57a007`, `e78fd03d`, `0d02d4a1`, `7da0a4e7`.
Gate: **1016 files — equal to the suite file count**, 16 chunks, `tsc` 0, `next build` 0. No `gate:shadow`: every approved plan was checked for a migration before any agent started and none needed one, so agents were forbidden from creating one. Journal watermark unchanged at `max(idx)=488`.

Built by two workflows in five file-disjoint worktrees — 10 agents (build + adversarial verify), then 8 (fix + independent recheck) — with the money item and every remaining defect hand-finished by the parent.

### `3fa088fb` IS THE ROUND, AND THE FIRST CUT REINTRODUCED THE DEFECT IT FIXED

Approved TP1 reliefs never reached PCB. `payroll_input.tp1_deduction` had exactly one writer — `prefillTp1FromSelfRelief`, behind a **manual button** — and nothing called it at batch creation or generate time. Zakat had an automatic path; TP1 did not. Measured on production: **88 payslips issued, ZERO carrying a TP1**, against 8 approved 2026 declarations. Every employee who declared a relief was over-deducted, every month, silently.

The build derived LP₁ at generate time and correctly decided the open question the plan named — the derived leg is **regular-run only**, because deriving on an additional run would double-claim a regular + bonus month.

**Then it struck the delta against the wrong figure.** `lpAlreadyFed` replayed prior payslips' `st.lp`, which is `tp1 + en.lpDeclared` — the relief AND the month's optional-deduction pay codes. An unrelated pool was netted off the declaration, so an employee with those codes would watch their approved TP1 shrink toward **LP₁ = 0.00** as the year ran on: the reporter's exact symptom, through the new path. **69 tests passed over it.** Adversarial verification found it; it was hand-fixed per §8 (money is never sent back to an agent) to replay `st.lpDetail.tp1`, and pinned by an arm that fails `expected 100 to be 800` on the old code.

### DECISIONS THE TICKETS DID NOT SETTLE

- **A statutory transcription is not a sign-off.** `57d48735` corrected `disabledSpouse` RM5,000 → RM6,000 off printed p.28 item f and took the ruleset to 2026.9, retiring the red flag r339 left in three places. `disabledIndividual` keeps RM7,000 but loses its stale RATE-ONLY flag — same table, item e. The rows still read "pending sign-off", and that is correct: a checkable transcription and an accountant's signature are different things.
- **`available` and `balance` keep different names.** `7da0a4e7` asked for a rename that would have pointed one label at both figures. `core/read.ts:3012` records that they answer different questions. The plan declined that half and the reporter approved the decline; a guard now pins that they read differently in all six locales.
- **An absent box and a zero are different statements.** `ad7bc503` renders "nothing was recorded" where no declaration exists, rather than RM 0.00 across seventeen lines — the one place the page deliberately differs from the reporter's LHDN reference.
- **A typed number is never dressed as a calculated one.** `04b88724` marks the qualifying-child figure derived or entered, and leaves it editable in manual mode, where 71 of 75 employees sit.

### CORRECTIONS OWED TO THE REPORTER, AND ONE TO OURSELVES

- `ad7bc503`'s premise was wrong: the page was never "only a summary PCB amount" — sections 3, 9 and 10 were already built. Said at the top of the plan.
- My own earlier note that `pcbWorksheet` was missing `QC` was wrong. LHDN prints `Q` and `C` separately too, exactly as we do.
- `3fa088fb` is **wider than reported**: not one employee in one month, but every employee with an approved relief, every month.

### WHAT WAS NOT DONE

- **No backfill of the 88 issued payslips.** Re-cutting an issued payslip moves money already paid and reported. The reporter's decision, deliberately out of scope; raise it as its own item.
- The **cross-form per-code cap** — a relief declared on both a previous employer's TP3 Section D and our TP1 can push combined ∑LP past the statutory annual — remains unbuilt. Deciding which declaration yields is policy this repo has no source for.
- The leave **Explain panel** is only partially reconciled, and `app/admin/personnel/[employmentId]` still shows a borrower the pool's Full Entitlement. Both belong to a follow-up item.
- The **additional run's** PCB increment still computes with `lpCurrent = 0`. Byte-identical to today and flagged rather than changed.

### THE GUARDS EARNED THEIR KEEP, AND ONE WAS NEARLY DEFEATED

`7da0a4e7` forced **seven guards across six files** to be updated rather than loosened — five found only by the full gate. `r303`'s byte-for-byte fixture was **diffed before regenerating**, per its own header: 3 of 18 sections differ, all English, all the single word `balance` → `Balance`, no markup change. Separately, the leave build had kept a foreign guard green with a **decoy literal** left inside an unused local; the fix pass updated it properly. And two locale typos the fix pass introduced (Vietnamese `bên dưối`, Tamil `டனி`) were caught by the recheck — **no guard can see a misspelling**, which is why the English-only convention was kept for new keys and the shared leave labels were populated from existing human translations rather than written fresh.

## r338 + r339 (2026-09-25) — seven items, shipped as one deploy after four failed attempts on box memory. `main@3e094ae8`, migration **0488**.

Closed: `639bf4a5`, `73ddd5a1`, `00e28308`, `bb2b2e86`, `4ca06dea` (r338); `04b88724`, `20837372` (r339).
Gate: **998 files — equal to the suite file count**, 14 chunks, `tsc` 0, `next build` 0, `gate:shadow` **PASS 401/401**. Render check: 4 screens × 6 locales, 24 × 200, zero poison tokens, and the corrected child reliefs verified **on screen** (RM 8,000 ×2, RM 16,000 ×1, retired RM 14,000 absent).

⚠️ **Gated as ONE receipt across two rounds**, because main moved past r338's receipt while its deploy was blocked. That is the honest shape: the tree that shipped is the tree that was gated.

### THE REPORTER WAS RIGHT AND WE WERE WRONG — TWICE, ON STATUTORY MONEY

`04b88724`: we told them our five `childByCategory` figures "match HASiL line for line". They contested, citing the LHDN 2026 MTD specification. **They were right.** Printed p.27 gives a qualifying-children table — a disabled child counts as **4** children (RM8,000), one in further instruction as **8** (RM16,000). We held RM6,000 and RM14,000: the **annual assessment** figures. Malaysia has two schedules and they disagree for disabled children.

**Our own code had said so.** That object carried `⚠️ RATE-ONLY, NOT YET VERIFIED` and we quoted it as confirmation anyway. Every value now carries its printed-page citation.

Three things the build found that the brief did not name:
- **Nobody was affected** — stronger than "at most one". The money path reads `child_relief_table` gated on `auto_table`; the one disabled child belongs to an `auto` employee.
- **A THIRD source carried the old figures.** `localization/statutory-pack/bundled/my-2026.01.01.pack.json` embeds a **signed** copy; `pnpm statutory:sync` would have reinstated 6,000/14,000 **over** the fix and stamped them 2026.7. Caught by an existing guard, fixed by rebuilding the pack.
- **`disabledSpouse` is wrong too** — p.28 item f gives RM6,000, we hold RM5,000. Raised as `57d48735`, not swept in.

### TP3's SECTION D REACHED NOTHING

`20837372`: LHDN p.22 — *"The information amount from the TP3 Form shall be treated in the formula as variable (Y−K\*), X, Z and ∑LP."* We wired three. Section D was captured, validated, stored and read by **nothing**, and ∑LP is subtracted inside P — so a new joiner who declared previous-employment reliefs was **over-deducted**.

⚠️ **CORRECTING MY OWN BRIEF, MEASURED AFTER THE BUILD:** I told the agent this was live. The one production TP3 form has a Section D with seventeen keys and **every amount zero** (Section C totals 75,579). The 0488 backfill carries `AND d.lp <> 0`, so it correctly skipped it: `tp3_lp` is NULL, read as zero, **no payslip moved**. The structural defect was real; the urgency was mine.

Three of that brief's premises were wrong and the source won: **C2 was already five sub-items** (`c.c2?.amount` is the server's *sum*); **the TP3 form prints no limit column on Section C**, so ADR-0008 decides it — captured, never blocked; and therefore **capping C2 would tax the same ringgit twice**, because p.20's "any amount exceed the restricted amount shall be taxable" addresses the *previous* employer, whose over-limit portion is already inside C1. Two of the five C2 limits are `null` and stay null — the build **stopped rather than invent**, which is the discipline `04b88724` proved we needed.

### THE GATE CAUGHT WHAT NO WORKTREE COULD

One red chunk: `employee-import-field-parity` walks the **merged** schema and found `tp3_lp` neither carried by an import column nor excluded with a reason — invisible from inside the TP3 worktree, the same shape as `maritalStatusSourceRequestId` in r334. Given its **own** exclusion entry rather than appended to the four existing `tp3*` fields, because their stated reason (*also loaded by the payroll history import*) is **not true** of a form-only column; appending would have made the guard assert something false.

### r338's FIVE

`639bf4a5` **reverses r336 one round after it shipped**, on the reporter's contest: Locations returns to Attendance as a company listing with dedicated screens. Route and `screenKey` deliberately did not move; the drift ratchet is byte-untouched (it governs imports, not menus); a company's second location is **shown**, rowSpanned, because production has 8 locations across 6 companies and the ticket's one-per-company example did not match the data.

`73ddd5a1` proved **my plan overstated the cost**: I told the reporter blank marital status would cost Caregiver *and* Natural Disaster Leave; `NDL` has no eligibility row at all. Now an assertion, not prose. It also made concrete that production holds **5,922 days of granted-but-invisible balance** — created before the read and grant paths agreed, never created again, existing days untouched.

`00e28308` caught that there are **TWO** find-or-create sites, not the one I named — r337 made a non-regular run able to open a month, so stamping only `createBatch` would have left every **bonus-led** month unstamped. Stamped at creation so **no `UPDATE` of the column exists anywhere**, making a later stealth backfill structurally impossible.

`4ca06dea` found a **third** omission I had missed (the `groups` array), so a corrected count alone would have disabled Process **without saying why**; and `actions.ts` was reporting the wrong reason entirely.

`bb2b2e86` found the 50-row cap default was **never pinned**, and that its own first locale guard would have shipped a **malformed Thai ICU string green** because next-intl swallows `FORMATTING_ERROR`.

### THE DEPLOY, AND THE BOX IS OUT OF RUNWAY

**Four failed attempts**, ~40 minutes producing nothing, every one memory. `deploy.sh`'s heap cap went `4096 → 2560 → 3584 → 4096` across r336–r339 as the diagnosis converged. The rule now recorded there: **the cap must fit RAM + free swap, not RAM alone**, and a cap above what the box can back converts a clean V8 self-OOM into a kernel kill. Also recorded: a killed `pnpm build` leaves a **~2.5 GB orphan reparented to init for ~10 minutes**, which starves the retry and looks exactly like capacity — check `ps --sort=-rss` before blaming the number.

⚠️ **The next bump does not fit.** 4096 plus overhead is ~80% of this box's entire 5.6 GB. The type pass has needed more memory in four consecutive rounds. **Add RAM or grow `/swap.img` (267 GB of disk free) before touching that number again.**

### NOT DONE

`disabledSpouse` (`57d48735`, raised). TP3 **R1**: C1's Malay caption reads *"yang dikenakan cukai"*, which if correct means `C1 − ΣC2 − C3` double-subtracts and **under**-deducts — not flipped on an unresolved reading; the only document that settles it 404s on both LHDN URLs. **R2**: TP3 Section D and our own TP1 now both feed ∑LP and `checkTp1OverClaim` has never seen a TP3. The child-relief mode migration for the other 74 employees stays the reporter's separate trigger.

## r337 (2026-09-24) — one item, and it caught a silent under-remittance to LHDN. `main@9cff0a25`, no migration.

Closed: `23e7dac3` (payroll cycles in any order).
Gate: **991 files — equal to the suite file count**, 14 chunks, **zero red chunks on the first pass**, `tsc` 0, `next build` 0. No shadow gate: no migration, journal verified unchanged after the merge at 400 entries / max idx 487. Render check: 3 screens × 6 locales, 18 × 200, zero poison tokens in the dev log and in `<script>`-stripped markup.

### THE FINDING: OPENING THE SELECTOR NAIVELY WOULD HAVE UNDER-PAID LHDN

The reporter asked to run BONUS or Off Cycle before Monthly. Measured through the real kernel **before any code was written**: RM5,000 salary + RM500 overtime + RM3,000 bonus, bonus first, produced month **PCB 60.00 instead of 100.00**; a variant put EPF employer at **1,030 instead of 1,080**. The regular run was not a delta — it recomputed the whole normal-wage month beside an increment taken on a base that did not yet contain the overtime.

So the load-bearing half of this item is **the month restating when the regular run lands**, which ADR-0085 lists and the brief did not emphasise. Both orders now telescope to the same month, pinned as literals, with the same month paid as a single run as an independent oracle.

### AND THE ADR WAS WRONG ABOUT WHY IT WAS BLOCKED

ADR-0085 §1.2 said order-independence is unbuildable without signed deltas (step 3), because the first run would be "taxed as though its payment were the employee's normal monthly pay". **False against the kernel**: `wagesExOt` is recomputed per employee from the COMPENSATION RECORD on every run, so the month's normal wage is in the statutory base whether or not the regular run has happened — Y1 was never taken from the runs. Recorded as a correction in the ADR rather than relied on silently. **Step 3 remains NOT STARTED; `clampDelta` and `deltaStat` are untouched.**

### BUILD ORDER WAS THE SAFETY ARGUMENT, AND IT WAS HONOURED LITERALLY

Step 4 — the refusal for a month already filed with LHDN, EPF or SOCSO — is commits 1 and 2, **proven before a line of the selector or the kernel order moved**. It consumes r330's `periodFiledTx` unchanged and adds `describeFiledEvidence` so the message names the return, its period, its filing date and the acknowledgement. Three doors: `createAdditionalRun`, `createBatch`, `generatePayslips`. The line is `run_seq > 1` — "a run that changes a figure an earlier run already produced" IS "a run that is not the month's first" — which keeps a lone regular run byte-identical and preserves r292's judgement that a wrongly filed month must stay correctable.

### ONE RESIDUAL, BOUNDED AND DISCLOSED

The EPF Third Schedule steps the EMPLOYER column at RM5,000 and `deltaStat` still clamps at zero, so whichever run crosses the step contributes RM0 rather than handing the difference back. **Bound RM38.00** — the step's size — and **upward only**, so an out-of-order month is never under-remitted, only over, and the excess lands in the employee's own EPF account. Absorbing it on the regular run works arithmetically and was **rejected**: that is step 3 under another name, and it would make a regular run's EPF disagree with the Third Schedule row for its own wage on a payslip an employee reads.

ADR-0085 also gained the **§7 worksheet its own build order cites and did not have** — the citation pointed at ADR-0024 §7, which always runs the regular run first and so structurally cannot answer "does the order matter?". The example is traced both ways with every per-run figure pinned as a literal in the test, so document and kernel cannot drift.

### THE DEPLOY, AND THE BOX IS OUT OF RUNWAY

Two attempts. r337's ~1,270 added kernel lines pushed the type pass past the 3584 cap r336 had settled on — a clean V8 self-OOM — and 4096 got it through on 5.6 GB of RAM+swap.

⚠️ **The trend now matters more than the number**: `2048 → 3072 → 4096 → 3584 → 4096` across R52, r83, r336, r337. The pass has needed a bump in **consecutive rounds**, and 4096 plus node overhead is already **~80% of this box's entire RAM+swap**. The next bump does not fit, and raising past what the box can back converts a clean V8 self-OOM into a kernel kill (the r336 story). **Add RAM or grow `/swap.img` — 267 GB of disk is free — before touching that number again.** Recorded in `deploy/deploy.sh`.

### NOT DONE

`batchDownstreamWarnings` is **narrower than the filed-period predicate**, so a month can read *filed* to the new refusal and *not-filed* to the amber banner an operator is looking at. Widening it changes a warning four screens rely on and wants its own round — **this is the one open decision handed back**. Per-leg filed granularity is still period-coarse (a filed Borang A bars a run that would only have moved PCB); the release valve — reverse the filing — is tested. The multi-cycle worksheet screen still excludes out-of-order months, documented in place rather than fixed, because teaching it the restating rule would move ADR-0024 §7's signed-off figures for no live caller.

## r336 (2026-09-24) — eleven items, six concurrent builders, and eight defects only the gate could see. `main@94ec3522`, migration **0487**.

Closed: `1bb09a73`, `3783fd87`, `7f251381`, `8d3a7bff`, `20f6c6a8`, `da7463b4`, `7d2df42a`, `639bf4a5`, `cbfa8b0b`, `99b2d6c0`, `2a57a007`.
Gate: **988 files — equal to the suite file count**, 14 chunks, `tsc` 0, `next build` 0, `gate:shadow` **PASS 400/400**. Render check: 5 screens × 6 locales, 30 × 200, zero poison tokens, the one new string asserted to resolve per-locale rather than by English fallback. Chunks 1–10 were **re-run on the final tree** because two fixes touched product code; a green gate has to be green on what ships.

### THE CONCURRENCY MODEL CHANGED, AND THE OLD RULE WAS MY OWN WRONG INFERENCE

"Two builders max" came from watching three agents stall and blaming the agent count. Measured: 12 cores sat **~57% idle** at 284 MB free. RAM binds only while *vitest* runs — an agent costs ~200 MB reading code and 1.5–3 GB testing. So `~/.aihr-gate-state/testlock.sh` caps **test runs** at 2 while any number of agents read and edit. Six ran concurrently on hardware that had held two.

A second lock followed, and an agent found the need, not me: `pnpm db:seed` **truncates the one shared `ai_hr_dev`** every render check reads, so two overlapping checks silently swap each other's data. `devdb-lock.sh` serialises the whole check — seed, server, curls, kill — because holding it only for the seed leaves exactly the window it closes. It was live risk for several hours.

### FOUR VACUOUS GUARDS, FOUND BY FOUR DIFFERENT AGENTS AND BY THE GATE

- **r332's holiday-claim guard** — and this one had shipped a lie. ADR-0086 removed the work site's hold on public holidays a fortnight earlier, but only the `stateNote` KEY went; the sentence survived in `admin.locations.pageDescription` and was **live on production in all six languages**. The guard could not have caught it twice over: it matched `stateNote`'s exact words, which the other key's wording never matched, *and* that case mocks `getTranslations` to echo key names, so no English sentence was ever in the markup it searched.
- **A clocking-grouping test** asserting order and the unlinked group's existence — so a page that had stopped grouping altogether stayed green.
- **`3783fd87`'s "not required" check** — `/name="companyLabel"(?![^>]*\brequired\b)/` scans forward from `name=`, and React emits attributes out of JSX order, putting `required` first. It was green **with the field required**.
- **`cbfa8b0b`'s own submit-blocking assertions** — passing because an empty form disables the button anyway.

### EIGHT INTEGRATION FAILURES THE GATE CAUGHT THAT NO BRANCH COULD

Only one was a product defect: the Leave Credit dialog's rewrite dropped its `lib/day-format` import and printed **raw day counts — `0.5` where every other leave surface says `0.50`** — the fault a `toFixed` grep cannot see, because the screen never formatted at all. The other seven were guards following code that legitimately moved; each was **updated with its reason, none loosened**, and four would otherwise have kept passing against **dead keys or renamed ids** while the screen said something else.

### MY BRIEFS WERE WRONG FIVE TIMES; THE SOURCE WON EACH TIME

- The **LHDN e-Data writer already ships** (`localization/my/cp39-file.ts`, served by `/payroll/reports/cp39-file`). I verified no *specimen* existed and read that as no *writer*. Listing it unavailable would have reshipped the r296 defect — a screen denying a file another screen hands over.
- The draft employee's **IC→DOB server path already existed** (`core/employee-draft.ts:755`); the gap was that nothing derived *while the draft was being filled in*.
- **`isValidIC` is `/^\d{12}$/`** — a digit count with no date check. Month 13 passes, the DOB silently comes back null, and the employee is created without one. Nothing refuses it anywhere.
- **An off day IS bankable** from the employee-request path; r334's finding held only for the roster election. The divergence is between *paths*, not day kinds.
- **"Most of point 1 is DONE" was false.** Only Balance is zero on a pooled borrower; Entitlement and Earned to Date still print the POOL's figures, because `rows.ts` resolves the breakdown through `balanceStoryTypeId`. Left open deliberately — reversing it re-opens the r209 red-notice trap and is load-bearing for `8d3a7bff`, which shipped this round.

### DECISIONS

- **`20f6c6a8`** — `verification` is a REQUIRED field on every payment format: `filed-file` (EPF, SOCSO — byte-equal to files the customer really filed), `specification-sample` (LHDN), `field-table-only`. The lesson from the wrong Borang A is not "only ship formats with a filed file", which would delete a shipped capability; it is that **a file's provenance may never be invisible**. Its LHDN row was taken OFF the new shelf **during the gate** rather than add debt to a ratchet that only shrinks — the row stays listed, with its provenance, pointing at the screen that serves it today.
- **`99b2d6c0`** — not one disabled-relief amount changed. The LHDN spec was never supplied, and `childByCategory` turns out to be flagged RATE-ONLY too. Also pinned **two kernel gates no test reached**: deleting either `auto_table` mode read would have left the whole suite green while every such employee silently reverted to flat child-relief counting — a wrong PCB with nothing on screen.
- **`cbfa8b0b`** — `eligible_minutes` is a record, never a valuation input (`day_type` stays NULL); `EXCLUDE_TOIL_BANKED_DAYS` byte-untouched, proven by a mutation showing **RM173.04 of overtime** would be paid on a banked day without it. Ticket point 4 stayed unbuilt as the plan promised. Migration **0487 extends** `replacement_leave_request_date` rather than adding a claim-line table, because a separate table would give "what did this employee claim for this date" two owners.
- **`2a57a007`** — the pooled Share columns go positive. Verified safe first: nothing computes from them, and the `sum(balance)` invariant is about `balance`, not the displayed share. Said so **at the line that decides the sign**, or the next reader restores the minus.
- **`639bf4a5`** — the work-site register MOVED pack surface rather than merely stopping being advertised, because the pack's surface claim was the only thing authorising its direct `core/clocking-location` import. The ratchet **shrank** by one entry and nothing was added at the new address.

### CORRECTIONS OWED TO THE REPORTER

- **`7f251381`'s approved mockup mislabels four symbols.** It captions `Y1` "Previous employment income" and `Yt` "Accumulated remuneration"; the engine has `Y1 = p.monthlyWage` (this month's wage) and `Yt = p.additional` (the bonus). Building to it would have printed a bonus under an accumulator caption — the exact defect the item exists to remove. The screen is right; the picture they approved is not.
- **`73ddd5a1` is wider than we told them**: three leave types, not one (Maternity 5,390 days, Paternity 385, Marriage 147 — 5,922 standing across 74 employees). Sent with the correction at the top. The useful half: **all 19 clear-cut cases are already reversed at net 0.00**, so every remaining day hangs on a blank field and filling them in genuinely resolves it.
- **`20f6c6a8`'s plan says we are waiting on their LHDN file.** We are not waiting to *write* it — it exists. We are waiting to *verify* it against a real filed one, which moves the entry to `filed-file`: a one-word registry change, not a build.

### THE DEPLOY, AND A REAL BUG IN `deploy.sh`

Four attempts. The script capped the build heap at **4096 MB on a box with ~2.5 GB available**, so V8 never approached its own limit, never collected hard, and the kernel killed it first — a bare `Killed`/137, unlike the two earlier OOMs this file records, which died as V8's own `Ineffective mark-compacts`. **Different failure, opposite fix.** Lowering to 2560 converted 137 into V8's own `FatalProcessOutOfMemory`, proving the mechanism and showing 2560 was simply too low; **3584** got it through.

The rule is now stated correctly in the file: the cap must fit **RAM + free swap**, not RAM alone. And the confounder is recorded, because it cost a wrong diagnosis: a killed `pnpm build` leaves a **~2.5 GB `next` worker reparented to init in D state for ~10 minutes**, which starves the retry and makes a capacity problem out of a cleanup one. Check `ps --sort=-rss` before blaming the number. `typescript.ignoreBuildErrors` was never on the table — that pass catches RSC boundary errors `tsc` alone does not.

### NOT DONE

`23e7dac3` is **built and gated-pending** on `build/r337-23e7dac3`, deliberately unmerged so these eleven could ship against a known sha. `73ddd5a1` step 2 is the reporter's own data entry. Three items await their answer (`bb2b2e86`, `4ca06dea`, `00e28308`). The `unpayablePayMode` screen/server mismatch and the missing `pay_period.statutory_version` were **raised, not fixed** — both sit on the money path and both are the reporter's call.

## r335 (2026-09-24) — two items, and both corrected something I had written. `main@6281abb3`, no migration.

Closed: `0fe1ca2e` (rev 6), `6af80f5d` (rev 2). Gate: **971 files — equal to the suite file count**, 14 chunks, ~15,040 tests, **zero red chunks on the first pass**, `tsc` 0, `next build` 0. No shadow gate: no migration, journal verified unchanged at 399 entries / max idx 486. Render check clean.

### `6af80f5d` — MY BRIEF CONTRADICTED ITSELF, AND THE BUILD CAUGHT IT

I wrote "round the DISPLAY field only — `currentYearEntitlement`" and, two paragraphs later, "the SUM must use the exact figure (to tile)". **`currentYearEntitlement` is not a display field.** `core/read.ts` builds `totalEntitlement` from it; `entitlement-panel-config.ts` lists it in `RECONCILIATION_ADDENDS` with `sign: 1`, where `reconciledBalance(b)` must equal `b.balance`; `lib/leave-summary-explain.ts` builds the HR sentences and the Total formula from it. Rounding it is exactly what my second instruction forbids. I verified the addend membership directly before merging.

Resolved by the repo's own r313 `DisplayEntitlement` precedent: a new `currentYearEntitlementRounded`, **required rather than optional** in both mirror types, so no hand-built breakdown can silently fall back to the unrounded figure.

**And it explained why 11.18 exists at all** — worth telling the reporter: `accrueEarnedLeave` *already* rounds at source (b81d3c52), but tops up by `toGrant = earnedToDate − already` behind a `toGrant > 0` guard, the forward-only contract. Days credited **before** a rounding table was configured are never clawed back, so the cycle keeps its raw running total. A display fix is the only answer that does not rewrite ledger rows.

Mutation B (rounding `cycleAccrual` at source) fires both named invariant guards: *"totalEntitlement is byte-identical with the rounding rule on and off — expected 11 to be 11.18"* and *"Σ(addends · sign) still equals the balance — expected 6 to be 6.18"*.

### `0fe1ca2e` — IT CLOSED A COVERAGE GAP MY BRIEF ASSUMED EXISTED

`test/clocking-map.dom.test.tsx` drove a **hand-built look-alike `<form>`**, never `ClockingLocationForm`. So **no test in the suite could have caught the address search leaving the form's subtree** — trap 1, and the one failure mode that is silent, because `form-bridge` finds its inputs through the enclosing form.

A new describe mounts the real component. Mutation (d) renders the search outside the form and fails with *"the address the search wrote: expected '' to be 'Menara KL…'"* **while the other 11 DOM tests stay green** — demonstrating the old harness's blindness rather than asserting it.

Order is asserted by **measured index** in the stripped markup, not by presence (a presence check passes on today's layout too), and the search is anchored on its `aria-label` read out of `en.json` rather than a hardcoded English sentence.

Two of the three things the reporter asked for were **already built** since r279 — the search already filled Address/Latitude/Longitude and already sat above Latitude. The real complaint was the card boundary between them, and the plan said so rather than claiming credit for building them.

### OPERATIONAL

- **The gate ran under heavy swap pressure** — 146 s on chunk 1 against a 124 s baseline, load ~17–20, ~5 GB swap in use after 1M+ swapouts across two days. Still green first pass.
- **Three builders stall this machine; two do not.** Two agents were lost to the 600 s watchdog earlier in the session at *lighter* load than the gate ran at. The working limit is two concurrent builders, and the gate alone.

### WHAT WAS NOT DONE

- **Six items approved and unbuilt**: `1bb09a73` and `3783fd87` (building at the time of writing), `20f6c6a8`, `7f251381`, `99b2d6c0`, `da7463b4`.
- **`8d3a7bff` planned**: the second "Special Leave" card is **Compassionate Leave** drawing on the Special Leave pot — measured, and it must NOT be removed. `lib/shared-leave-balance.ts`'s header records why the borrower tells the pool's story.
