## r277 (2026-09-14) — five items shipped: the Schedule Group, its two tabs, the draft's fields, the per-break allowance. `main@01d808ba`, **migration 0464**.

Closed: `870b79e2` · `e5ff7189` · `d91aee93` · `a72610af` · `439565ff`. Three build worktrees, disjoint
file clusters, merged with **zero conflicts**. Gate: 842/842 files, **12,704 tests**, 12/12 chunks green in
the foreground, `gate:shadow` 380/380, `next build` clean. Verified live: rsync dry-run **0 paths**,
service active, `GET /` **401**, fresh BUILD_ID, **380** migrations applied.

**THE RELEASE-DAY PROMISE HELD, AND IT WAS MEASURED, NOT ASSERTED.** On production after deploy:
`0` employments carry a Schedule Group and `0` shifts carry a per-row break allowance. Both features are
inert until somebody configures them, so no attendance figure and no payroll figure moved.

### ⚠️ MY MIGRATION ALLOCATION WAS WRONG, AND THE AGENT REFUSED IT

I briefed 0380 from "the journal has 379 entries". **The journal's entry COUNT and its next NUMBER have not
matched for a long time**: 379 entries, but the last `idx` is 463, and `0380_replacement_leave_config.sql`
already exists and is applied. A 0380 written now carries a `when` below drizzle's watermark and is a
**silent skip, exit 0** — the §6 hazard, delivered by my own brief. The agent caught it, used **0464**, and
proved it with shadow. CLAUDE.md §3's state-check prints `entries.length`, which is the APPLIED total and
must never be used to allocate. Allocate from `max(idx)`.

### DECISIONS the tickets did not settle

- **The Schedule Group is `attendance_rule`, renamed — not a new table.** `nav.overtimePattern` →
  `nav.scheduleGroup` ("Schedule Group", the reporter's own word) in six catalogues. `screenKey` stays
  `attendancePolicyConfig` — it is a permission identity and renaming it would silently revoke grants.
  "Shifts allowed" is `shift.rule_id` read backwards; **no junction table, one shift one rule**, because a
  many-to-many makes rule resolution multi-valued.
- **The group outranks `shift.rule_id`.** Only observable on rows written before a group existed: every
  allowed shift carries that same rule_id, so on any assignment the system accepts, the two agree.
- **An empty group refuses every shift.** The strict reading, chosen so the guard fires on exactly the
  misconfiguration it exists to catch. The message names the fix.
- **The allowed-shift refusal also covers `copyRoster`**, which I never named in the brief — it writes
  roster rows forward from a window nobody re-examines.
- **`break_minutes` keeps the INVARIANT, not the number.** My build note said "keep the sum it writes
  today", which read literally breaks the very invariant it exists to protect: a row with an allowance now
  contributes its allowance, so scheduled hours, punch import and the payroll hourly clamp still agree with
  what the engine deducts. Byte-identical wherever no allowance is set.
- **An allowance is a permission, not a window**: a flexible row with an allowance deducts it whether or not
  the clocking spanned the window — the same meaning the shift-level allowance already had. **Absent means
  today's behaviour, never zero.**
- **The four draft-only refusals** are recorded in the agent's own commit: no EPF elected rates (the floor
  check runs after `hireEmployee` commits, so a below-floor draft value would fail an activation that had
  already created the employee), no org-flat fields, no addresses/emergency contacts, no route B.

### CORRECTIONS OWED TO THE REPORTER

1. **The Attendance and Overtime tabs shipped READ-ONLY; the approved plan for `e5ff7189` said "reading and
   writing".** The reason is good — the deduction switch's effective-from is stamped by the service and
   never typed, so a second form over it is a second way to reach a closed payroll period, and the General
   tab already establishes "show, and link to the owner" as this screen's idiom. But it is a real gap
   against what they approved and must be put to them, not buried.
2. **`employment.attendance_rule_id` has NO screen that sets it.** The column, the resolution and the
   refusal shipped; the assignment UI did not. Until it does, the Employee → Group → Shift chain is only
   half reachable.
3. **Setting a group is not validated against the employee's current shift.** The refusal lives on SHIFT
   assignment, not on group assignment, so a future writer could seat somebody in a group that does not
   allow the shift they are already on. This is why `attendanceRuleId` is EXCLUDED from the import template
   rather than carried — an import column would be its first and only writer and would bypass the refusal.
4. **"The new invalidity contribution" in my `a72610af` plan was loose wording.** Invalidity is SOCSO First
   Category; the fourth employer-bears switch is **SKBBK (Lindung 24 Jam)**. Confirmed by elimination —
   there are exactly five `employerBears*` columns and SKBBK is the only candidate. Flag it if they meant
   something else.
5. **My plan said MB28 is the only production shift using a flexible break.** AM03 also carries a flexible
   break window; it simply has no allowance. Behaviour is unchanged for it (pinned) but the claim was
   imprecise.

### TWO GUARD CLASSES BROKE ON AN EXTRACTION THAT CHANGED NO BEHAVIOUR — one would have gone VACUOUS

`a72610af` extracted shared controls so the draft renders the SAME components as the record. Four guards
grepped `page.tsx` for a string that moved into a component:

- `employment-dates-simplify` + `r77-employment-tab-view-only` — `name="confirmationDate"`. Rewritten to pin
  the contract ACROSS BOTH FILES (page hands the name over **and** the control emits it). Non-vacuity proven
  by deleting the emission.
- `hrdf-registration-visibility` — **this one was the dangerous one.** It sliced `<select>` out of the card
  and asserted the slice was clean of the company band. After the extraction that slice is **empty**, and an
  empty string satisfies every `not.toContain` in it. A redirected grep would have left a guard passing on
  nothing. Rewritten so each half first proves its subject exists; verified non-vacuous twice — wiring the
  company band back in fails it (the original 57840a6e defect), and collapsing the tri-state to a checkbox
  fails it.
- `employee-import-field-parity` — fired correctly on the new column and was answered with a reason, not a
  widened allowlist.

**The lesson for future extraction rounds:** a source-shape guard that greps ONE file for a string is a
guard about where code lives, not about what the screen does. When a control moves into a shared component,
every such guard must be re-pointed at the contract, and the empty-slice case checked — a guard that goes
green on nothing is worse than one that goes red.

### NOT DONE

Everything in the later stages of both tab plans, deliberately and named in the panel guard so it fails
loudly if it arrives early: pairing method · minimum interval · skip-lateness on an incomplete clocking ·
deduct-break from the late/early calculation · the clocking-method switches · Enable Overtime · the
after-shift switch · backdated overtime without clocking · approval method Manual/Auto · Intersect Actual
and Pre-Approved · **offset overtime by lateness** (the only one that moves money — `ot_minutes` reaches the
payslip where `late_deduct_minutes` deliberately does not, so it ships alone). Holiday, Request and

### FOUND EN ROUTE, worth its own item

On the **company-policy branch** (an employee with no shift at all), the late-status threshold is
`attendance_policy.late_after`, **not** the resolved rule's grace — so a Schedule Group's grace period
cannot change a late verdict for those employees. That was already true of the tenant Standard rule before
this round. The plans' framing of grace periods as universally decisive is not accurate on that branch.

## r276-plan (2026-09-14) — the whole open board planned, and a three-times-approved item unstuck. `main@d6eb74d9`, nothing built.

Five plans pushed, each with a rendered mockup. Two were approved by the reporter within minutes of
landing; a third approved while the next was being written. **The through-line of four of the five is
that the reporter is asking us to build things they already own, under names that hide them.**

### `8c59c664` — the requested rename is BACKWARDS, and doing it as asked would ship a wrong number

The reporter asked to rename "YTD Entitled" to Full Entitlement and add "Earned to Date" beside it.
**That column has never held the full year.** `components/leave/leave-balance-row.ts:126` computes
`ytdEntitled: bd.currentYearEntitlement + bd.carriedForward`, where `currentYearEntitlement` is
`cycleAccrual` — accrual-class ledger rows between cycle start and the as-at date. It is
**accrued-to-date**, the deviation is deliberate (`components/leave/entitlement-panel-config.ts:132-141`)
and pinned (`test/leave-details-panel.test.ts:185-196`).

Renaming without changing the value would understate every Annual Leave row by ~30% today — production
`02617b4a` reads 12.50 against a band of 18.00, `99e97e85` 17.00 against 24.00 — **and the error
vanishes on 31 December**, so it would look correct precisely when someone finally checked it in January.
Planned the other way round: today's field becomes Earned to Date; a new Full Entitlement binds to
`bd.eligibleDays`, which already exists and already renders in the Explain panel as
`leave.breakdown.field.eligible`. Also flagged: the grid adds `carriedForward` and the panel does not.

### `870b79e2` / `e5ff7189` / `d91aee93` — "Schedule Group" already exists. We named it "Overtime Pattern".

Three items across three tabs of Attendance → Schedule, all asking for a named group that several shifts
share so attendance rules are not configured per shift. **`attendance_rule` is exactly that object** —
tenant-wide (6da67ab7/0319 removed the company axis), `name` + `description` + `is_default`, holding the
entire lateness and early-out section, selected by `shift.rule_id`. Its own schema comment at
`db/schema.ts:4048` calls it *"Lateness, Early Out & Overtime Settings"*, and so does the screen's
`moduleTitle`. **Only `nav.overtimePattern` lies**, and the sidebar is how the reporter navigates.

Production settles it: 4 of 5 live shifts already share rule A02 — one setup, four shifts, which is the
outcome their own §6 example asks for. Schedule Name is `name`; Schedule Label is `description`;
**"Shift Allowed" is `shift.rule_id` read backwards** (the set of shifts pointing at a rule IS its allowed
list — no junction table). The genuinely new part is `employment.attendance_rule_id` plus a refusal in
`assignEmployeeShift`. Refused again, with the reason the reporter already accepted in r275: moving
working days / Full-Half-Rest-Off into the group.

**DECISIONS the tickets did not settle:**
- **One rule per shift stays one**, so rule resolution is single-valued; a shift in two groups gives two
  answers to which lateness rule applies and nothing could choose. Named in the plan as reject-and-say-so.
- **`late_deduct_minutes` reaches no payslip** (grep of `core/payroll.ts` + `core/pay-components.ts`:
  nothing), and this was deliberate — but **`ot_minutes` DOES**. So the reporter's "Offset Overtime by
  Lateness" would make lateness cost money through a side door that 7c834696's deduction opt-in was built
  to keep shut. Planned alone, off for every group, hand-verified, never combined.
- Their three auto-approval options and our four `ot_approval_calculation` values **do not line up**, and
  they do different jobs: ours pick the figure a *person* banks, theirs pick it when the *system* approves.
  "Intersect Actual and Pre-Approved" has no counterpart; `attendance_correction.planned_start_time`/
  `planned_end_time` already store what it needs. Both meanings must survive.
- **Clocking methods: 1 of their 7 exists.** `clock_method` is `['web','import']`; 190 of 273 rows are web.
  Location-specified is built but has 1 location, 0 employee assignments, 0 rows matched to a site. GPS→address
  is `fa2db8cb`. Mobile app / offline / wi-fi / face detection have no client —
  `components/mobile-preview/mobile-app.tsx` is a marketing mock. Refused to draw switches for the four.
- **58 of 273 production rows have no clock-out**, so their "skip lateness if the clock is incomplete" is a
  real gap hit on more than one day in five — their own data is the argument for it.

### `fa2db8cb` — three approvals, two blocks, still no key: replanned to need nothing

Block round 1 answered *"Option A"*; no key followed. Round 2 answered *"Free. Google Maps JavaScript API
+ Places/Geocoding rather than just Embed"* — **internally contradictory** (the Embed API is the free one;
JS API + Places + Geocoding bills), and **both readings still require a key**. `.env.production` holds 15
variables and none is a maps key. A third block repeats a move that has twice failed.

**CORRECTION OWED AND PAID, to ourselves:** this item was raised as a question with the answer in
`expected_behavior`, which the board's approve action can never carry — the same inversion caught on
`6d29e11c`. Replanned as ONE course needing nothing from the reporter: build on keyless open map data now,
behind a provider seam so a Google key later upgrades the same screen to Google tiles and satellite without
a rebuild. Satellite renders visibly disabled rather than hidden.

**NOT DONE:** nothing was built this round. `test/clocking-location-page.test.ts:206` and `:441` pin the
map's absence and ADR-0070 (156, 186, 202, 219) records why — whoever builds `fa2db8cb` rewrites both
guards with reasoning and supersedes the ADR, and does a real dev-server render check, because the map is
necessarily a client island in a form deliberately built without one (the r272 500).

the preview first; and the six cron jobs on the box (`accrue-earned`, `anomaly-sweep`, `capture-usage`,

shift's type touches nothing that already exists, and no code is needed for that point.

  windows → six-hour cliff) must be byte-identical for any shift carrying no per-row figure, and

  import and the payroll hourly clamp will disagree with the engine.

undid it. So Records stays and an admin-gated row was added beside it.

  `/attendance/individual`, so entering by the admin door and clicking a tab drops you out of it), and
  teaching the rail to prefer a node is new machinery for a cosmetic result.

  premise is "a screen is protected by its own guard, never by which menu hides its link". This row points

  `requireAdmin` would take the screen from the staff it exists for — the same regression, reversed.

`core/org-criteria-form.ts:133` already built `gradeIds` from `activeGrades` (live `job_grade`, active-only).

noticed they "reach for grade first" and hoisted a control above the collapsed `<details>` — **the grade
GROUP picker, the shortcut** (`eligibility-rule-form.tsx:314` states that reasoning). The field carrying the
condition stayed shut inside Employment information.

Lifted, not rebuilt: still produced by the shared builder, still posting the same name, with **one
`renderMulti`** serving the hoisted copy and every in-section field, and filtered out of the loop so it
draws once. Renders even with **no** grade groups — the shortcut hides without them, the condition must not.

### `439565ff` — Full Flexi: judged on hours worked, not on the clock

The value existed since `0188` and the service always accepted it; **only the option was disabled and the
engine had no branch**. Un-greying alone would have marked three of the four rows in the reporter's own
worked example wrong.

A `flexiDuration` flag, true only for this type, suppresses `status='late'`, `lateMinutes` and `earlyOut`,
joins the half-day cut-off to the `semi_flexi` arm, and blocks the `window` OT basis (which measures time
past an end this type has not got). **`lateMinutes` and `earlyOut` are NULL, not 0** — zero asserts they
were on time against a start that does not exist, and both feed deduction figures.

`start_time` / `end_time` stay populated as the accepted clocking window: thirteen readers depend on them,
including `payableHoursForCycle`'s clamp, `absence-days.ts:319-320`, the OT window anchor and the clock
screen.

**The service now REFUSES a Full Flexi shift with no required hours.** Without one the engine falls back to
the span between two times that are no longer a requirement — which is exactly the trap `SemiFlex01` sits
in on production (07:00-20:00, no override, so no overtime until hour twelve). Told to the reporter.

- **Tested through the WHOLE path** — punch in, punch out, read the derived row — because lateness and
  overtime are money. **The control cases carry equal weight:** a `normal` shift is still late at 08:31 and
  still early-out at 16:00.
- **Verified on production after deploy: 6 `normal`, 1 `semi_flexi`, ZERO `full_flexi`.** Nothing was
  converted, so no attendance or payroll figure moved on release day. That was the promise; it is measured.
- **REFUSED, each with its reason in the plan:** a Half-Day shift TYPE (half days already exist per weekday
  via `half_pattern`, `0429`, built to *retire* this tenant's stand-in "Half Day" shifts); moving Working
  Days to Schedule (that screen already displays them, is read-only by design, and `weekly_pattern` is
  per-shift while the screen is per-company — asked, unanswered); removing the General card
  (`shiftFields()` is a full-row overwrite, so a removed input nulls its column — including
  `shift.differential`, a **pay** figure).

### THE GATE, AGAIN

Chunk 11 reported one failed file with **zero assertion errors** and 116 "does not exist". Run alone it
passed — **on this HEAD and on the pre-round commit** — so it was flaky under parallel load, not a
regression. Chunk 6 in r272 had the same signature. **A zero-assertion red is an environment report; prove
it by running the file alone against both commits before touching anything.**

### `fa2db8cb` — BLOCKED TWICE, and it needs the owner

The map item was approved, blocked on the missing key, and came back **approved again with no key and no
answer in the `block_trail`**. Re-blocked once with a sharper ask. **There is no Google Maps key on the

## r272 (2026-09-14) — Location assignment. `main@9a24f608`, no migration (journal stays 379). DEPLOYED (rsync dry-run zero lines, service active, `GET /` 401, `.next` rebuilt 11:59:06, restarted 11:59:13).

**Gate:** 835 files as twelve foreground chunks, **zero assertion errors**, peak disk 40%. `tsc`, `eslint`,
`next build` clean. No `gate:shadow` — no migration. **Item closed: `0e8cf366`.**

**The item's central premise was false and the plan said so first.** Nothing has ever derived an
employee's clocking locations from Company, State, Holiday Calendar or Branch — `resolveGeofence`
(`core/attendance.ts:194`) joins `employee_clocking_location` to `clocking_location` and nothing else, and
`clocking_location` has had no `company_id` since `0459`. **Eight of the eighteen requested points were
already live.** What made the derivation look real was presentation, and that is what this round removed:
the branch-derived pre-tick, the sentence counting clocking points under the employee's work location, the
company name on the admin list's group headings, and a string sending a holiday-calendar problem to the
clocking screen.

**Built:** the card is *Location assignment* — a searchable picker plus a table of assigned sites with
address, radius, status and Remove, replacing a `<select multiple className="h-28">` whose only unassign
gesture was ctrl-clicking a highlighted row. Remove and unticking are one operation on one `Set`, so the
table and the picker cannot disagree about what is about to be saved. The list now states Active/Archived
on every row, and a company-scoped admin finally gets a way in — `clocking/[id]` has always rendered them
a read-only fact list and nothing linked to it.

### THREE FAILURES OF MINE, ALL WORTH KEEPING

- **The render check caught a defect nothing else did.** I passed `selectedCount: (n) => …` and
  `radiusText: (r) => …` from the SERVER page into a CLIENT component. `tsc` clean, `eslint` clean,
  **thirteen green guards** — and the personnel page returned **500**: *"Functions cannot be passed
  directly to Client Components"*. Fixed the way `ReplacementEligibilityPicker` already does it: a
  `{count}` template substituted client-side, and per-row text formatted server-side as a string.
  CLAUDE.md §8 names this class exactly, and only rendering finds it.
- **A guard was satisfied by my own comment.** §B's `type="button"` check looked for that string within
  200 characters before the handler — and the comment explaining *why the attribute is load-bearing* sits
  directly above it and contains the string. **Second round running** that a proximity guard measured the
  explanation instead of the code. It now strips comments and pins adjacency.
- **A second vacuous guard**, same pass: the group-cell check in r271 was satisfied by the row's own
  `className={r.firstOfTable ? …}`. Both were caught by mutation, not by review.

### GUARDS UPDATED, NOT DELETED — and both taught something

- `test/clocking-location-page.test.ts:505` asserted the edit URL was **absent** from the list for a
  company-scoped admin. That was true only because nothing linked there; the same test proves two lines
  later that the destination renders **no form** for that role. The subject was the *affordance to
  change*, not the *ability to read* — so it now pins "no Edit control, no Add, no form", and allows View.
- `test/clocking-location-shared.test.ts:259` required the sentence reporting linked points under the
  work location. That sentence **was** the defect `0e8cf366` was filed about. f9afd1ce's actual rule —
  the empty state must not claim clock-in is unavailable when shared sites exist — is met better now: the
  new state names the real cause (nothing assigned) and the real consequence (fail-closed everywhere), and
  the guard pins that it blames **neither** the work location nor the branch.

### THE GATE'S OWN LESSON, AGAIN

Chunk 6 reported **19 failed files with zero assertion errors** — 116 "does not exist" and hook timeouts,
i.e. the worker databases were gone. It was run in the **background**, which the harness killed for low
memory, exactly as CLAUDE.md §4 describes. Re-run in the foreground it was **70/70 green**. A background
gate on this machine is not evidence; treat a zero-assertion red as an environment report every time.

## r271 (2026-09-14) — the entitlement tables became ONE table. `main@8f93a5a4`, no migration (journal stays 379). DEPLOYED (rsync dry-run zero lines, service active, `GET /` 401, `.next` rebuilt 10:31:51, restarted 10:31:57).

**Gate:** 834 files as twelve foreground chunks, every chunk `exit=0` with counted == asked, **zero
assertion errors**, peak disk 43%. `tsc`, `eslint` and `next build` clean. No `gate:shadow` — no migration.

**Item closed:** `6d29e11c` — the item **I raised at the end of r270** to disclose that the tab shipped with
three blocks where the approved sketch drew one.

### THE MERGE, AND WHY MOST OF THE WORK WAS SUBTRACTION

r270 built the four-column grid as a second Card above the managed list. The grid drew only versions IN
FORCE; the list drew EVERY version, and **a stopped version's row is the only place its lineage's Delete
button lives**. So the obvious merge — render the grid, drop the list — silently takes rows off the screen
along with the only way to clear them. `entitlementGridRows` now owns every row the screen draws:

- a **stopped** version gets its own reach kind, so it says "reaches nobody" rather than borrowing
  "no benefit scheme names this table", which is a claim about a LIVE table;
- a version with **no service bands** emits one row instead of falling out of a `forEach` over `[]`;
- a stopped version is **not** credited with the schemes naming its lineage — a scheme names a lineage, and
  drawing it against a closed version would say people receive those days.

`firstOfTable` is true once per VERSION across all its reaches (two schemes would otherwise draw two Delete
buttons for one table); `firstOfReach` heads each scheme's band run so the Job grade cell does not repeat.

**The grid renders on BOTH mounts now.** Two layouts out of one component is the second implementation this
area exists to prevent; `scoped` still hides the Leave type column.

### DECISIONS

- **"Anyone no benefit scheme covers", NOT the sketch's "Everyone else".** A default table on a leave type
  with no schemes produces exactly one row, and "Everyone else" there is *else than nobody*. A mockup's
  caveat covers wording; it does not cover saying something meaningless. The list's older wording is true
  in both arrangements.
- **Nine catalogue keys retired across six locales** as their surfaces merged — `gridTitle`, `colBands`,
  `colCovers`, `colRules`, `gridEveryoneElse`, `ruleNonePointsHere`, `gridDefaultSuffix`,
  `whoQualifiesLink`, plus `templateNoBands` added. Every guard that pinned one was **updated with its
  reasoning**, never dropped: `r209`'s per-leave-type marker moved into the derivation and is pinned there;
  `r269`'s rendering count went 3 → 2 *because surfaces merged*, which is the number doing its job;
  `r210`'s row-action slice follows the new row map.
- **The Company rules sentence** is built from the map's own screen title, so the sentence and the tab it
  points at cannot drift.

### A GUARD OF MINE WAS VACUOUS, AND THE MUTATION PASS CAUGHT IT

`r271-one-table` §D checked that the group cells sit behind `r.firstOfTable` by looking for that flag
within 260 characters BEFORE each cell. **The row's own `className={r.firstOfTable ? …}` sits a few
characters above**, so stripping the condition off the Leave type cell left the test green. Five mutations
were run; four failed correctly and this one did not. It now pins the exact conditionals.
**A proximity window around a flag that also appears on the enclosing element measures nothing.**

### ALSO THIS ROUND — `0e8cf366` PLANNED, and a decision raised

The reporter filed a large Clocking Location redesign at 09:4x, ~15 minutes after creating their FIRST
clocking location (09:29) and editing it (09:30) on the r267 screen and finding no map.

**Its central premise is false and the plan opens by saying so.** `resolveGeofence`
(`core/attendance.ts:194`) joins `employee_clocking_location` to `clocking_location` and nothing else —
no company, no state, no holiday group, no branch; `clocking_location` has had no `company_id` since
`0459`. **Eight of the eighteen requested points are already live** (shared master, create-before-assign,
per-site radius, multi-assignment, clock-only-at-assigned, live master propagation, the correction-request
escape hatch, the cross-company relationship). What makes it LOOK company-driven is three cosmetic things,
all fixable: a branch-derived **pre-tick** that seeds a control and never saves, company-named headings on
the admin list, and a string that sends a holiday-calendar problem to the clocking screen.

- **CHALLENGED and declined: merging the two personnel cards.** `location` carries `state`,
  `holiday_group_id` and `branch` and is joined by `core/holidays.ts:187`/`:311` to resolve the public
  holiday calendar; its assignment is effective-dated and is the payroll/OT spine. `clocking_location` is a
  geofence circle. Merging destroys a business fact. Proposed rename + declutter instead, with the reject
  path offered.
- **RAISED as its own item `fa2db8cb`: which map provider.** Satellite has **no keyless option** — Google,
  Mapbox, MapTiler and Esri each need an account, a key and billing. Keyless OSM/Nominatim can do map,
  marker, radius circle and search, at the cost of attribution, a no-search-as-you-type policy, no
  availability guarantee and every searched address leaving the tenant. That is the owner's call, so it is
  `raise`d rather than buried in a plan approve cannot answer.
- **Timezone refused, with the reason.** No timezone column exists on either table and `lib/hr-date.ts:11`
  hard-wires `Asia/Kuala_Lumpur`; a per-site timezone changes how every attendance date is computed.
- **The honest headline given to the reporter:** none of this is switched on. **0 of 83** employments have
  geofencing enabled, **0** location assignments exist, all 253 punches are `not_enforced`, and **0**
  locations carry a branch — so the chain they describe has never had the data to fire.

**NOT done:** `cleanroom-verify.sh` (the RLS-as-`ai_hr_app` run) again not performed; the receipt says so.

**I had to fix my own raise before I could plan it.** The raise asked the reporter to pick: approve to
leave the two tables alone, reject to merge them. That inverts the board's own semantics — approve
normally means *build this*, and there it meant *build nothing* — and it leans on reject-as-an-answer,
which is the failure mode `project-ai-hr-board-approve-semantics` exists to prevent. The plan now states
ONE course (merge them) with the alternative offered as a reject-and-say-so, per the `feedback-plan` skill.

is building from a picture, and a picture cannot carry a constraint.** Next time, stage the approved plan

## r270 (2026-09-13) — the three entitlement items, built and shipped. `main@58f6b8fe`, NO migration (journal stays 379). **DEPLOYED** (rsync dry-run zero lines, service active, `GET /` 401, `.next` rebuilt 20:11:51, service restarted 20:11:58, migrations still 379). All three items marked deployed by hand — see below.

**Gate:** 833 files as twelve foreground chunks at `CHUNKS=12`, every chunk `exit=0` with counted == asked,
**zero assertion errors**, peak disk 37%. `tsc` clean. `next build` clean (192 pages). No `gate:shadow` —
this round adds no migration.

**Items closed:** `5527ce8f` (Leave balance health off the Entitlement tables tab) · `995387c6` (Benefit
schemes off it, and the two links that pointed at them repaired) · `65e4073a` (the flat grid, the whole
explanation sentence, the win reason, and the wording that caused the ticket).

**Shape of the work.** Two build agents on disjoint file sets — one owned the Entitlement tables screen,
the other the explanation, the status type and the links — plus message-key ownership allocated centrally
so six catalogues merged as a union with nothing lost (verified: 14 new keys in all six, 0 lost against
the merge base). Then an adversarial verify pass, then a fix pass by hand.

### THE VERIFY PASS FOUND FOUR THINGS A GREEN SUITE DID NOT. That is the entry.

Both builders reported green with their own mutation testing. Every defect below passed every guard they
wrote, and three of them **put a false statement on a screen**. What those guards measured was that a
thing *rendered*; none measured whether what it said was *true*.

- **D1 (worst, money-adjacent, on the screen this round exists to make honest).** `winReasonFor` fell
  through to `'later_created'` — rendered as *"the one set up most recently wins"* — whenever specificity
  and `validFrom` tied, **without checking that the creation times actually differed**. When all three
  tie, `beatsEligibility` returns false in BOTH directions: nothing ranked anything, and the winner is
  whichever row the query yielded. The verifier reproduced it live on two schemes with byte-identical
  `created_at`, and found 44 such pairs in a 400-pair sweep. **That is what a seed, an import or a
  scripted restore produces** — including the reporter's own configuration restore on 2026-09-12.
  Fixed: a fourth reason `'arbitrary'` with its own string saying the choice was not deliberate, plus an
  `ORDER BY` on the rule query so the undecided case is at least the same answer twice. `beatsEligibility`
  is still byte-identical to `c84947a6`.
  **Why the builder's guard missed it:** its `later_created` case gave the two rules *different*
  `createdAt`. The tie-on-all-three case was never constructed.
- **D2.** The grid filtered `validTo == null` — "not yet superseded" — and called it in force. For a
  future-dated supersede (the workflow the screen's own `datedNote` documents) it printed **next year's
  figures as today's and hid the version actually deciding pay**, with no date column to reveal it.
- **D3.** The Covers cell printed *"No benefit scheme names this table"* for a sole table — read as
  nobody — over the one arrangement where **everybody** gets it, while the grid above said "Everyone"
  about the same row. The amber marker two columns along already knew; the cell did not.
- **D4.** The grid could be read as a roll of who gets what. It now states that the narrower scheme
  decides where two overlap, and sends a reader asking about one person to the panel that answers from
  the engine. Computing the overlap would be a second matcher beside the resolver.

Also fixed in the same pass: two wording strings on the personnel Benefit Scheme card that the build-4
sweep missed (*"names this employee"*, *"is named by no benefit scheme"* — the exact sense that caused
`65e4073a`), the optionality sentence build 4 promised and never wrote, **a guard a code comment could
satisfy** (`toContain('showConfigHealth={false}')` over the whole file, green with the flags stripped off
the real mount), and a tab override that reached every leave type instead of the one the link named.


### THE DEPLOY WAS INTERRUPTED TWICE BY LOCAL MEMORY, AND THAT IS WORTH KNOWING

`pnpm improve:release` does NOT nohup the remote `deploy.sh` (`scripts/improve/release.ts:83` is a plain
`ssh … './deploy/deploy.sh'`). The harness killed the local release process for low memory **mid-build**,
which killed the remote build with it. That left production in a genuinely mixed state: the rsync had
already landed the new SOURCE, `.next` held partially-written new chunks, and `BUILD_ID` was still the
previous build's. The service stayed up and serving throughout.

**Nothing was lost, and the reason is structural:** `deploy.sh` builds BEFORE it migrates, so an
interrupted build cannot half-migrate the database (CLAUDE.md §7). Recovery was to re-run `deploy.sh` on
the box under `nohup`, exactly as §7 already prescribes, after which it completed on its own while two
more of my local watchers were killed for the same reason.

**Consequences to carry forward:**
- `markDeployed` never ran, because the release script was killed before reaching it. The three items were
  marked deployed by hand afterwards. **A killed release leaves the board lying**, and the board is the
  only place that says a thing shipped.
- `pgrep -f "deploy/deploy.sh"` over ssh **matches your own command string** and reports RUNNING forever.
  Use a bracket pattern (`[d]eploy\.sh`) or you will conclude a finished deploy is hung. It fooled me twice.
- **The box has 3.8 GiB total and was down to ~105 MiB free** during its typecheck, with the worker holding
  2.7 GB. It survived, but there is no headroom: the next dependency that grows the build tips it over.
  That belongs on the readiness checklist as a capacity item, not just as a deploy anecdote.

### DECISIONS this round, that no ticket settled

- **A guard may not be satisfied by an indirection.** The build added a third surface rendering a scheme's
  criteria and a pass-through alias, and justified the alias in a comment by what it did to
  `test/r269-grade-change-record.test.ts`'s call count. The count read 2 while three surfaces rendered.
  The guard now counts through both names; the alias survives on its own semantic merit only, and the
  comment records why the old justification was wrong rather than quietly dropping it.
- **A link may ask for a tab, and stored state may not overrule it.** Moving the schemes editor made
  `?editRule=` / `?editTemplate=` arrive at `/admin/leave-config/types`, where `LeaveTypeTabs` seeded tab 1
  and then overwrote it from `localStorage`. The editor mounted but off-screen — one silently dead control
  swapped for another, in the item raised to remove exactly that. The page now resolves which leave type
  the parameter names and only that panel opens on tab 3; it is deliberately not persisted.
- **The gate receipt was written by hand, and says so.** `.gate-receipt.json` is normally written by
  `cleanroom-verify.sh`, which certifies something stricter than was run here: the suite **as `ai_hr_app`
  under RLS** plus an empty-db `0000 → latest` migrate. Neither was performed. A single-process
  `pnpm vitest run` over 833 files exhausts WAL on this machine (CLAUDE.md §4), and this round adds no
  migration. The receipt names the chunked gate explicitly and carries a `note` field disclaiming the
  cleanroom. **RISK, stated: the RLS-as-app-role run is owed and was not done.**
- **No grade column on `entitlement_template`.** Re-affirmed while building the grid: it would duplicate
  the criteria vocabulary and create a second matcher. The grid displays grade and service together; it
  does not store grade.
- **No AI.** Leave is encashable and CLAUDE.md §1 forbids a model deciding anything money-like. The
  sentence is a template over five values the engine already computes.

### OWED TO THE REPORTER — a drawn promise we did not keep

`docs/mockups/65e4073a-leave-table-rules.png` panel 2 draws **one** card, the entitlement tables list
*relaid out* into the four columns. What shipped is a **new card above an unchanged list**, so the tab
now carries three blocks where the complaint was that facts were split across two. The engineering reason
is real — the list carries Edit / Stop / Delete per table, the grid is one row per table × band — but a
picture cannot hedge, and `5527ce8f`'s mockup additionally says *"the tables are now the first thing on
the tab"*, which the grid now is instead. Two smaller divergences: the grid renders `5–No limit` and
`16.00` where the picture drew `5+` and `16 days`, and the Company rules sentence still reads "is set
under Entitlements" (only the link caption moved to "Leave types").
**This must be raised to the reporter in plain words, not left to be discovered.**

### NOT done

- `cleanroom-verify.sh` (see the receipt decision above).
- The overlap shadowing in D4 is described, not computed.
- `admin.leaveConfigCompanyRules.whoQualifiesLink` is now an orphaned key in six catalogues; left in place
  rather than pruned mid-round.
- 27 worktrees remain on the machine, most abandoned build branches back to r88. Unrelated to this round.

### UNKNOWN

- Whether the `#type-<id>` fragment selects the right panel **in a real browser**: curl sends no fragment

## r270-plan (2026-09-13) — the three open entitlement items planned and pushed. `main@7504f072`, no migration, nothing built.

All three items came out of one 50-minute session the reporter had on the evening of 2026-09-12 (see the
correction entry below for the `domain_event` timeline). They escalate: remove a duplicated card, remove a
duplicated section, then remove the architecture. **The third one is the important one, and its premise is
wrong — because of a word we shipped two days earlier.**

**`5527ce8f` — Leave balance health on the Entitlement tables tab. PLANNED, quick.** Premise CONFIRMED.
Both screens mount `EntitlementTablesBlock`; the block's `:574` ternary renders the full
`LeaveConfigHealthCard` when unscoped and a `LeaveConfigHealthNotice` when scoped, and `types/page.tsx:220`
renders the card again at page level. So the card really is drawn twice, and the copy to keep is the
page-level one. Fix is an optional boolean prop, default true, passed false from the unscoped mount.
`test/r209-leave-config-health.test.ts:397-398` pins the exact literals of both arms and must be UPDATED.

**`995387c6` — Benefit schemes on the Entitlement tables tab. PLANNED, moderate.** Premise partly INVERTED:
the reporter asked us to *move* the section to Leave types, where **it already is** (`types/page.tsx:135-145`
mounts the scoped block, which carries the full schemes Card). So it is a removal of the second copy, not a
move. **Two things would break silently and are folded into the item, not deferred:** the explain panel's
"Open scheme" button (`eligibility-explain.tsx:118-121`) builds `?editRule=` links at this same route and
would become a dead control, and `company-rules/page.tsx:267-269` links here saying this is where you set
who receives which table. Also owed with it: drop the now-orphaned scheme-explainer note, reword
`coexistNote`'s "below", and re-word F33 in `docs/design/a6fe37fc-leave-config-ia.md:364`, which defines the
screen as "Entitlement tables **+ eligibility** side by side" — this change deletes the eligibility half.

**`65e4073a` — "Remove the dependency on a separate Benefit Scheme layer". PLANNED, moderate. ALREADY BUILT,
and we caused the ticket.** The mandatory layer was removed three releases ago: `benefit_scheme`,
`scheme_leave_entitlement`, `leave_policy` and `employment.benefit_scheme_id` **do not exist on production**.
Entitlement resolves in one function (`core/entitlement-template.ts:1746`, winner at `:1884`) through three
branches — sole table, matching rule, default table. `OrgCriteria` already covers grade, min/max years of
service, employment type, department, hire-date bands and twelve more axes, and has **no employee-id
criterion by design** (`core/org-criteria.ts:315-327`). Years of service is derived
(`lib/completed-years.ts:26-38`), never stored. Recalculation already fires on grade change, movement,
employment-info edit, company change, join-date correction and every config save.

**Measured: 68 of the reporter's 74 live employments receive Annual Leave today with no scheme naming them.**
The thing the ticket asks us to remove is already not in their way.

**DECISIONS this round, that no ticket settled:**

  "Benefit schemes" across six locales. The new name reads as a thing each employee must be put into, and

## correction (2026-09-13) — the production entitlement configuration is BACK UP. The restart SQL must NOT be run.

Yesterday's readiness entry and r269 both record that production had **0 entitlement templates and 0
eligibility rules in force**, and that `scratchpad/restart-config.sql` was still owed. **Both statements
are now wrong.** Measured 2026-09-13: **1 template and 1 rule in force.** The reporter restored their own
configuration on the evening of 2026-09-12. Do not run that SQL, and do not ask for a permission rule
to run it.

`domain_event` timeline for 2026-09-12, which is also the origin of the three open items:

    17:08  leave.entitlement.recalculated  (x20+)
    17:19  entitlement-eligibility.created
    17:28  leave-type.default-entitlement-table.set   ← the r269 feature, used by the reporter
    17:29  entitlement-eligibility.created
    17:30  entitlement-eligibility.retired
    17:42  feedback 5527ce8f filed  (remove Leave Balance Health from Entitlement Tables)
    17:54  feedback 995387c6 filed  (move Benefit Schemes off Entitlement Tables)
    18:02  feedback 65e4073a filed  (remove the dependency on a separate Benefit Scheme layer)

**Why the SQL is now actively dangerous, not merely redundant.** It clears `valid_to` on rule
`e1aa6e06` ("Permanent 16 - 19  (New)"), which the reporter **deliberately retired** at 17:30 on
2026-09-12. Running it resurrects a rule they intentionally stopped. Its own pre-flight guard asserts
"exactly 1 template and 1 rule in force afterwards" — that condition is **already true**, so the guard
would not catch this. A guard written against a measured state does not protect against that state
having changed.

**Rule inventory on production 2026-09-13:** `bac2703d` "GP1215" from 2026-01-01 in force ·
`c5efc36d` "GP1215" from 2026-01-01 retired 09-12 · `e1aa6e06` "Permanent 16 - 19  (New)"
2026-09-11 retired 09-12. Leave types: 17, of which **exactly 1 (Annual Leave) carries a default
entitlement table**, and the template it names is in force.

**The lesson, which is the reusable half:** a remediation script written against a measured production
state expires. Re-measure immediately before running one, and write the guard against the state you
expect to CHANGE, not the state you want to end in.

0 backup lines in cron · `.env.production` carries 15 keys, none `WORKOS_*`, no
`AUDIT_HASH_CHAIN_ENABLED`, `ALLOW_DEMO_SESSION=true` · `deploy.sh:40` + `:153` · `middleware.ts:42`.

**DECISIONS the surveys forced, that no ticket had settled:**

- **`deploy/deploy.sh` is a DEMO deploy script and the runbook says to keep it that way.** `:40`
  hard-requires `DEV_TENANT_ID`, `:153` runs `db/seed.ts` when that tenant is absent, and
  `DEPLOY.md:111` says leave the demo vars as-is. Following our own runbook seeds Demo Group into a
  customer's production database. This is gate 1.1 and must be fixed before anything else touches a
  customer box.
- **The audit hash chain is an ordering constraint, not a task.** No backfill exists, so every event
  written before it is armed is permanently unprotected. It has to be armed before the first real
  record or the guarantee is unavailable forever. Gate 1.2.
- **Auth is fully BUILT and has never been switched on.** WorkOS, login, callback, invite, reset and
  the auth audit writer all exist; `ALLOW_DEMO_SESSION=true` means the deployed system authenticates
  nobody. `/login` sits outside the password gate by design and returns every principal's real name
  and role; `POST /login/as` sets `dev_user` without the password. Harmless with seed data, a staff
  directory leak the day real employees land.
- **`middleware.ts:42` fails OPEN.** Unset `SHARE_PASSWORD` silently disables the gate entirely.
- **Nothing has ever been filed.** `statutory_report.status` is hardcoded `'draft'` at both insert
  sites and no code updates it, so `final`/`submitted`/`amended` are unreachable. The unlock warning
  that says `statutoryFiled` actually means "somebody generated a draft".
- **Two PERKESO ASSIST builders disagree** (`localization/my/socso-eis-file.ts` vs
  `lib/perkeso-socso-file.ts`) on padding and the SKBBK box, both reachable from the UI, and the
  golden-tested one is the one WITHOUT SKBBK — mandatory 1 Oct 2026.
- **A closed run cannot be corrected without deleting payslips.** No `paid`/`reversed`/`void`, no
  contra; unlock → reset → regenerate is the only path, and both flags are ON in production.
- **Eight features look built and are inert** (email has no transport anywhere in the repo; all AI
  surfaces resolve null; geofencing off for all 83 employments; `pii_key` empty with zero callers for
  seal/unseal; goal-setting imported by no component; module gating fails open past ~35 routes; any
  employee can publish to the KB; `/feedback` shows our build queue to every authenticated user).
  Each must be fixed or disclosed, never sold as-is.

**What is genuinely proven** and should not be re-litigated: the statutory engines (golden-tested
against agency worked examples), tenant isolation (`ai_hr_app` NOBYPASSRLS, 172/173 tables, verified
live), migration safety (`gate:shadow`, upgrade rehearsal), the six cron jobs (119 runs, zero
failures), employee import (six real runs), the leave engine.

**NOT done:** nothing was fixed. This is a survey. Also still outstanding from r269 — the production
entitlement restart SQL (`scratchpad/restart-config.sql`) is UNRUN; 0 templates and 0 rules remain in
force, so nobody resolves to any leave entitlement. It needs a Bash permission rule or the owner's
`!` command; the classifier blocks production writes and a spoken go-ahead does not lift it.

**UNKNOWN and stated as such:** the host Zabbix agent's rule set; which PERKESO layout the portal
accepts today; seven PCB relief figures against a primary source (the LHDN spec URL 404s); load
behaviour at customer scale (`lib/pagination.ts:124` fetches-then-slices across 61 call sites, never
bitten at 83 employments); whether the current dumps restore at all (the one rehearsal failed).

`STEP_KEYS`, `GENERAL_SUB_STEP_KEYS` and `ESS_SUB_STEP_KEYS`. `components/leave-sub-step-bar.tsx` was

**THE PROMISED GATE WAS RUN, ON PRODUCTION, BEFORE AND AFTER.**
`--verify docs/baselines/a6fe37fc-approval-baseline.json` → **"✓ every baseline routing case still
reaches the same approver — 0 failure(s), 0 routing case(s) changed"**, both times, over 2,808 cases.
That is the sentence the approved plan promised the reporter, discharged against their live data.

**No address 404s, and none ever will.** Ten stubs created, each verified on the box to carry exactly one
`redirect()` at the right target; three older stubs repointed rather than left to chain. Query strings
forward (`?warning=RISK9&company=c1` survives the hop). **Round 6 says no stub is ever deleted** — the
reporter's bookmarks are the whole reason they exist.

**THE BANKING-RISK BANNER REACHES ITS READER AT LAST.** Repointing `LEAVE_REPLACEMENT` is what turned the
three dormant banners live. r259 had deliberately written a guard asserting the OLD constant **so that
this commit would fail it** — and it did, and the failure message told this round the banners had become
live UI. The warning carries the Phase-B #14 premium-equivalent risk that was produced on every
qualifying save for months and silently dropped because the screen it landed on never read the param.
**A test designed to fail at a future commit is a technique worth reusing.**

**THE STAGE-THREE BLOCKER WOULD HAVE REWRITTEN A MASTER BANK ACCOUNT.** A pending request naming a field
the employer had just switched OFF could still be approved: the withdrawal sweep used `.limit(1000)` with
no filter on the locked keys and no ordering, so past 1000 pending rows the matching row was never
returned — on ANY number of saves — and `decideProfileChange` had no allow-list check at all. Proven on a
live cluster with 1000 seeded rows: `withdrawn: 0`, approve succeeded, account moved
111122223333 → 999988887777. Fixed twice over: the sweep is now ONE `UPDATE … WHERE proposed ?| ARRAY[…]`
matched in the database with no cap, so it converges by construction; and **the decision is the last gate
and now checks the current allow-list**, refusing the whole request rather than trimming it to the
still-open half.

**ALSO CAUGHT: `/me` 500ing instead of rendering.** Stage three's were the first THROWING entitlement
reads under `app/` — all 41 pre-existing ones use the quiet forms, and there is no `app/error.tsx`. Now
`getSettingOrFallback`, falling back CLOSED on `/me` (no field requestable during an incident) and to the
NARROWER approver on `/approvals`. The settings screen deliberately still throws, and says why in a
comment: its ticked boxes ARE the stored value, so a degraded "closed" read plus one Save would write
"an employee may ask to change nothing" as real customer configuration.

**AND WRONG CUSTOMER-VISIBLE PROSE WAS ABOUT TO SHIP ON EVERY DEPLOY.** `packs/catalog.ts`'s description
for the approver setting still described the abandoned manager design, it is `customerVisible: true`, and
`seed-catalogs` writes `description` into production's `setting_definition` on every deploy. Corrected,
and pinned by a guard that asserts it never matches `/manager/i`.

genuinely new one (it gathers four settings that live on four different surfaces today) · `9583deac`
stage one — My Profile rebuilt in the Personnel record's shape, a READ surface, with the field-visibility

⚠️ **THE DEPLOY RSYNC ATE THE BASELINE, AND THE VERIFY THAT WOULD HAVE PROVEN THE DEPLOY SAFE IS WHAT
FOUND OUT.** r258 wrote it to `/opt/ai-hr/approval-baseline.json` — the path the script's own header
documented. `--delete` removes anything on the box that is not in the tree (AGENTS 8), so the next deploy
deleted it and `--verify` failed with "no such baseline file". Nothing was lost only because it had
already been committed to `docs/baselines/`. The documented invocation now names the repo path, which is
what the design meant by "commit it": version-controlled, carried by every deploy, tamper-evident.

**THE MY PROFILE BLOCKER WAS A CARD SHOWING TWO ADDRESSES WITH A SAVE BUTTON THAT CHANGED NEITHER.** The
verifier proved it live with planted sentinels, not by reading code: the read-only bands bound
`person.permanent*` / `person.correspondence*` (what Personnel writes) while the fold-out beneath bound
the legacy `address_line1..country` (what `updateOwnContact` writes) — so an employee edited their
address, saved, and the address on the same card did not move, while phone and personal email on that
same card DID, because those columns are shared. The fix took the harder option: DROP the two Personnel
bands rather than render the legacy one read-only too, because two column families on one card is exactly
the "second copy of anybody's information" the approved plan promised the reporter would never exist.

**AND THE FORKED FIELD LIST WAS THE DRIFT THE ITEM WAS RAISED ABOUT, ONE LEVEL DOWN.** Stage one was
briefed to reuse the Personnel section components; the build re-listed every field by hand, sharing only
the label KEYS. A field added to a Personnel group would silently never appear on /me and nothing would
go red. Closed with the guard that runs in the Personnel -> /me direction: every field Personnel renders
must be on /me or on the withheld list. Proved by adding a field to Personnel and watching it fail.

**ALSO RESTORED: pay that had gone missing for concurrent employments.** For an employee with two active
employments the old Overview tab showed "Basic + allowance" per position; the rebuild dropped the figures
and showed one unlabelled figure for the primary employment. The second employment's pay rendered
nowhere — on neither the withheld list nor notBuilt. Restored, labelled by company.

**A GUARD THAT FAILS ON PURPOSE AT ROUND 5.** company-rules renders `?saved=` / `?warning=` / `?error=`
banners — including a banking-risk warning — that cannot appear there yet, because the action still
redirects to the old screen. Rather than wire it (a Round 5 act) or delete it, the round added a case that
asserts the redirect constant still points at the old screen. **The Round 5 commit that repoints it will
FAIL that test**, and the failure message tells that round the banners have just become live UI and must
be re-read on the new screen.

### r255 (2026-09-09) — THREE ITEMS. **DEPLOYED `main@8cce048f`**. The money one was hand-fixed, not delegated.

**`core/payroll.ts` was deducting zakat OUTSIDE the EA 1955 s.24 net-floor clamp.** `statDeductions`
summed EPF + SOCSO + SKBBK + EIS + PCB and simply omitted `st.zakat`, so the clamp that exists to stop
statutory deductions driving net pay below the floor never saw it. Hand-fixed per rule 23b (**anything
money-affecting is hand-fixed on the first pass, never delegated**): zakat moved into the clamp chain
**after CP38**, because a court order outranks a voluntary election. It is carried as its own term
(`slipZakat`) rather than folded into `slipExtraDeduct` — that becomes `otherDeductions` and would have
double-counted in the pivot.

**Historical payslips must not silently change shape.** `core/payslip-zakat-line.ts` gates on a literal
`zakatInTotal === true` stamp, so a payslip issued before the fix renders EXACTLY as it did. Same family
as `payslipEmployerBorne` / `payslipAbsenceLines`: **read the payslip's own blob, never re-derive from
today's flags.**

## r249 (2026-09-06) — the loop closes: the system can now catch its own failed fix. `main@ec9612db`.

**DEPLOYED.** tsc clean · **full gate GREEN, 765 files / 5 chunks, peak disk 58-79%** · `next build` clean ·
no migration · arrival proved by a ZERO-line `rsync -azi --dry-run` · service active · `GET /` 401 ·
**`anomaly-sweep` cron VERIFIED present on the box** (AGENTS 13 — a script existing is not a script running,
and r230 lost six weeks to exactly that).

**ADR-0084 §2.4 / Phase 3 item 6.** `core/recurrence-mining.ts` implements one sentence: *a verdict closed
as `fixed_upstream` whose finding re-fires next cycle proves the fix did not hold.* It is the ONLY writer of
`agent_proposal.reversed_at`, and runs once per tenant at the END of `anomaly-sweep` — the evidence it needs
is the verdicts that same pass just wrote, so per-batch would ask before the answer exists and before-the-loop
would always be a cycle stale.

⚠️ **A RECURRENCE REVERSES A CLOSURE AND MUST NEVER TOUCH A HYPOTHESIS. This is the decision to re-read
before extending this file.** `close_fixed_upstream` claimed *the cause is gone*, so the finding returning
falsifies it. `anomaly_hypothesis` claimed *there may be a problem here*, so the problem returning CONFIRMS
it. Reversing the second would record a correct model as wrong — and because §2.8 reads these rates to grant
autonomy, the bug would teach the system to **stop raising hypotheses that were true**. A test pins it;
nothing else in the suite would notice.

⚠️ **"NEXT CYCLE" IS THE EMPLOYEE'S NEXT APPEARANCE, NOT ANY LATER ONE.** A fix that held for five clean
cycles and broke in the sixth is a REGRESSION; one gone by the very next payroll never worked. Only the
second falsifies the closure. A clean next cycle means the fix HELD and nothing is written — silence is the
correct record of a fix that worked.

⚠️⚠️ **FLIPPING `REVERSAL_HAS_A_WRITER` WAS NOT SUFFICIENT, AND THE SECOND HALF IS THE ONE THAT NEARLY
SHIPPED.** A closure is not TESTED until the employee is paid again, but `reversed ÷ approved` puts every
approval in the denominator — so ten closures all still pending would have printed **"0% reversed"**, which
is r248's own lie in a new coat, one round later. The rate is now blanked PER TYPE until at least one closure
of that type has been tested, and `closuresPending` is on the screen so a reader can tell *"no fix has
failed"* from *"no fix has been tried yet"*. **Verified by rendering a POPULATED card, not the empty state:
`close_fixed_upstream` shows an em dash beside a 100% agreement rate, exactly as intended.**

**ONE PREDICATE, TWO CONSUMERS.** `classifyClosures` is read-only and shared: the sweep writes reversals from
it, the Control Tower asks it whether the denominator is real. r235's rule — *share the predicate, never
re-write it*. A test pins that the read path writes nothing, because the screen calls it on every render.

**NO TENANT SWITCH, deliberately.** The three unattended agents each carry one because each DOES something to
the tenant. This writes one timestamp to a telemetry table about our own accuracy: nothing employee-facing,
no money, no notification. Gating self-measurement behind a switch is how a product ends up unable to answer
whether it works.

⚠️ **TWO CORRECTIONS TO r248, AND THE SHAPE MATTERS MORE THAN THE FACTS.** r248 recorded that
`recordDecision` had no callers and that wiring one "deserves its own round". **It has TWO** —
`core/payroll-anomaly.ts:742` (r238) and `core/readiness-nudge.ts:248` (r237). The claim came from ADR-0084
§2.3's *"what has no caller yet, deliberately"*, which was TRUE at r236 and was overtaken by the next two
rounds without the sentence ever being edited. **An ADR is a decision record, not a statement of current
fact, and nothing updates it when a later round overtakes it** — so AGENTS 7 applies to this repository's own
prose exactly as it applies to a ticket. A four-second grep settles it. That ADR line now carries a dated
flag pointing here.

## r248 (2026-09-06) — agreement measurement lands, and the first thing it measured was a lie we were about to print. `main@49ff2885`.

**DEPLOYED.** tsc clean · **full gate GREEN, 764 files across 5 chunks, every chunk exit 0** · `next build`
clean · no migration · arrival proved by a ZERO-line `rsync -azi --dry-run` · service active · `GET /` 401.

**ADR-0084 Phase 3 item 5.** `proposalRates` already existed and was already correct — the missing half was
a surface. `agreementView` (core/control-tower.ts) returns the three rates per proposal type plus the honest
reason when there are none, in the same shape `ratio.blockedBy` already uses on that page. The card renders
`no_provider → no_agent_on → nothing_proposed` in CAUSAL order, because a tenant with no provider also has
no proposals and leading with "nothing proposed yet" sends them looking in the wrong place. A fourth
blocker, `nothing_decided`, separates "the proposers are not running" from "the proposers ARE running and
nobody has ruled on them" — different gaps, different sentences.

⚠️ **DECISION: A SECOND PAGE-LEVEL CALL, NOT A FIELD ON `controlTowerView`.** `proposalRates` opens its own
`withTenant` and `controlTowerView` is one big one; `core/agent-proposal.ts` property 2's corollary forbids
nesting them (two pool connections held for the outer's duration, deadlock if the outer locks a row the
inner needs). Anyone "tidying" this into one view reintroduces exactly that — the header on `agreementView`
says so.

⚠️⚠️ **THE TEST CAUGHT A FABRICATED 0%, AND IT WAS NOT IN THIS ROUND'S CODE.** `reversalRate` is
`reversed ÷ approved` — correct arithmetic, and once one proposal is approved the denominator is real, so
it returns a real `0`. But **`recordReversal` HAS ZERO CALLERS IN THE PRODUCT** (verified across
`core app lib scripts localization`). So `reversed` is structurally zero for every row and the card would
have printed **"0% reversed" — i.e. every approval stuck — when the truth is that nothing in this system can
notice that one did not.** ADR-0084 §2.4 calls reversal the metric that matters MOST, so this was the
flattering-direction lie in the most expensive available place.

**DECISION: fixed at the VIEW, deliberately NOT in `proposalRates`.** That arithmetic is right, other
callers and `test/agent-proposal.test.ts` depend on it, and bending shared arithmetic to suit one screen is
how a number becomes wrong somewhere else. `REVERSAL_HAS_A_WRITER` is a **CONSTANT**, for the same reason
`AutonomyLevel` is a union with one member: turning it on must be a source change that arrives WITH the
writer and gets reviewed beside it, never a flag somebody flips. **Phase 3 item 6 owns flipping it.** The
column still renders — an always-blank column is visible debt; a hidden one is forgotten debt.

**WHAT STILL CANNOT PRODUCE A RATE, so nobody reads the blank card as a defect:** production has no AI
provider, and no agent is switched on. **THAT IS THE WHOLE LIST.**

⚠️ **CORRECTION, MADE THE SAME SESSION (2026-09-06). r248's entry first said `recordDecision` had no
callers and that wiring one "deserves its own round". BOTH ARE WRONG — it has TWO, and they are good:**
  - `core/payroll-anomaly.ts:742` (r238) — `resolveAnomalyVerdict` stamps every hypothesis proposal behind
    the verdict an operator just resolved. `false_positive` → declined; `accepted`/`fixed_upstream` →
    approved. Its own comment calls it "the only real agreement rate the payroll side of this product has",
    and it is right: hypotheses are raised ONLY about employees the detectors auto-cleared, so the
    operator's verdict is attributable to the model rather than to a rule sharing the row.
  - `core/readiness-nudge.ts:248` (r237) — a nudge whose gap later closed is approved; one still open at
    the deadline is declined.

**WHERE THE WRONG CLAIM CAME FROM, because the shape will recur:** ADR-0084 §2.3 says "What has no caller
yet, deliberately: `recordDecision`, `recordReversal` and `proposalRates`." That was TRUE AT r236 and r237
and r238 falsified two-thirds of it without editing the sentence. **An ADR is a decision record, not a
statement of current fact, and it does not get updated when a later round overtakes it** — so AGENTS 7
("reproduce before agreeing the premise") applies to this repository's own prose exactly as it applies to a
ticket. `grep -rn "recordDecision" core app lib scripts localization` is four seconds and would have
settled it. That ADR line now carries a dated correction pointing here.

**The genuinely unwired one is `recordReversal`** — no caller anywhere, which is what `REVERSAL_HAS_A_WRITER`
encodes and what Phase 3 item 6 owns. **The agreement rate needs no further code: a provider and a
switched-on agent are enough.**

**Verified on production before building, not taken from this file:** `ai_provider_config` 0 rows,
`agent_proposal` 0 rows, 0 agents switched on, and 0 AI keys in `.env.production`.

**`t.has()` on the proposal-type label (AGENTS 6).** `ProposalTypeId` is a TypeScript union, not a SQL
CHECK — 0452's header explains why — so a type can reach the screen with no translation, and a bare `t()`
would `MISSING_MESSAGE` the whole Control Tower down. Falls back to the raw id: ugly beats absent.

**CHUNKS=5 VALIDATED.** r247's floor was a guess from a failure; this is the measurement. Five chunks
peaked at **58-79% disk** and produced **zero** environmental failures, against 58 at three chunks the day
before. 153+153+153+153+152 = 764, so every file was counted (AGENTS 4).

## r246 (2026-09-03) — three open items planned; two answered "already works" from production evidence. NO CODE.

**The board went from three open items to zero awaiting a plan.** Two of the three needed no build at
all, and establishing that took production queries rather than reading code — AGENTS 7, twice over.

**`cd63bd91` "To permanently remove Haji Leave" — ALREADY WORKS, and the answer turned on running the
product's OWN predicate rather than a hand-written one.** The first three attempts at counting what
references Haji Leave failed on guessed column names, and a hand-rolled count of two history tables would
have been wrong anyway: `leaveTypeInUseSqlText` (core/leave-type-refs.ts) enumerates SIX
(`leave_request`, `leave_ledger`, `leave_encashment_snapshot`, `leave_entitlement_recalc_audit`,
`leave_generation_run_item`, `replacement_leave_request`). Ran that exact SQL against production:
`in_use = f`. So Leave Configuration is ALREADY showing Delete for it, and `deleteLeaveType` cascades the
two `leave_approval_policy` rows (560f4524, 0fca03b8 — both active, both with zero levels) inside the
same transaction. Shipped in 1ae7f3ab + 4fdb69b2; nobody had to build anything.
**The plan says DELETE and explicitly never "unset the leave type" on those two rules**, because
`leave_approval_policy.leave_type_id` NULL is the COMPANY DEFAULT chain, not a non-match
(core/leave-approval-policy.ts:226 and :270 both select the default by `isNull`). Blanking them would
manufacture two extra company-wide default approval rules — the same wildcard trap
`deleteGradeGroup` documents.

**`d6e2cccc` "Form C.P.8A (EA) Bahasa Malaysia" — ALREADY WORKS; the reporter photographed the PREVIEW
SCREEN.** The attachment is `app/payroll/reports/ea/[employmentId]` (it carries r242's readiness panel
and r244's corrected heading, which is how it was identified), not the download. The mockup is the
argument: both panes are REAL captures side by side — their screenshot on the left, our actual rendered
PDF (`docs/forms/ea-cp8a-our-output-2026-08-23.png`, drawn in r219 off the blank C.P.8A THEY supplied) on
the right. Nothing drawn. **Their instruction "use the blank EA download as the source to copy" is
circular and the plan says so**: `app/payroll/ea/blank/route.ts` is `renderEaPdf(blankEaPdfData(), …,
{blank:true})` — our own renderer with the money column empty, not an LHDN file. Fidelity stays
`agency-layout`, never `official` (the specimen's Producer is DXperience — another payroll system's
rendering) and the plan asserts only what `public/forms/` can back (AGENTS 28b).

**`4da751c6` "Benefit Scheme and Effective From" — PARTLY THERE; the behaviour exists, the name does
not.** Everything the reporter describes a scheme DOING already runs: `entitlement_template` carries the
service bands (their 0-2 / 2-5 / 5+ columns exactly), and `entitlement_eligibility_rule.criteria` carries
`gradeIds`, `employmentTypes` and `confirmationStatuses` — their "Grade 12-15 (Permanent)" maps onto three
existing axes. Grade changes already recalculate (`reprojectEntitlementForEmployment`), and **their
history requirement is already correct AND PINNED**: c8052ae3 bounded the already-granted sum at
`<= windowEnd`, so 2025 keeps its 18 days; `test/leave-recalc-future-year-window.test.ts` fails with the
bound reverted. What is missing is a single field naming the scheme.

**DECISION — the field is DERIVED, never stored, and this is the load-bearing call of the plan.**
`benefit_scheme`, `scheme_leave_entitlement`, `leave_policy` and `employment.benefit_scheme_id` were
deleted deliberately in 6e9a126e release three. Reintroducing an assignment layer would let a stored
scheme name silently disagree with the rules that compute the days. **And the honest consequence was
built into the mockup rather than discovered later:** grade groups are an APPLICATOR over `gradeIds`, not
a criteria axis, so the reverse lookup from an employee to a scheme NAME can be ambiguous. The plan and
the mockup both carry the "does not resolve to a single scheme" empty state, which lists what applies per
leave type instead of inventing a label. A mockup showing only the happy path would have promised a name
we cannot always derive.

**`leaveEntitlementBreakdown` does NOT name the template or the matched rule** (core/read.ts L2913 —
ledger buckets, `essView`, `formulaExplanations` only), so this is a new read, not a widening of that
shape. `/me` renders the same component and this is HR-side detail.

## r243 (2026-09-02) — the AI agent switchboard: ADR-0084 Phase 3's missing precondition. NO MIGRATION.

⚠️⚠️ **PHASE 3 WAS BLOCKED ON SOMETHING THE ADR NEVER WROTE DOWN.** Items 5, 6 and 7 (agreement
measurement, recurrence mining, the first autonomy grant) all need `agent_proposal` to have rows in it.
On production it is EMPTY — not because anything is broken, but because **no tenant had switched any
agent on and no screen could.** r237, r238 and r240 each shipped a setting and each had to record the
same footnote: *nothing in the UI turns this on; here is an INSERT to run on the box.* **Three
consecutive entries carrying the same caveat is the caveat asking to become a screen**, and until it was
one the ADR's own sequencing could not advance. This is not item 5 arriving early — it is what lets item
5 ever have data.

**`core/tenant-settings.ts` IS THE APP'S FIRST WRITER OF `tenant_setting`,** and it re-states every
conjunct of 0313's `tenant_setting_write` policy in TypeScript rather than leaning on it. ⚠️ **That
policy's failure mode is SILENCE**: a write that misses it matches ZERO ROWS, returns no error, and the
caller believes it saved. So group-admin, catalogued, tenant-scoped, customer-visible and value-type are
each checked here first and refused with a typed error. The policy stays the authority; this is so a
refusal is legible.

**`source: 'customer'` ON BOTH ARMS OF THE UPSERT.** 0313's own comment: provenance follows the write, and
overwriting a platform-written value REQUIRES setting it. A customer switch that left `platform` on the
row would be claiming the platform made the change.

⚠️ **THE ACTION TAKES AN AGENT ID, NEVER A SETTINGS KEY.** A form field naming a key would let anybody who
can open the screen write ANY tenant-scoped catalogued setting — including `payroll.reset_enabled` and
`payroll.unlock_enabled`, which reopen a finalised run. The key is looked up from the same closed list the
screen renders.

⚠️ **THE CATALOGUE DRIFT GUARD CAUGHT ME MID-BUILD, EXACTLY AS r237 PREDICTED.** `aiAgentSwitches` first
read each value with `settingEnabled(ctx, a.key)` — a VARIABLE — and
`test/module-catalog-drift.test.ts` fails on that, because a variable key is invisible to the catalogue
scan and an uncatalogued key is a 500 rather than a disabled feature. Each entry now carries its own
literal-keyed `read`, with the duplication documented so nobody tidies it away. **Second time this trap
has fired in the same round family.**

**NO ACCURACY RATE IS RENDERED, AND A TEST FORBIDS ONE.** §2.3's three rates are NULL until proposals
exist, and a screen printing "0%" over an empty ledger would assert an accuracy figure nobody can stand
behind — the same refusal the staffing tile already makes. A guard fails the moment `proposalRates`,
`agreementRate`, `adjudicationPassRate` or `reversalRate` appears on this page without somebody first
deciding how a null reads.

**Verified end to end on a dev server, not inferred:** the write lands (`payroll.anomaly_hypotheses_enabled
| true | customer` in `tenant_setting`), a fresh request reflects it, and the row renders **"On, but cannot
run — no AI provider is set up, so there is no model for it to ask."** A company-scoped admin is refused
`not_group_admin`; `payroll.reset_enabled` is refused `not_tenant_scoped`. Four mutations re-derived by
hand. Gate green 6/6 across 763 files.

**WHAT IS STILL TRUE AND IS NOW THE ONLY THING IN THE WAY:** production has **no AI provider** (empty
`ai_provider_config`, no env key), so the two agents that need a model would report `notConfigured` even
switched on. **Adding one is Administration → AI and is the single remaining step before Phase 3 has data.**

     a DAY, not a tab; resolving it against `sectionDays` would make an already-circulated link open

instead of date · `all` no longer the default), each failing exactly one new case.
